## 2026-10-05 ARV-062 Complete Helm deployment
- Dependency: the PRD lists ARV-002, whose only open criterion is the first release on the dev cluster by a human. None of ARV-062's own criteria needs a cluster, so the story was built and verified by rendering, schema validation and running the database image as the pod runs it. The first cluster release (ARV-002) remains the real end-to-end check of this chart.
- TimescaleDB chart (`Charts/timescaledb`), installed by the Helmfile in every environment:
  - What it deploys: a StatefulSet with one replica and a `data-timescaledb-0` claim (50Gi, kept on delete); the `timescaledb` Service the base settings expect; a headless Service; a NetworkPolicy that admits pods of its own namespace only.
  - Image: `timescale/timescaledb-ha:pg17-ts2.30`, pinned by digest. `base-images.mjs --check` keeps it on the tag of `docker-compose.dev.yml`, which CI and the integration tests also use.
  - Pod privileges: runs as the image's `postgres` user (uid 1000) with a read-only root filesystem, every capability dropped, RuntimeDefault seccomp and no service account token. The only writable paths are emptyDirs for `/tmp`, the socket directory and `/dev/shm`.
  - Authentication: initdb gives peer on the socket and scram-sha-256 on every TCP connection, loopback included. The image's default is trust, which a port-forward would reach.
  - First start: the init script (env only, through psql `\getenv`) creates the migration login (CREATEROLE, not superuser) and gives it the database. Passwords come from the `timescaledb-credentials` secret.
  - Release guards refuse: an image without a digest, `latest`, a missing secret, and the superuser or an Ariva role as migration login.
- Kafka topics job:
  - `api-main --provision-topics` (new `TopicProvisioning` command) runs as a Helm hook next to the migration job.
  - It creates missing topics and dead-letter topics, never alters an existing one, refuses plaintext Kafka in k8s-prd as the hosts do, and exits 1 when the broker is still unreachable after five minutes.
  - With the job on, api-main runs with `Kafka__ProvisionTopics=false`.
  - `kafkaTopics.adminSecretName` gives the job a principal of its own, so the hosts' principal can lose create rights (recommended in production; empty by default).
- Helmfile: `timescaledb` (a state value, true in dev, demo, prd and localk8s) is applied first and waited for; `ariva-platform` needs it.
- Pipelines:
  - `Release-ariva-k8s-dev.yaml` creates `timescaledb-credentials` from two new variable group secrets. It refuses an undefined (macro text) or short password, and removes its files on exit.
  - `ci.yml` installs Helmfile 1.1.7 with a sha256 check, so the chart test renders every Helmfile environment in CI.
- Chart test (30 rules self-tested on fixtures), new rules:
  - third-party images pinned by digest;
  - no literal credential in `env`;
  - a StatefulSet needs a NetworkPolicy and no service account token;
  - a PostgreSQL container needs peer and scram initdb arguments and no `POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD`;
  - no `CREATE ROLE` without `NOSUPERUSER`;
  - the topics job implies `Kafka__ProvisionTopics=false`.
  
  It also renders the database chart and its guards, and every Helmfile environment, and checks that production without a build number is refused.
- Tests:
  - `TopicProvisioningCommandTests` (unit: flag, Kafka off, plaintext in production, unknown protocol, unreachable broker within the deadline).
  - `TopicProvisioningTests` (integration: every topic created once with partitions, retention and min.insync; a second run succeeds; a hand-made topic is never altered).
  - `DatabaseChartBootstrapTests` (integration). It reads the digest, initdb arguments and init script from the chart and runs the image like the pod (uid 1000, read-only root, no capabilities). It checks: no password-free TCP from outside or on loopback; a wrong password is refused; the migration login is a non-superuser owner; the real migration runs as it; the runtime login cannot create a table.
  
  Red checks: changing the chart to trust fails both the chart test and the integration test.
- Also verified by hand:
  - `kubeconform -strict` (Kubernetes 1.30 schemas) on every render;
  - `api-main --migrate` as the non-superuser owner against the read-only container;
  - `api-main --provision-topics` end to end against the E2E broker (peak memory about 75 MB; the job's limit is 256Mi).
- Docs: wiki/04 (status; database options; secrets in 6.2; release order and hook jobs in 6.3; bootstrap in 7.1 and 7.2; the database pod) and `Platform/Cloud/CLAUDE.md`. In docs/security: the CWE-269 row; ASVS V12.3.3, V13.2.2 and V13.3.2.
- Gates:
  - backend PASS (unit 2281);
  - integration 317 passed, 1 pre-existing skip;
  - e2e 491 passed, 1 skipped (log scan clean);
  - chart security PASS with Helm 3.19.0 and Helmfile 1.1.7;
  - base images PASS; docs PASS; security scan 0 errors.
- Security review (independent reviewer, CWE-269 and the matrix):
  - First pass FAIL, three fixes: no automated test held the database authentication (now a chart rule and the bootstrap integration test); the pipeline would have initialised the database with the public macro text if a variable was missing (now refused); the docs claimed the hosts' Kafka principal needed no create rights even without a job principal (now qualified).
  - Second pass PASS.
  - Recorded, non-blocking:
    - The database NetworkPolicy admits every pod in the namespace, and there is no egress policy.
    - The topics job mounts both appsettings secrets but needs only Kafka.
    - The migration job still mounts a service account token (predates this story).

    - wiki/Home.md's dated status table (1 October) still calls the TimescaleDB chart a placeholder.

## 2026-10-05 ARV-063 Dynamic security scanning pipeline
- Summary: OWASP ZAP 2.17, pinned by digest, scans the real hosts (Playwright project `zap` in `Platform/Testing/Ariva.E2E/tests/zap`, `node scripts/verify.mjs zap`, `.github/workflows/security-zap.yml` weekly and on demand).
  - API scans (passive and active) of the Main, Ingest and Integration OpenAPI documents with the token of `e2e.zapadmin`, a system administrator with no second factor, so every critical action answers 401 and none is carried out. The sign-in, session and hub operations are removed from the documents, because ZAP's import calls every operation, and excluded from the active scan and the spider. Each scan must still hold its session at the end.
  - Baseline scans of every API host, and of the web build under the web image's own nginx image and configuration.
  - When `ARIVA_DEV_WEB_URL` is set, a passive baseline of the dev deployment.
  - Gate: the run fails on a High risk alert without an approved entry in `security/zap-triage.json`. An incomplete entry is an error, and a PENDING approver accepts nothing. Reports (HTML, JSON, logs, `summary.md`) are uploaded as artifacts. A grep of the reports found no token, password or Authorization header.
- OpenAPI documents (needed by the API scan):
  - Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi, which was already in the package catalog.
  - Served at `/openapi/v1.json` only with `OpenApi:Enabled`, only to SystemInfo.View, and never in k8s-prd: the host refuses to start (`OpenApiTests`). No UI.
- Findings and triage (final run: no High, Medium or Low left):
  - Fixed: four endpoints answered 500 to `siteCode=%00`, because PostgreSQL refuses NUL in text. The reviewer then found the same class elsewhere (search text, topology names). Two fixes:
    - Every controller now refuses a NUL character with 400 (`NulCharacterFilter` for the query, route values and forms; `NulRejectingStringConverter` for JSON strings). Tests: `NulCharacterTests`, red-checked; e2e `null-bytes.spec.ts`, 11 cases.
    - `SiteScopedAttribute` answers 404 before the lookup for any other value that cannot be a site code.
  - Fixed in the harness: the E2E log scan matched the numeric TOTP canary inside a log timestamp (".4938178" holds 493817), a false positive that can fail any long run, possibly the unexplained CI log-scan failure on 40da919. A digits-only secret now counts only as a whole number. The rule is self-checked on every teardown.
  - Informational, accepted with no action:
    - 4xx client errors from ZAP's placeholder values;
    - the CSP being set in a meta tag as well as the header (SvelteKit hash mode, by design);
    - "Modern Web Application".
  - Also found: the rate limiter answered most of the first scan with 429, so the scan run raises the global limit; the limiter's own tests are unchanged.
- Also fixed:
  - wiki/04 gave a break-glass command that cannot work: `dotnet Ariva.Api.Main.dll` does not exist in the runtime-deps image, and the pod had no settings. It is now `kubectl exec deploy/api-main-deployment -- ./Ariva.Api.Main --create-break-glass`.
  - `base-images.mjs` keeps the scan's ZAP image equal to the workflow's, and its nginx equal to the web image's base.
- Gates:
  - backend PASS (unit 2302);
  - integration 317 passed, 1 pre-existing skip;
  - e2e 502 passed, 1 skipped;
  - zap 5 passed;
  - docs PASS; security scan 0 errors; base images PASS.
- Security review (independent reviewer, all 14 CWEs):
  - First pass FAIL: the triage file could silence a High finding without approval; NUL bytes still reached PostgreSQL through other inputs; the log-scan change had no test. All fixed.
  - Second pass PASS.
  - Open, for the product owner: `.claude/hooks/guard-paths.mjs` protects only `security/allowlist.json` from agent approvals. Extending it to `security/zap-triage.json` changes the hooks, which needs your approval.
  - Follow-ups, non-blocking:
    - scan depth: ZAP fills placeholder values, so most Main requests end in 404 or 400, and Ingest and Integration are scanned without their own credentials. Seeded example values and device or integration credentials would reach further;
    - URL-scoped triage entries;
    - tests for the guard's route and form branches;
    - the web image serves `/nginx/default.conf` (pre-existing, low risk).

## 2026-10-05 ARV-073 Signed images with SBOM and provenance
- Summary: `.github/workflows/images.yml`, for every image pushed to GitHub Container Registry. Images are pushed only from a `v*` tag, or when the workflow is run by hand from `main`; any other ref builds and scans without pushing.
  - The digest is read from the registry and checked.
  - The image is signed with cosign keyless: GitHub OIDC, a Fulcio certificate naming the repository, workflow, ref and commit, and the Rekor log. cosign 3.0.6 via sigstore/cosign-installer v4.1.2, pinned by SHA.
  - Its CycloneDX SBOM (Trivy 0.75.0) is attached as a signed attestation.
  - Both are verified at once against this repository's `images.yml`, on `v*` tags or `main` only, with the GitHub issuer and `--certificate-github-workflow-repository`.
  - A digests job writes the table for the release notes, with the verify command, to the job summary and the `image-digests` artifact.
- Docs:
  - wiki/04 section 6.5:
    - verification and SBOM extraction;
    - what keyless signing publishes;
    - the trust preconditions (tag ruleset, protected `main`);
    - `oras copy -r` to carry signatures and SBOMs into Dalil Container Registry;
    - an optional Kyverno `SigstoreBundle` policy in Audit mode, labelled untested.
  - wiki/18: release notes carry the digests.
  - wiki/05: flow 24, Sigstore egress for verifiers.
  - Platform/Cloud/CLAUDE.md; ASVS V15.1.2; ARV-096 (SBOM per release delivered).
- Verified locally (keyless needs GitHub's OIDC, so not end to end here):
  - With cosign 3.0.6, Trivy 0.75.0 and a local registry, using a key and no transparency log: sign, a CycloneDX attestation, `verify` and `verify-attestation`, and the documented `jq` SBOM extraction.
  - `oras copy -r` to another repository keeps the digest, signature and attestation; `cosign copy` does not.
  - The signer pattern matches `images.yml` on a tag and on `main`, and refuses `ci.yml`, another owner and a feature branch.
  - The digests script ran on sample files.
  - The Kyverno policy passes `kubeconform -strict` against Kyverno's schema.
  - `docker inspect .RepoDigests` was found to return the upstream index digest, hence the registry lookup.
- Not verified: the first real signed run. It happens on the first `v*` tag, and CI is not running on this account (billing, see earlier). After the first copy to ACR, run the documented `cosign verify` there; ACR serves the native referrers API, whereas the local test used the fallback tags.
- Decisions for the product owner (docs/product/decisions.md):
  - **Keyless signing publishes the private repository's name, workflow, refs and commit ids in the public Rekor log** (keep it, or use a Key Vault key);
  - a ruleset protecting `v*` tags, plus protected `main`, is needed before the first signed release.
- Gates: workflow YAML parses; docs PASS; security scan 0 errors. No application code changed.
- Security review (independent reviewer, CWE-494 and the matrix):
  - First pass FAIL: the documented `cosign copy` loses the evidence; the Kyverno example matched the wrong registry and namespaces and read the legacy format; the tag-trust precondition and the public-log disclosure were missing; the ASVS and ARV-096 statements were off. All fixed.
  - Second pass PASS. Its wording notes on key-based signing and the summary command were acted on.
  - Recorded residuals:
    - `id-token: write` is granted to builds that sign nothing (a separate sign job would narrow it);
    - a window between push and the digest lookup (needs `packages:write` on a per-run tag);
    - no SLSA provenance attestation (GitHub artifact attestations for private repositories need Enterprise Cloud);
    - the Azure DevOps builds stay unsigned (Target);
    - CWE-494 is not a row of the 14-CWE matrix.

## 2026-10-05 ARV-064 Scripted demo and runbook
- Summary: the reference evening at DMO (seed 9303) played in real time through the whole pipeline, with nothing planted: the simulator's sensor emulator pushes to Ingest as devices registered and calibrated by the demo, Stream computes the queues and evaluates the seeded rules, Main relays both to the live screens.
  - Three scripted events, each for the role that owns it: 18:05 the visitor wave takes the A-VIS nowcast past 15 minutes and R-001 reaches the border shift supervisor; 18:20 to 18:30 sensor S-17 is offline and R-003 names it; 19:10 check-in island C breaches its 15-minute P90 and R-004 reaches the handler station manager.
  - `tests/demo/reference-day.spec.ts` (Playwright project `demo`, only with `ARIVA_E2E_DEMO=1`, so CI's e2e job is unchanged) walks the three events; `node scripts/verify.mjs demo` runs it. It loads every counting sensor (20) by default and starts on the next whole minute with up to 14 demo minutes of pre-roll, so the 15-minute bins fall on quarter hours.
  - `scripts/demo-local.mjs` (`prepare | start | status | stop | accounts | code`) runs the same demo on a developer machine through Ariva.AppHost: demo accounts and the AppHost settings in `.demo/` (git-ignored, owner-only), loopback only unless `--remote`.

Live only: replays never set it, so the golden replay is unchanged.

- Fixed on the way (found by the rehearsal and the gates):
  - Alert evaluation judged a minute as soon as its row existed. The stream stores a minute's counts while it runs and its queue length and nowcast about half a minute after it ends, so a tick in between took the minute without a nowcast and never judged it again. R-001 missed the visitor wave in two rehearsals (A-VIS above 15 minutes for 7 minutes, rule state "sustained 0"); a 5-second probe showed the tick at :29 and the nowcast written at :32. `AlertInputs.LatestMinutesAsync` now counts only minutes with a queue length (the live part). Regression test `Tick_Should_WaitForTheLivePartOfAMinute_When_OnlyItsCountsAreStoredYet`, red before the fix.
  - The live alerts panel showed an alert's zone or, without one, its device, so R-003 said A-VIS and never S-17. It now shows both (functional test).
  - The guard for `Auth:DevelopmentUsers` and `Auth:TotpRequired` false ran only in Main's token issuing and read the `environment` configuration key. It now runs in `AddArivaAccounts` (every host and the break-glass command) with the host's own environment name; Cronz reads `Auth:TotpRequired` when it picks report recipients.
  - `ImmigrationIntakeTests` counted every AMAN desk session in the class's shared database; the XS2 test's two sessions failed it depending on order.
- Gates: backend PASS on 5896e1b (2,324 unit tests, golden replay unchanged, security scan, base images, chart security, NuGet and npm audits); integration 313 passed and 1 skipped, the 6 Toxiproxy fault tests not runnable here (their ghcr.io image is blocked in the cloud sessions); e2e 504 passed and 1 skipped (CI's command, local TimescaleDB, Kafka and Redis); web PASS (svelte-check, lint, build); visual 14 of 14 after 8 baselines were regenerated on fresh services (live and immigration screens, the intended changes reviewed); the demo rehearsal: event 1 passed in one run and events 2 and 3 in the next, after the two fixes above; the local path (`demo-local.mjs prepare` and `start` through Ariva.AppHost) showed R-001 to demo.border at 18:06 demo time. GitHub Actions does not start on this account, so no CI run.
  - Also fixed for the gates: the `DeskTerms` integration test left DMO desk minutes 40 days ahead in the class's shared database, which stopped the DMO desk feed of `DeskFeed_Should_DriveTheDeskEngine...` whenever xUnit ran it first; it now removes them.
- Security review (independent reviewer):
  - Cowork's review: PASS after one round (Medium: the TOTP bypass and development users were not enforced at runtime; fixed).
  - Delta review of this session's commits: first pass FAIL (Medium, CWE-287/306: the guard ran in Main only), fixed in 22a4b9e; second pass PASS. The alert change passed on the first pass (bound SQL; no input can write a row without a queue length).
  - Residuals: an image started without DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT falls back to `environment.json` (vm-local) and `Application:Environment` defaults to vm-local, so a hand-run container could enable the local-only settings (the chart always sets the environment); if the stream's live write stalls, BinP90 and PredictedNowcast rules stop without a signal that evaluation is behind; `LatestMinutesAsync` has no lower time bound; all hosts share `ariva_runtime`, which may write `queue_minute`.
- Learnings:
  - Visual baselines must be regenerated on fresh services: after the full e2e suite the masked panels on the live screen grow with leftover alerts and desks.
  - `--repeat-each` cannot repeat a test that signs in with TOTP: a code counts once per account.
  - In the cloud sessions `pkg-containers.githubusercontent.com` is blocked, so the Toxiproxy fault tests (ghcr.io image) cannot run there; everything else pulls from Docker Hub.
  - The repository hooks allow edits under the repository path only, so a second git worktree elsewhere cannot be edited with the edit tools.
- Follow-ups (not in this story):
  - MassTransit 8.5 sends usage telemetry (versions, OS, the server's time zone, Kafka topic names) from Main, Ingest, Integration and Stream at startup; nothing disables it. Disable it in code with a test.

## 2026-10-06 ARV-097 No outbound usage telemetry from MassTransit
- Summary: MassTransit 8.5 reported versions, the OS, the server's time zone and the Kafka topic names to `usage-tracking.masstransit.io` about five minutes after a host started (Main, Ingest, Integration, Stream). `AddArivaMessaging`, where every host registers the bus, now calls `DisableUsageTelemetry()`, and `EnsureNoUsageTelemetry` refuses to start a host whose `MASSTRANSIT_USAGE_TELEMETRY` is true or non-zero (MassTransit's tracker reads it after the options are built and would turn reporting back on).
- Tests: `MessagingRegistrationTests` (telemetry off, red without the fix; the variable refused or allowed), `MessagingLayeringTests` (only `MessagingExtensions.cs` registers a MassTransit bus anywhere in `Platform/`, generic form included), and the E2E log scan fails a run whose host logs report usage telemetry (a backstop: the report comes about five minutes after start and only with Kafka).
- Docs: `docs/security/asvs-l2.md` (V14.2.3, V13.2.4, ARV-097 row), `wiki/13-Security-Guide.md`, `docs/product/phase0-exit-review.md` (item closed).
- Gates: backend PASS (2,330 unit tests, 14 CWEs, audits); e2e 504 passed and 1 skipped, the log scan clean over 9 minutes of host logs (the run outlasts the report delay). GitHub Actions does not start on this account, so these were local runs.
- Security review: first pass FAIL (Medium: the environment variable re-enabled reporting; Low: V13.2.4 row, PRD entry), fixed in 8de1aea; second pass PASS. The PRD entry came with #57, so `passes: true` and this entry landed after #57 and #59 merged (PR #60 merged as 963ab41 and 471152c).
- Learnings:
  - A library's options can be overridden after they are built: test the behaviour the library ends up with (here the tracker's environment variable), not only the options.
  - `dotnet test` in this repository runs vstest: arguments after `--` are run settings, so use `--filter "FullyQualifiedName~..."` to run a subset.

## 2026-10-06 ARV-098 Images fail safe without their environment
- Summary: a container or pod started without DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT used to run as vm-local (development accounts, sign-in without TOTP, SchemaUpdate, the demo seed): `ArivaEnvironment.Resolve` fell back to `environment.json`, shipped as vm-local in every image, and then to vm-local, and `appsettings.base.json` defaulted `Application:Environment` to vm-local.
  - Images are published without `environment.json` (`CopyToPublishDirectory` Never in the five API projects and the simulator); developer build output keeps it, so `dotnet run`, the E2E suite and the AppHost still get vm-local.
  - `Resolve` has no default and accepts only vm-local, k8s-dev, k8s-demo and k8s-prd (any case, trimmed, returned canonical); anything else stops the host. The simulator's copy moved to `SimulationEnvironment` with the same rule.
  - `Application:Environment` comes only from `appsettings.base.<environment>.json`, and every host refuses to start when it is missing or differs from the host environment (`ArivaEnvironment.EnsureConfigured`, right after configuration layering, before `--migrate` and `--provision-topics`). A release that replaces that file from the `APPSETTINGS_BASE` secret must keep the key (wiki/04).
  - Chart rule (`Ariva.K8s/tests/checks.mjs`): every container running a .NET Ariva image must resolve the release environment the way the host does (an `--environment`, `/environment` or bare `environment=` argument wins, then the last env entry, then the last envFrom ConfigMap; a Secret source or valueFrom counts as unknown).
- Tests: `SecuritySettingsTests` (no environment, unknown names from arguments and from the file, canonical names, publish exclusion per project, base settings name no environment, `EnsureConfigured`, every host refuses a mismatched `Application:Environment`), `SimulationEnvironmentTests`; chart self-test 36 rules with a bad fixture per bypass. Verified by hand: a published Main has no `environment.json` and stops with "No Ariva environment is set".
- Gates: backend PASS (2,358 unit tests, 14 CWEs, audits); e2e 506 passed and 1 skipped, log scan clean; chart test rendered for real for all four values files through an `alpine/helm` container (get.helm.sh is blocked in the cloud session, Docker Hub is not).
- Security review: first pass FAIL (Medium: the chart rule ignored `--environment` arguments; Medium: envFrom precedence read first-wins, prefixes and Secrets ignored); fixed in 84bb7ef together with the recommended `EnsureConfigured`; second pass PASS, its Low (the bare `environment=` argument) fixed in 9d38cf0.
- Learnings:
  - Kubernetes resolves duplicate variables last-wins, and explicit `env` beats `envFrom`; a manifest check must mirror the runtime's precedence, and its bad fixtures must cover overrides, not only absence.
  - Helm can run from Docker Hub's `alpine/helm` image (`HELM=<wrapper>`) where its download site is blocked, so the chart test need not be skipped in the cloud session.
  - An Aspire AppHost unit test waits forever when Docker is down; after a container restart start dockerd before the backend gate (a suggested task covers making it fail fast).

## 2026-10-06 ARV-080 Data Protection key ring with RSA-OAEP and AES-GCM, and crypto agility
- Summary: the key ring that protects refresh cookies, TOTP seeds and outbound secrets was wrapped by the framework's `EncryptedXml` (RSA PKCS#1 v1.5, AES-256-CBC without a MAC) and read every key in the table.
  - `OaepGcmXmlEncryptor`: each key element is AES-256-GCM under a fresh key wrapped with RSA-OAEP-SHA256, with the algorithm label and certificate thumbprint as associated data, and signed with RSA-PSS-SHA256 by the certificate's private key; the decryptor verifies the signature before decrypting. New keys protect payloads with AES-256-GCM.
  - `TrustedKeyRingRepository` in front of PostgreSQL: a key is admitted only in the exact shape Data Protection writes (one encryptedSecret at key/descriptor/descriptor, no masterKey or value elsewhere, one unqualified creationDate, activationDate, expirationDate and descriptor). Keys in the older format are read only while `DataProtection:LegacyFormatUntil` is in the future, and only as expired copies, so they decrypt but never protect. vm-local sets 2027-01-06; no committed cluster file sets it (test).
  - `DataProtectionCertificates.RequireStrong`: RSA 3072 or larger, current and previous; EC refused (it cannot wrap with OAEP).
  - Cronz `SecretReprotection` (daily 02:40 UTC): re-protects user and integration client TOTP seeds and outbound secrets under the current key when Data Protection reports they need migration, each with a compare-and-swap UPDATE; values under revoked keys are left alone; logs carry row ids only.
  - Split: algorithm labels on refresh token, recovery code, device and display credential hashes went to ARV-080a, so V11.2.2 stays Partly. ASVS: V11.3.1, V11.3.2 and V11.3.3 Met (125 Met, 69 Partly).
- Tests: `KeyRingEncryptionTests` (24: round trip, each part altered, relabelling, missing or altered signature, certificate swap, written keys free of rsa-1_5, CBC, EncryptedData and plaintext, AES-256-GCM descriptor, legacy readable only in the window, planted plaintext key, decoy encrypted secret, legacy key planted in the window, namespaced expiry decoy, production wiring, pinned decryptor type name, weak RSA and EC refused, cluster files keep the window closed), `SecretReprotectionTests` (6 against PostgreSQL: the three tables, unreadable values, a concurrent re-enrolment, a revoked key, no secret in logs), `JobsDashboardTests` (the job's schedule). Each attack test was run against the filter it fixes and failed there.
- Gates: backend PASS (2,382 unit tests, 14 CWEs, audits); integration 321 passed and 1 skipped, the 6 Toxiproxy fault tests not runnable here (ghcr.io blobs blocked), as in the exit review; e2e 506 passed and 1 skipped.
- Security review: four rounds. 1 FAIL (High: a key planted in the table, which the job would then use for every stored secret; Medium: no end to the legacy format, docs overclaiming, missing tests). 2 FAIL (High: a plaintext key with a genuine signed blob copied in as a decoy passed the filter, reproduced against the framework; Medium: a legacy key planted during the window could become the default). 3 FAIL (Medium: a namespaced expirationDate decoy kept a planted legacy key active). 4 PASS at 3dfa071.
- Learnings:
  - Data Protection stores the master key as an encryptedSecret in place of masterKey and reads dates by exact unqualified name; a filter over its XML must check the exact shape and names, not the presence of an element.
  - A test that plants a key must activate it after the genuine key, or the planted key never competes to be the default and the test proves nothing; run every attack test against the old code.
  - Since .NET 9 the key ring refreshes in the background: a test that rolls a key waits until the new default is visible.
  - Upgrading an installation that holds data: set `DataProtection:LegacyFormatUntil` before deploying, let the job run, then remove it (wiki/04); without it old TOTP seeds, outbound secrets and refresh cookies become unreadable. Belongs in the release notes.

## 2026-10-06 ARV-113 Per-line minute counts in the stream (MVP, branch story/mvp-phase1, PR #67)
- Summary: the queue engine counts every crossing per line and minute (entry, exit, overflow entry and a new Count role read from the published profile; interval counts spread as for the queue) in the pure `LineCounts` (Ariva.Core), closed once the watermark passes the minute and saved in the zone snapshot (`ZoneProcessorState` version 3). `StreamStore` writes them to `line_minute` (script 0037, hypertable, DELETE and TRUNCATE revoked, plus the read-only 15-minute aggregate `line_minute_15m`) by binary COPY into staging and an upsert in the checkpoint transaction. Source `Ariva` only (owner decision: `Vendor` deferred until Ariva computes crossings from tracks).
- Bound: at most 20,000 open line minutes per zone; beyond it the earliest is released early and later parts of that minute are written as additive parts (merged per checkpoint, added by a second constant upsert), so no count is lost. Known exception, documented: a commit that succeeds on the server but errors on the client and is retried adds an additive part twice; reachable only after an early release, which the engine cannot produce (only the watermark's minute is open, at most 1,000 lines per profile).
- Golden replay: new hash 8d13749079c0c0ca347dcd8c9e41f6708a7360b7145ad61af32c4d49cf0e0a2c (2,716 outputs; was 451f62ed547d4806ceb5e2e9587705cc67275442a4883f3b435021605ea11729, 2,083), approved by the owner on 2026-10-06: the replay now hashes 633 closed line minutes; every earlier output is unchanged (verified by leaving the line outputs out, which gives the old hash back). A replay of an old range now hashes differently from the value recorded in `replay_run` before this change.
- Tests: `LineCountsTests` (roles, count lines, interval spreading, late events inside and behind the watermark, restart mid-minute, the bound and its additive parts, hostile snapshots, the early-release mark), a golden check that line counts equal the zone's entries and exits per minute, `QueueStreamTests` (restart gives identical `line_minute` rows; store upserts, additive merging and adding, dropped rows logged by zone key; runtime role denied DELETE, TRUNCATE and writes to the aggregate).
- Gates: backend PASS (2,391 unit tests at first pass, then the fixes); integration 333 passed and 1 skipped; scan.mjs 0 errors; docs PASS.
- Security review: first pass FAIL (Medium CWE-120: an early-released minute could be overwritten and lose counts; Low: engine snapshot restore less strict, silent drops, aggregate privileges untested); fixed in c76221c; second pass PASS, its two Lows (document the retry exception, the early-release counter's comment) folded in.
- Learnings: a bound that releases state early must say what happens to the rest of that state; replace-on-upsert is idempotent only for whole values.


## 2026-10-06 ARV-114a Continuous health checks: conservation, track completion and occupancy sanity (MVP, branch story/mvp-phase1; passes)
- Summary: the pure `HealthChecks` (Ariva.Core/Queueing) computes F18's continuous checks per queue zone and bin, and `BinAccumulator` emits a `ZoneHealthBin` with every bin result (same start, revision, status). Inputs come from the queue engine: the queue's sensor occupancy at each minute boundary (queue zone plus the overflow bands heard so far, each fresh within 2 minutes; a band never heard counts as empty), each zone's lowest and highest reading per minute, tracked entries per minute and a `Tracked` flag on resolutions. Ariva.Api.Stream writes `zone_health_bin` (script 0038, hypertable, Final rows immutable, DELETE and TRUNCATE revoked) by binary COPY and upsert in the checkpoint transaction. Zones get an optional physical capacity (queue zones and overflow bands, 1 to 5,000, `zone.physical_capacity` in 0038), set on drafts, frozen with the published version, outside the geometry hash (F22 unchanged); the zone editor has a Physical capacity field; the demo v12 takes the scenario's snake capacities. `GET api/v1/sites/{siteCode}/zone-health?zone=&from=&to=` (new `DataQuality.View`: border shift supervisors, terminal duty managers, administrators) reads the latest revision of each bin, at most 31 days and 3,000 bins.
- Script 0038_zone_health.sql, SHA-256 b1c3a25277443f1000aacaf5a4bea62797b98435f4bd56718062bbe8127e8e31. `ZoneProcessorState` version 4 (bins open at the upgrade report only what follows it).

The in-memory reference replay now reads the evening's records in [From, To) as the archive does: the occupancy reading stamped exactly 20:30:00 changed no output before, but is an occupancy minute of the 20:30 bin now, and the archived replay (integration) left it out. Approved by the owner on 2026-10-06 (recorded in docs/product/decisions.md).
- Owner decisions (2026-10-06): the golden replay head above (3,202 outputs) is approved; the `DataQuality.View` grants as built (SystemAdministrator, BorderShiftSupervisor, TerminalDutyManager; not HandlerStationManager) are approved. Both recorded in docs/product/decisions.md.
- The reference evening is healthy: residual 0 in every bin with both ends measured, every track completes, no minute above capacity (the emulator's occupancy is exactly entries minus exits). Unit tests cover non-zero residuals, censored, fragmented, abandoned and open tracks, minutes above a zone's and a band's capacity, and the golden replay with CI-C at 40.

- Security review: security-reviewer verdict PASS (no Critical/High/Medium; four Low findings fixed in this story: snapshot occupancy upper bounds, non-queue capacity E2E, parameterised test SQL, site-before-query E2E). The fixes: a restored engine refuses an occupancy sample above the queue's bound (`QueueZoneGeometry.MaxQueueOccupancy`, 10,000 per zone that counts in the queue) or of a minute twice, and a zone occupancy above 10,000; a restored bin refuses an opening or closing occupancy above the same bound (hostile rows in `HealthChecksTests`); `zone-profiles.spec.ts` sends a capacity for a service zone on adding and on editing (400 with the domain's message, never 500); the health row test in `QueueStreamTests` binds the bin start as a parameter; `zone-health.spec.ts` sends an invalid range to a site the caller does not reach and gets 404, not 400.

- Learnings: a Playwright mouse drag needs its handle on screen: a taller side panel moved the plan's corner out of view after clicking Save, so the test scrolls the handle into view first. A replay's own range must match the archive's, or an input at the boundary that changed nothing yet will change a later output; a health input must never mark a bin changed, or it adds bin results and changes earlier outputs.

## 2026-10-06 ARV-115 Overflow band occupancy, OverflowDetected and the OverflowOccupied rule (MVP, branch story/mvp-phase1; passes)
- Summary: the pure `OverflowBands` (Ariva.Core/Queueing) takes each overflow band's readings from the engine's steps (`QueueStep.Readings`), holds the lowest and highest per minute until the watermark passes the minute, and releases an `OverflowMinute`; each closed minute moves the band's state, so `OverflowChange` Occupied (first occupied minute after an empty or unheard spell) and Emptied (first minute with readings and no occupancy after an occupied spell) come once each; a minute without readings changes nothing. `ZoneProcessorState` version 5 keeps the open band minutes and band states (a version 4 snapshot restores with every band empty); version 6 adds a band's Unknown state (owner's silent band decision below; a version 5 snapshot restores as written). `StreamStore` writes `overflow_minute` (script 0039, hypertable, DELETE and TRUNCATE revoked; parts of a minute released early merge by LEAST and GREATEST) by binary COPY and upsert, and the `OverflowDetected` event (Ariva.Core/Domain/Events, `[KafkaTopic(FlowOverflowDetected)]`, keyed by the zone key) into `outbox_message` in the same checkpoint transaction, with a name-based id (zone, band, minute, change, profile version) and ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING, so a repeated checkpoint adds no second event. View `overflow_bin_15m` counts overflow minutes per zone and 15-minute bin (TC-19, Proposed). `AlertInputs` supplies `OverflowOccupied` (1 when any watched band held anyone in the minute, 0 when the bands reported empty, nothing without a reading; a queue zone watches all its bands, an overflow zone its own) and `LatestOverflowMinutesAsync` for the live tick; `OverflowOccupied` left `AlertRuleErrors.NotEvaluatedMetrics` and the web's `notEvaluated`, so R-002 is evaluated.
- Script 0039_overflow_minute.sql, SHA-256 4cb65ba8c39acf6bda350b962dc0e07e577acc87f972cb65bbe64ba5bfc64829 (was f2664569d05baff7d04b7508d358c7b1df0e38ed92472d29b23a4b7d92b755e2 before its comment recorded TC-19 as decided; the script is not merged yet, so it changed with checksums.lock).
- Scenario: seed 9303's reference evening never fills a band (A-VIS peaks at 148 of 190), so the simulator gained the case `ScenarioConfig.OverflowEvening` (Visitors snake 60 people, scripted events unchanged) and the sensor emulator splits a queue at the run's snake capacity (`ScenarioDay.SnakeCapacity`, the defaults unless set). In the case A-OV is occupied 18:03 to 18:31 and 19:33 to 19:52 (49 overflow minutes; S-25 is the band's lead).

## 2026-10-06 ARV-114c Zone keys that fit the outbox: ZoneHealthChanged and every event keyed by zone (MVP, branch story/mvp-phase1; passes)
- Summary: the default path (validation, not a wider column). The 200-character key limit moved to Core as `MessageKeys` (Ariva.Core/Messaging: `MaxLength`, `Fits` counting code points as PostgreSQL does); `OutboxLimits` in Infra now follows it (`MaxMessageKeyLength = MessageKeys.MaxLength`, `FitsMessageKey` delegates), so Core never references Infra. `ZoneKeys` gained `Fits(site, queueZoneName)` and `MaxQueueZoneNameLength(site)`. `ZoneProfile.AddZone` and `RenameZone` refuse a queue zone name whose key would pass 200 characters (`ZoneProfile.QueueZoneNameTooLong(site)`: names the site and the allowed length, never the refused name; 400 through the existing domain error path), and `Validate` (so publishing too) lists such a zone in a draft copied from an earlier version. Only queue zone names are bound: every zone-keyed event (the sensing batches, `DeviceHealthReported`, `ZoneHealthChanged`, `OverflowDetected`) uses `<site>/<queue zone name>`, devices bind only to queue zones, and service, staff and overflow zones share their queue zone's key (the band name rides in `OverflowDetected`'s payload). Site codes never change, so nothing else can push a key over. `SvcDeviceHealth.AssessZoneAsync` skips a zone whose key does not fit (one warning per zone per process through `DeviceHealthMetrics.ZoneNotKeyable`, counter `ariva.zones.not_keyable`), so the sweep and the health consumer commit the other zones and the device states instead of failing every pass.
- Validation messages are English domain messages like the other zone profile rules: `Ariva.Resources/Languages` holds no validation resources yet, so there was no Arabic resource to add.
- Seeds: `DemoTopologySeedTests.BuildProfile_Should_GiveEveryQueueZoneAKeyThatFitsAMessageKey_When_Built` (DMO's longest queue zone name is 5 characters; the seed builds through `AddZone`, so it would fail loudly anyway). No other seed adds zones. Migration note for deployed profiles: wiki 10 section 4.2a (SQL to find the zones and devices, then draft, rename, publish, move and recalibrate the devices).
- Tests: unit `ZoneProfileTests` (key of exactly 200 accepted; 201 refused without repeating the name; 7 astral characters and 186 letters, 200 UTF-16 units and 193 characters, accepted, 6 and 188 refused; rename refused and the old name kept; overflow, service and staff names of 200 accepted; a copied overlong queue zone is a validation problem and blocks publishing), `TopicTests` (`OutboxLimits` follows `MessageKeys`; `ZoneKeys.Fits` at DMO, AUH-T1 and a 17-character site, ASCII and astral, null parts), `ZoneHealthTests` (`ZoneNotKeyable` counts every skip, true once per zone), `DemoTopologySeedTests` (above). Integration `DeviceHealthTests`: `ZoneHealthChanged_Should_ReachTheOutbox_When_TheZoneKeyIsTheLongestAllowed` (HBF and a 196-character name through the service: Healthy then Degraded in the outbox with a 200-character `message_key`), `Sweep_Should_CommitTheOtherZonesAndTheDeviceChanges_When_OneZoneKeyIsTooLongForTheOutbox` (a device row moved to a 200-character zone name by SQL, a 204-character key: the sweep commits Snake A's events and both devices' Offline marks, writes nothing for the overlong zone, and a later report and sweep still commit; with the skip removed the test fails with the outbox's "partition key longer than 200 characters"). E2E `zone-profiles.spec.ts`: at E2E2, 195 letters and 5 astral plus 190 letters are accepted; 196 and 200 letters, 4 astral plus 192, and markup and SQL payloads padded to 196 answer 400 without any fragment of the name; a rename to 196 answers 400 and leaves Snake A.
- Docs: docs/product/decisions.md (decision proposed by the engineer, pending the owner, and an Open decisions row), wiki 10 section 4.2a, wiki 11 section 7 (name rule), docs/architecture/overview.md (zone key limit).
- Gates: backend PASS (2,554 unit tests); integration 352 passed and 1 skipped (full); e2e 511 passed and 1 skipped (full run, fresh services); scan.mjs 0 errors (the 6 pending allowlist warnings as before); docs PASS; quick PASS.
- Security review (CWE-120, CWE-501): security-reviewer verdict PASS (2026-10-06), no blocking finding. Folded in: a unit test pinning that a lone surrogate counts as one character (Low), and a runbook 4.2a line to alert on `ariva.zones.not_keyable` since skipped zones are not in `ariva.zones.degraded_now` (Info). Left as is (Info): `Validate`'s problem text names the zone, which is stored data shown only to administrators, JSON encoded, like the other problem texts.
- Learnings: the device health sweep is deployment-wide, so integration tests on the shared database assert at least the devices they own were marked; the name rule counts UTF-16 units (200) while the key rule counts code points, so an astral name can be refused by either, and a test of code point counting needs a name of exactly 200 units.

- Summary: a staff or service zone of the published profile that names its desk (not an e-gate) now feeds that desk's state at its F10 rank. `ZoneGeometrySource` links each such zone hanging off a queue zone to the desk's key (site/checkpoint/desk, `DeskKeys`; one zone per desk and role, the first by name; keys over 64 characters left out) in `QueueZoneGeometry.DeskZones`. Replaying A-VIS with S-18 to S-20 added gives the golden replay's A-VIS outputs exactly, plus 6,296 desk readings (desk case head 807253ec2cbf4d4be460e58bba939cd048d223c5b7240bb18aa5a91910792a64 over 7,776 outputs, not locked), and twice gives the same hashes.

## 2026-10-07 ARV-117 Sensor-only shadow nowcast for the ground-truth proof (MVP, branch story/mvp-phase1; passes)
- Summary: every live queue minute now carries a shadow nowcast without AMAN inputs, written in the same `queue_minute` row and checkpoint as the published one (script 0041_shadow_nowcast.sql, SHA-256 00f21ae0fa1c6822cd5355041c528131110ab16e5d6f8b6feeee08101258777f after the second review fix (efbe46fe46c76986faee4621d66da4d56cd1dab08da9dc254df139d064c6c388 after the first, 145bd806fdaabffffb4255b83901f594dff945ac5ba70acb76eb8ffbcdc68ba6 before; not merged, so still editable): `shadow_nowcast_minutes`, `shadow_no_service`, `shadow_nowcast_degraded`; checks: minutes at least 0, reason one of the `NoServiceReason` names, never a number and a reason together, and the F11 flag exactly when there is a number or a reason). `ShadowNowcasts.Inputs` (Ariva.Core/Queueing/ShadowNowcast.cs) builds both inputs from one queue-side input (Q, exits, window, the queue's flags) and a desk term: the published one takes the term as before (its row is unchanged), the shadow its `DeskTerm.SensorOnly` part. `DeskTerms.SensorOnly`: n_open counts desks open for at least half of the term's minute by their zones alone (`desk_minute.sensor_derived_seconds`, now read by `DeskTermSource` into `DeskMinuteSample.SensorDerivedSeconds`); a desk open through AMAN only is Unknown to the shadow (flags it; with none open from the zones there is no term); no cycle time. `QueueLiveMinute.Shadow` is `[JsonIgnore]`, so neither the live snapshot nor the replay ledger carries it. Computed always: no setting turns it off.
- Decisions (docs/product/decisions.md; points (1) and (2) decided by the owner, Ahmad Al-Sadder, on 2026-10-07: keep the F8 exit-term fallback for the cycle time, flagged Degraded, and revisit with pilot data; AMAN-only desks Unknown to the shadow accepted for ARV-117 so it runs from the first day of burn-in, with the follow-up ARV-117a, a sensor-only desk engine per site, added to backlog/prd-phase1.json at priority 7 (later priorities shifted by one), depending on ARV-117, and made a dependency of ARV-137 so the go-live gate cannot pass without it; it must land before burn-in at a site where every desk has an AMAN code). As proposed: (1) the sensor desk term has no cycle time without AMAN (AMAN's statistics and the desk minutes' transactions are both AMAN), so the shadow takes the F8 fallback: the exit term alone, flagged, or NothingOpen when the zones show every desk closed; alternative offered: c = sensor open desk minutes / queue exits over the window. (2) A desk open through AMAN only is Unknown to the shadow. Limitation: with AMAN live the desk engine records no sensor-derived time for AMAN desks, so at an all-AMAN site (AUH) the shadow is the exit term alone while AMAN is live; a sensor-only desk engine per site would be a follow-up story. (3) No column-level SELECT revoke; the absent read path is enforced by tests.
- Golden replay: unchanged, 3cce63edfb17660f53a3fb7eead6c8ae92b20c491135b406a7df8cb032199a6f over 3,202 outputs (a replay has no desk term, so every replayed minute's shadow equals its published nowcast, tested; the ledger never serialises it). Overflow case unchanged too.

Source side: `ShadowNowcastExposureTests` collects, per statement, the aliases declared for `queue_minute` (schema prefix and double quotes allowed; keywords after the table are not aliases, and a missing keyword only adds findings) and flags any use of an alias, or of the bare table name outside a table-reference position (after FROM, JOIN, INTO, UPDATE, TABLE, ONLY, COPY, ON, EXISTS, LATERAL), that is not `.column` and not the declaration (`SELECT q`, `f(q)`, `f(q ORDER BY ...)`, `(q).*`, `q::text`, `json_build_object('r', q)`, `array_agg(q)`, `q IS NOT NULL`; parameters `:q` and `@q` and string literals are not uses; a comma-separated table list naming `queue_minute` is flagged, write a JOIN); it also flags the `TABLE queue_minute` command (not ALTER, CREATE, LOCK TABLE or ON TABLE) and `COPY` with a schema prefix or quotes. The theory grows to 47 statements, each in SQL and C# form (23 new flagged cases, 6 new negatives beside the 6 existing ones); current production sources pass. Accepted residual risk (also in the V8.1.2 evidence): the scan is per statement, so SQL assembled across separate C# statements, or at run time, is not seen; the exact-dependents allowlist (database objects) and ARV-104f's dedicated read role are the backstops. (Low) `Nowcast.Compute` returns a number or a reason on every path, never neither (new unit test `Compute_Should_GiveExactlyANumberOrAReason_When_InputsAreAnything`, 5,000 random inputs with negative, NaN, infinite and missing values), so `ck_queue_minute_shadow_flag` is now `(shadow_nowcast_minutes IS NULL AND shadow_no_service IS NULL) = (shadow_nowcast_degraded IS NULL)` and the 23514 loop gains the forged flag without a shadow; `ShadowNowcast` is a public record, so StreamStore writes the flag only beside a number or a reason (a hand-built shadow with neither becomes no shadow instead of failing the checkpoint; covered in the store test). New 0041 SHA-256 in checksums.lock. (Low) The column regex is now case-insensitive `shadow_?(nowcast|no_?service)` (StreamStore.cs, the script, and the engine's ShadowNowcast.cs and ZoneProcessor.cs match it), and the more robust guard was added too: `Members_Should_BeNamedAfterTheShadowOnlyOnTheWritePath_When_EveryArivaTypeIsReflected` fails on any member (including compiler-generated ones) named after the shadow on any Ariva type outside the engine and the stream's checkpoint, worker and store, so a convention-mapped `ShadowNowcastMinutes` on an entity is caught however its name was written. docs/product/decisions.md and the V8.1.2 evidence describe the widened checks.
- Gates after the second fixes: backend PASS (2,676 unit tests); integration PASS (362 passed and 1 skipped); scan.mjs 0 errors (6 pending allowlist warnings as before); docs PASS; quick PASS.
- Third security review (2026-10-07): verdict PASS, no blocking finding. Confirmed the runtime role cannot create views, functions, triggers or publications (0001_roles.sql; SqlScriptRunnerTests), so only versioned migrations can add a read path; plpgsql bodies in migrations are seen by the source scan. Accepted residual risk: SQL assembled across separate C# statements (backstops: the exact dependents allowlist and ARV-104f's own read role) and session-local temp views. Optional hardening carried forward: assert no user trigger on queue_minute and no publication of it. A domain question from the review (a desk term without a sensor-only part falling back to the exit term without the shadow's flag) does not arise: `Nowcast.Compute` flags every exit-only result Degraded (F8 sensor-outage fallback), as the owner's decision of 2026-10-07 requires. Structural alternative offered to the owner: move the shadow to its own table the runtime login cannot read (same transaction), so the database enforces the rule instead of tests; pending the owner's choice, for ARV-117a.
- Deferred: the validation comparison that reads the shadow (ARV-104f, with its own authorized read path); a sensor-only desk engine for AMAN desks (ARV-117a); a sensor cycle time (revisit with pilot data).

## 2026-10-07 ARV-118 Availability ledger per operating minute (MVP, branch story/mvp-phase1; passes)
- Summary: a site operating calendar and a write-once availability ledger for the pilot criterion "availability 99 percent of operating hours" (D6, formulas F18, Proposed). Core (`Ariva.Core/Availability`, pure): `OperatingInterval` and `WeeklyHours` ("HH:MM" intervals per weekday in site local time, at most 4 a day, overnight intervals, no overlap on the week's circle, canonical JSON read back strictly), `OperatingCalendar` (per UTC minute: Operating, Closed or Maintenance with its local date; weekly versions, dated exceptions and maintenance windows each count only when recorded before they take effect), `AvailabilityRule` (thresholds in `Availability:*`: grace 120 s, live window 180 s, staleness 150 s, lag 180 s; live decision from Redis snapshots and queue_minute rows; catch-up from the database alone) and `AvailabilitySummary` (ratio, days, Monday-to-Sunday weeks, range). Entities `OperatingWeek`, `OperatingDayException`, `MaintenanceWindow` (NHibernate, soft deleted, `ISiteBound`). Ariva.Api.Main: `api/v1/admin/sites/{siteCode}/calendar` (GET with ViewSite; PUT weeks, POST exceptions and maintenance-windows, DELETE each with EditSite; `[SiteScoped]`; audited `SiteCalendar.*`; 404 for another site or another site's entry, 409 once an entry has taken effect or for a second exception of a day) and `GET api/v1/sites/{siteCode}/availability?from=&to=` (DataQuality.View, local dates, at most 92 days; 404 for a foreign site before the range is checked; 400 without echo). Ariva.Api.Cronz: TickerQ `AvailabilityLedger` every minute at second 30 (`AvailabilityLedger` in Ariva.Infra/Availability): per site with a published or retired profile, one transaction under `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(50, hashtext(site))`, live minutes first, then the backlog from `availability_cursor` (at most 1,440 minutes a run), binary COPY into a staging table and INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; Redis and the database only (a unit test checks the ledger takes no HTTP client); after a Redis failure the rest of the run does not wait for Redis again.
- Script 0042_availability.sql, SHA-256 68daa57e718b00714984dd13adff98b989c0eb3b771ae47df7db94c45ab2090e: `operating_week`, `operating_day_exception`, `maintenance_window` (runtime role: no DELETE, TRUNCATE), `availability_minute` (hypertable, 30-day chunks, PK site and minute, checks on states, reasons and zone counts; runtime role: no UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE) and `availability_cursor`.
- Decisions taken (Proposed, recorded in docs/product/decisions.md with an Open decisions row, TC-83 in docs/product/pilot-to-confirm.md): (1) available minute as in the story's proposal, made concrete: every queue zone of the profile in force at the minute has a Redis snapshot published within 150 s whose minute has reached the minute and trails real time by at most 180 s, and a queue_minute row; (2) a maintenance window recorded at or after its start does not count at all (the API refuses it, the calendar ignores such a row), not "from its recorded time", so an outage cannot be excused once it has begun; weeks and exceptions likewise count only when recorded before their local day starts, and nothing changes after it takes effect, so a minute's calendar state is fixed before the minute; (3) catch-up after Cronz downtime: a missing queue_minute row is Unavailable (MissingMinute, NotObservedLive), every other minute Unobserved (NotObservedLive) and counted as not available, never Available from current Redis state; (4) a site with no weekly version in force is open around the clock; time zone from the site's airport (UTC without one); local dates stored with each minute; (5) calendar read with ViewSite (every role of the site), changed with EditSite (administrators).
- Screen: none. The story's wording asks for the calendar API, the job and the GET availability API; no screen is named, so this story is API only and adds no Playwright functional test (the gate's "functional tests for this story" is empty). A calendar and availability screen is deferred.

Integration `AvailabilityTests` (calendar service with audit, replace, refusals and 409s once in effect; site and entry scoping; ledger live Available, idempotent rerun, stale, lagging and missing reasons, Redis failure and the run-level skip, catch-up with Unobserved and Unavailable minutes and the cursor over several passes, a second replica holding the lock, calendar hours, closed exception, counted and late maintenance over three Dubai days, London fall-back day of 1,500 minutes through the read service, RunAsync, runtime privileges and hypertable, refused rows). E2E `availability.spec.ts` (calendar as a one-site administrator, markup and SQL stored as text, 409, 16 refused bodies without echo, 401, 403, 404 cross-site and cross-entry, audit; availability values per day and week from planted rows, roles, 404 cross-site before the range, 10 refused ranges without echo, 92 days accepted; the real Cronz job records an E2E site's planted live minute as Available, then Unavailable with StaleZone once its snapshots stop), eight rows in security/permission-matrix.json. ## 2026-10-07 ARV-117a Sensor-only desk engine per site for the shadow nowcast (MVP, branch story/mvp-phase1; passes)
- Summary, part A (owner decision 2026-10-07): the shadow nowcast moved out of `queue_minute` into `queue_minute_shadow` (script 0043), keyed like `queue_minute` and written in the same checkpoint transaction as the published row (`StreamStore.WriteLiveAsync`: the live staging table, now with a primary key, feeds both upserts). The runtime role has INSERT, UPDATE of the value columns and SELECT of the two key columns only, no DELETE or TRUNCATE. Verified on PostgreSQL 17 with TimescaleDB 2.30 (a scratch container, then the integration tests): ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE needs SELECT on the conflict target's columns, and an `EXCLUDED.<column>` reference needs SELECT on that column of the target table (the story's expectation that EXCLUDED avoids it does not hold), so the shadow upsert sets its values from the staging table by key (`SET (...) = (SELECT ... FROM stage_queue_live s WHERE s.zone_key = queue_minute_shadow.zone_key AND ...)`). New chunks copy the hypertable's table-level privileges (not its column grants, which is less privilege); the check is made on the hypertable. 0043 copies 0041's rows (`shadow_nowcast_degraded IS NOT NULL`), drops 0041's two constraints and three columns (0041 untouched), and creates `ariva_validation_reader` (NOLOGIN, SELECT on `queue_minute_shadow` only), following 0001's role pattern; ARV-104f grants it to its own login.
- Summary, part B: `SensorOnlyDeskEngine` (Ariva.Core/Desks, pure) wraps a `DeskStateEngine` whose desks are the site's desks with staff or service zones, with those zones as their only sources; `Offer` applies `DeskZoneReading` only and refuses and counts anything else; at most 2,000 desks per site (left out in key order, counted); `Restore` also refuses any AMAN memory (session, transaction, transaction count, presence time). `DeskFeed` runs it per site beside the published engine, offers it the same zone readings, writes its minutes to `desk_sensor_minute` (script 0044: seconds per state and the F11 flag, checks per column and on the total, desk key with a site, runtime role without DELETE or TRUNCATE) in the same transaction as `desk_minute`, keeps its snapshot in `DeskFeedState.SensorEngine` (absent in older states), and rebuilds it by replaying the stored zone readings of the last 15 minutes (those the zone cursor has passed, a minute at a time, at most `MaxRead`, the latest) when the snapshot is absent, invalid, AMAN-tainted or oversized. Counted warnings name the site and a count only (desks left out, readings refused, minutes beyond 120,000 a read). `DeskTermSource` joins `desk_sensor_minute` to the desk minutes (`DeskMinuteSample.Sensor`, `DeskSensorSample`), and `DeskTerms.SensorOnly` uses it for each desk that has one (open at 30 s, flagged when the minute is flagged or 30 s Unknown), keeping ARV-117's reading for desks without one.
- Scripts: 0043_queue_minute_shadow.sql SHA-256 9cff3b10a2f061853b9c7b6962121227c85061a5ecf66c7e97e1f861d9ca752d (after the review fixes; was aaed6b14...); 0044_desk_sensor_minute.sql SHA-256 bea4098537db481def0ac767b9efe7e1c3163a3e18c945b68126e7357c22de2e (checksums.lock).
- Privilege test results (`QueueStreamTests.RuntimeLogin_Should_WriteButNeverReadTheShadow_When_TheStreamStoreUpserts`, a login made by `ariva_ensure_runtime_login`): the stream store inserts, rewrites the same minutes through ON CONFLICT and writes a minute in a second chunk; 21 statements fail with 42501 (each value column, `SELECT *`, `TABLE`, `row_to_json(s)`, `SELECT s`, a WHERE and an ORDER BY over a value, `SET x = x + 1`, RETURNING on UPDATE and INSERT, an `EXCLUDED` upsert, both COPY forms, a chunk read directly by column and by wildcard, DELETE, TRUNCATE, an UPDATE of a key); `count(*)` and `min(zone_key)` work; `has_column_privilege` and `has_table_privilege` confirm SELECT false, INSERT true, value UPDATE true, key UPDATE false, not a member of the reader role; `ariva_validation_reader` reads all three rows and cannot read `queue_minute`.
- Exposure tests: the ARV-117 per-statement wildcard and whole-row scans of `queue_minute` (the 47-statement theory and the source scan) are retired, since `queue_minute` no longer holds the shadow; the name scan is narrowed to `queue_minute_shadow` (only the store, the engine's two files and the scripts); new scans and type-graph tests keep `desk_sensor_minute`, `SensorOnlyDeskEngine` and `DeskSensorSample` to the desk feed, the store, `DeskTermSource` and `DeskTerms`, and no exposed type has a member named after them. The pg_depend test is now `Migrations_Should_LeaveNoReadPathOverTheShadowOrTheSensorOnlyDeskMinutes_When_Applied`: an exact allowlist (empty) of views, rules, materialized views, continuous aggregates, SQL functions, user triggers and publications over either table or its chunks, with a rolled-back positive control of 9 such objects, each caught (the third review's optional hardening on triggers and publications included).
- Tests: unit `SensorOnlyDeskEngineTests` (profiles, the 2,000-desk cap, a 50,000-reading flood, 50 random hours with every kind of AMAN input interleaved giving identical minutes and every AMAN input refused, an AMAN-logged-out desk Serving from its zones, exact JSON continuation, 10 hostile snapshots refused), `ShadowNowcastTests` (F8 at an all-AMAN site with AMAN live: published 7.5 and 7.89 unchanged, the shadow's term n_open = 6 from the zones; zones showing four, then none: NothingOpen; silent, flagged and NaN sensor minutes; an AMAN-only desk beside sensor desks; 400 random sets where only AMAN changes), `DeskZoneScenarioTests` (below), `ShadowNowcastExposureTests`. Integration: `QueueStreamTests` (store, restart comparison of the shadow table, runtime privileges, dependents, 8 new runtime-role cases), `ImmigrationIntakeTests` (desk term from `desk_sensor_minute`), `DeskZoneFeedTests` (A1 logged out by AMAN is Serving in the sensor-only minutes, S1 as published, the snapshot holds A1 and S1 only, an AMAN-tainted snapshot is refused and rebuilt with the same values, XS4's counter).
- Scenario (S-18 to S-20, AR-08 to AR-22, AMAN reporting every Visitors desk's staffing as live sessions): the published engine records 0 sensor-derived open desk minutes of 2,524 open desk minutes (the gap); the sensor-only engine's minutes equal a zones-only engine's exactly, within one desk of the scenario's open desks in 206 of 209 minutes (98.6 percent), 182 exact (87.1 percent), largest difference 5; the shadow's n_open equals the zones' in every minute and the published n_open is AMAN's.

- Decisions for the owner (docs/product/decisions.md entry and Open decisions row): key columns readable by the runtime role (required by the upsert); what ARV-104f's login gets beside the reader role; the Proposed bounds; the 15-minute rebuild; and, with no sensor cycle time, the shadow's number at an all-AMAN site is still the exit term while a desk is open (ARV-117a changes its desk term and its "nothing open" minutes), so the owner may want to revisit the sensor cycle time now that sensor-only open desk minutes exist.
- Docs: formulas F8, F10, F11; overview (tables and desk feed); data-boundary and wiki 14 rows for both tables; asvs-l2 V8.1.2 (now enforced by privileges) and V13.2.2; wiki 03 and wiki 04 (roles check); decisions.
- Gates: backend PASS (2,794 unit tests; the retired theory accounts for the lower count); integration PASS (386 passed, 1 skipped; full run); scan.mjs 0 errors (the 6 pending allowlist warnings as before); docs PASS; quick PASS. E2E not run: no API or web change.
- Security review (2026-10-07), first verdict: FAIL, one Medium and three Low. Fixed:
  - Medium (0043's data copy never tested with data): `QueueStreamTests.Script0043_Should_CopyEveryShadowOf0041AndDropItsColumns_When_QueueMinuteHoldsShadows` applies the scripts up to 0042 through `SqlScriptRunner.ApplyAsync`, writes `queue_minute` rows with a shadow number, with a shadow reason (in another chunk) and with no shadow, applies 0043, and finds exactly the two shadows with the same values, flags and `updated_on` (to the microsecond), no row for the minute without one, every `queue_minute` row kept and no `shadow_*` column or check left; the later scripts then apply on top.
  - Low-Medium (CWE-269, the read role): `QueueStreamTests.ValidationReader_Should_HoldNothingButSelectOnTheShadow_When_TheMigrationsHaveRun` checks `pg_roles` (no login, superuser, createrole, createdb, bypassrls or replication), `pg_auth_members` (no membership), `information_schema.role_table_grants` and the ACLs of relations, columns, schemas, the database, functions and default privileges (SELECT on the shadow and its chunks, USAGE on public, nothing else). 0043 now corrects an existing role's wider attributes. Not the single `ALTER ROLE ariva_validation_reader NOLOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOBYPASSRLS` asked for: verified on PostgreSQL 17 that a migration login without SUPERUSER (a managed server's admin) may not name SUPERUSER or BYPASSRLS at all, even to turn them off ("Only roles with the SUPERUSER attribute may change the SUPERUSER attribute"), so that statement would fail every such deployment. Instead a DO block issues one ALTER ROLE per attribute that is actually set (a no-op normally; a superuser attribute then needs a superuser, so the script fails closed), and raises when the reader is a member of another role. The correction was verified by hand on a scratch container (a role made LOGIN CREATEDB is corrected, also by a CREATEROLE migration login); it is not an integration test because the role is cluster-wide and shared by the parallel test classes.
  - Low (CWE-120, minutes per read): the cap was checked before each step and a whole step added after it. `DeskStateEngine.Advance(referenceUtc, maxRecords)` (and `SensorOnlyDeskEngine`'s) now ends the step at the caller's budget, and the desk feed passes what the cap leaves, in the catch-up and in the rebuild replay, so the bound is exact. The cap is `Border:DeskFeed:MaxSensorMinutesPerRead` (Proposed 120,000, also the maximum; 100 to 120,000). Tests: `SensorOnlyDeskEngineTests.Advance_Should_CloseNoMoreMinutesThanTheBudget_When_ItCatchesUpAfterAPause` (720 minutes in steps of at most 100, together equal to one unbudgeted catch-up) and `ImmigrationIntakeTests.DeskFeed_Should_WriteExactlyTheSensorMinutesTheCapLeaves_When_ItCatchesUpAndLogTheSiteAndACountOnly` (site XS5, cap 100: an hour of catch-up writes exactly 100 minutes, warns once with the site and the count, the rest follow on the next read with no minute missing). Hardening: `SensorOnlyDeskEngine.Restore` refuses a desk whose current state is open (Serving or Idle) without being sensor-derived, or whose open time in the minute exceeds its sensor-derived time (three new hostile snapshots; a closed or unknown sensor-only desk is legitimately not sensor-derived, so `SensorDerived == false` alone would refuse valid snapshots). The same integration test forges such a snapshot (refused, rebuilt) and proves every sensor-only warning (readings refused, minutes over the cap, the refused snapshot) carries the site and a count only, with no exception and no desk key.
  - Low (CWE-862, CWE-863, documentation): the one-bit residual (an UPDATE probe tripping `ck_queue_minute_shadow_one`, 23514, rolled back, tells whether a number or a reason is held) is named in the 0043 header and asvs-l2 V8.1.2 and recorded as accepted residual risk in docs/product/decisions.md; `QueueStreamTests.RuntimeLogin_Should_LearnOnlyWhetherANumberIsHeld_When_ItProbesTheShadowCheck` pins it (with Include Error Detail: the row detail lists only the key columns and the column the probe set, never the number, the reason or the flag). Watch item in the 0043 header: never enable chunk skipping on a value column. 0043's checksum regenerated.
  - Gates after the fixes (2026-10-07): backend PASS (2,798 unit tests; golden replay unchanged, 3cce63edfb17660f53a3fb7eead6c8ae92b20c491135b406a7df8cb032199a6f over 3,202 outputs); integration PASS, 390 passed and 1 skipped (full run); scan.mjs 0 errors (the 6 pending allowlist warnings as before); docs PASS; quick PASS.
  - Security re-review (2026-10-07): all four findings of the first review fixed and tested; one Low required fix, a test of the `Border:DeskFeed:MaxSensorMinutesPerRead` bounds (99 and 120,001 refused, 100 and 120,000 accepted), added as `DeskFeedZoneTests.Settings_Should_BoundTheSensorMinutesPerRead_When_Configured`; with it the verdict is PASS. The reviewer agreed with both deviations (conditional ALTER ROLE, because a non-superuser migration login may not name SUPERUSER on PostgreSQL 16 and later; the restore rule refusing an open desk not backed by its sensors rather than any non-sensor-derived state). Accepted: the reader role's correction path has no integration test (cluster-wide role, parallel tests). Planning note: ARV-104f reads `queue_minute_shadow` but depends only on ARV-117. Backend gate after the added test: PASS.
- Deferred: ARV-104f (the comparison and its login); the sensor cycle time for the shadow, now ARV-117b (owner decision 2026-10-07: added to backlog/prd-phase1.json at priority 8 right after ARV-117a, later priorities shifted by one, depending on ARV-117a, and a dependency of ARV-137); the retention of `desk_sensor_minute` with `desk_minute`'s (To confirm).
- Learnings: in PostgreSQL an `EXCLUDED.<column>` reference in ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE needs SELECT on that column of the target table; take the values from the staging table by key instead. The 0041 rows are copied by the script itself, so a deployment that had 0041 keeps its shadows.

## 2026-10-07 ARV-117b Sensor-derived cycle time for the shadow nowcast only (MVP, branch story/mvp-phase1; passes)

Built: Serving desk minutes over exits, the capacity per busy desk; it adds the desks open now and the busy share, and under saturation is still the exit rate per busy desk (no independent service speed: the sensors see no service starts). Known bias: service-zone time leaves out the walk-up gap (optimistic where the gap is long); the simulator does not model it.

## 2026-10-07 ARV-117c Realistic AMAN interval statistics in the simulator (MVP, branch story/mvp-phase1; passes)
- Summary: the AMAN emulator's desk interval statistics now come from the scenario's served people. `AmanDeskProcess` (simulator, new) takes each minute's served share of every border desk (the lane's served people shared between its active desks by their speed, as before) and works it through as discrete transactions: a family of 1, 2 or 3 people (80, 15 and 5 percent, mean 1.25), each needing its people times the desk's service time per person times a variation of mean 1 (0.5 plus an exponential of mean 0.5, at most 4; hashed from the seed, the desk code and the transaction's index). A transaction is counted whole in the interval in which it completes, with its service time (working seconds) and its cycle time (previous transaction's start at the desk to its start, in open time: paused minutes left out, idle minutes in); the first transaction of a session, or after a gap over 3,600 s, has its own service time as its cycle; a pause keeps the transaction in progress, a close drops it. The interval reports transactions, documents, mean and nearest-rank P90 service time and mean cycle time, all zero when none. Computed once per day for the eight immigration queues and cached per `ScenarioDay` (`ConditionalWeakTable`, `Lazy`); `AmanFeed.Desks` reads it. E-gates, sessions, lane demand, source event ids and the HTTP surface are unchanged; seed 9303's scripted events are untouched (the scenario itself is not changed).
- Minute boundaries (the caller's question): not spread. `TransactionsProcessed` counts completions and Ariva's `LaneCycle` (F10) weights each interval's mean cycle by it, so counting each completed transaction once, whole, in its completion interval makes the lane cycle time the mean cycle per transaction; spreading a transaction over the minutes it spans would break both the count and the weighting. `AmanDeskFeed` takes only the transaction count (`DeskTransactionsCompleted` at the interval's end) and is unaffected. Documented in the simulator README and formulas F10 (to confirm with AMAN).
- Comparison (reference evening, seed 9303, 17:20 to 20:25, Ariva's own simulator, not field data; `SensorCycleScenarioTests`): AMAN's lane cycle time as the published term reads it, median 2.11 min (1.02 to 23.13; was 1.00 all evening). Published (AMAN n_open and lane cycle time) mean absolute error 1.85 min, bias +1.85 (111 minutes, 1 without a number; was 1.17, -1.07). Shadow with the sensor cycle time 0.74, +0.53; shadow without it 0.81, +0.61; open desk minutes over exits 1.01, +0.94 (all unchanged: the shadow reads no AMAN input). For the owner only (Ariva unchanged): lane cycle time per person (cycle seconds over documents) median 1.70 min, published 1.22, +1.11; per person in working time (idle left out, not published by AMAN) 1.49 min, published 0.63, +0.28.
- Per lane (`AmanIntervalScenarioTests`, reference day): while a lane runs at capacity for the whole 12-minute window, AMAN's lane cycle time per transaction over 1.25 people's service time has median A-VIS 1.00, A-CIT 0.99, D-VIS 0.95, D-RES 1.00 (per person 0.99, 1.03, 0.98, 1.04; asserted within 10 percent for every lane with at least 10 such minutes); over all minutes with a cycle 1.20 (A-VIS) to 10.0 (D-CRW), because a start-to-start cycle while open carries the idle time after a lull; in working time per person 0.89 to 1.00. Over the day, documents are within 4 percent of the scenario's served people in every lane with at least 200 (A-VIS 3,988 against 3,985), 1.25 people a transaction where at least 1,000 transactions; every desk record of the day passes `ImmigrationRules` (contract V1 bounds); deterministic across runs.
- Findings for the owner (docs/product/decisions.md entry and Open decisions row): the published nowcast is now pessimistic for two reasons in Ariva's reading of contract V1, which would hold against a field AMAN: (a) `LaneCycle` is per transaction while F8's c is per person (20 percent low throughput at 1.25 people a transaction); (b) idle time in a start-to-start cycle after each lull. Decisions: (i) a per-person lane cycle time in F10 (a published nowcast change, its own story); (ii) idle time in `MeanCycleSeconds` (contract wording with AMAN, or a bound in Ariva); (iii) the criterion "median within 10 percent" is met at capacity, not over all minutes.

## 2026-10-07 ARV-117d Published nowcast: AMAN cycle time per person in working time (MVP, branch story/mvp-phase1; passes)
- Summary: F10's lane cycle time is now per person and leaves idle time out. `LaneCycle.PerPerson` (Ariva.Core/Desks/LaneCycle.cs, pure; moved out of DeskStateEngine.cs) takes each AMAN interval as `DeskIntervalSample` (transactions, documents, mean and P90 service, mean cycle; no key), checks it against contract V1's bounds (`WithinContract`, the `ImmigrationRules` bounds, CWE-501), and gives c = sum(MeanService x Transactions) / sum(Documents) / 60 with a `LaneCycleResult` (minutes, intervals, refused, documents, `LaneCycleFallback` NoIntervals or NoDocuments). `DeskTerms.Compute` has an overload taking the result: when any interval was read, c is its value or none (no fallback to the desk minutes' open time per transaction), and refused intervals flag the published term; with no interval rows the old fallback stays. `DeskTerm.LaneCycle` carries the result (published term only). `DeskTermSource` reads documents, mean and P90 service with the cycle, passes them through `LaneCycle.PerPerson` with `CycleMethod` (MeanService), counts `RefusedIntervals` and logs the site and the count only. The old reading is kept as `LaneCycle.PerTransaction` for the comparisons only.
- Method (docs/product/decisions.md, Proposed pending the owner): mean service time per document, chosen over the cycle capped at the interval's P90 service. The plain cap is biased low: with one or two transactions in a one-minute interval its P90 is its own transaction's service while its cycle is the previous one's, so the cap takes the smaller of two consecutive times. Floored at the mean service (kept in code as `LaneCycleMethod.CycleCappedAtP90`, unused) it measured no better. What mean service gives up: the walk-up gap (D4), absent from the simulator; the shadow's sensor cycle time has the same bias, so the pilot compares like with like.
- Comparison (reference evening, seed 9303, 17:20 to 20:25, Visitors desks all AMAN, AMAN live; Ariva's own simulator, not field data; `SensorCycleScenarioTests.Published_Should_TakeTheLaneCyclePerPersonInWorkingTime_When_AmanPublishesFamiliesAndLulls`):
