## 2026-10-16 CI: the Kafka test fixture hands out a broker only once it names a controller (QueueStreamScaleOutTests)
- `QueueStreamScaleOutTests.Worker_Should_KeepEveryZone_When_PartitionsAreAddedWhileItRuns` failed in PR #67's CI on d5ae9e7 (a run being cancelled) and on c3ec4b1, passing on 3b77c55 between them: "Failed while waiting for controller: Local: Timed out" after 60 s at its first statement, `CreateTopicsAsync` on the class's fresh Kafka container. Testcontainers.Kafka 4.15.0 (decompiled) reports a KRaft broker ready when it logs "Transitioning from RECOVERY to RUNNING"; this class is the one that calls the admin API at once (the others start a host first, whose topic provisioning retries), so a first metadata answer without a controller left librdkafka's admin request waiting its whole timeout. Not reproduced locally.
- Fix (test infrastructure): `KafkaContainers.UntilControllerAsync` polls `DescribeClusterAsync` with a new admin client per try (5 s each, every 500 ms, bounded at 2 minutes with a fixed message) until the broker names a controller, and `KafkaFixture.InitializeAsync` calls it after the start, so every class of the fixture (KafkaPipelineTests, TopicProvisioningTests, AmanKafkaTests, QueueStreamTests, QueueStreamScaleOutTests, QueueStreamEventTimeTests) gets a broker with a controller. The six classes 61 of 61. CI on the push is the evidence for the race itself.

## 2026-10-16 ARV-127: Basic offline install bundle
- Built `scripts/offline/bundle.mjs` (the release script), `scripts/offline/verify.mjs` (the verifier for a connected machine), `scripts/offline/stand-ins.mjs` (cosign, ORAS and docker stand-ins for the self-tests), `Platform/Cloud/Ariva.K8s/Helm/helmfile-offline.yaml.gotmpl` (the bundle's Helmfile) and `.github/workflows/offline-bundle.yml` (by hand from a version tag or main). The bundle holds the seven Ariva images as OCI layouts by digest with their cosign signature and SBOM attestation as referrers (ORAS 1.3 `copy -r`), TimescaleDB by the digest its chart pins, each SBOM from its verified attestation, the packaged charts, the values files, `images.yaml` and `timescaledb-image.yaml`, and the web build. All of it sits under `SHA256SUMS` and a `manifest.json` that the workflow signs keyless. ci.yml runs a dry run on every pull request (web job): verified, with an altered chart archive refused. wiki/04 section 12 now describes the procedure as implemented: produce, verify on a connected machine, recheck after the carry, mirror, install, and what stays Target.
- Found while building: the target procedure listed only "the seven images", but the TimescaleDB release pulls `timescale/timescaledb-ha` from Docker Hub, which an air-gapped site cannot reach; the bundle carries it (both platforms of the pinned index digest). The first real-tool rehearsal caught a path rule that refused Vite chunk names starting with "-" (`_app/immutable/chunks/-CWa0sji.js`): every real web build would have failed; fixed and pinned in the self-tests.
- TC-52 (web build per site): Proposed answer, one build for every site. The browser calls only Ariva.Api.Main on the web app's own origin (ADR-0026), and no screen reads the other `VITE_ARIVA_*` URLs, so runtime configuration is needed only if a site ever puts Ariva.Api.Main on a host of its own (wiki/04 section 5, pilot-to-confirm.md).
- Rehearsals (2026-10-16, local `registry:2` from mirror.gcr.io, Docker Hub rate-limited): real ORAS 1.3, cosign 3.0.6 and docker, with a rehearsal key (`--use-signing-config=false --tlog-upload=false`, nothing sent to the public Rekor) and a wrapper that turns the keyless certificate flags into the key. Bundle with 570 files, the web build copied out of a real web image (identical to the build), verification PASS, one appended byte in a web layer refused (hash and content address), `sha256sum -c` and the step 1 checks of section 12.4 as documented, layouts copied into a "site mirror" with signatures and attestations verifying there, the Helmfile rendering every image from the mirror pinned by digest. A key has no certificate, so the identity, ref, commit and trigger checks are proven only through the stand-in; the keyless path is To confirm on the first real bundle, which needs PR #67 on main and the images workflow run.
- Security review round 1 (security-reviewer, 2026-10-16): FAIL.
  - H1: the job that held `id-token: write` also ran `npm ci` and `npm run build`, so a compromised package could have signed its own manifest as this workflow.
  - M1: a dry run's Helmfile rendered with images pulled by tag, while the tools said it could not be installed.
  - M2: the in-site `sha256sum -c` had no trusted reference.
  - M3: version, ref and commit were not tied to the signature, so an older or relabelled bundle could pass.
  - M4: "same commit as the images" was claimed but not checked.
  - M5: a databaseValues file could change the TimescaleDB tag and digest.
  - M6: on Windows a cosign.exe in the bundle could run in place of cosign.
  - Lows L1 to L7: the values files were not checked against the manifest, test gaps, an ASVS overclaim, the out-path prefix check, pipes, TC-54 not cited, and the wording on what the walk follows.
- Round 1 fixes:
  - The workflow is split into a bundle job (read only, no id-token, no npm: the web build comes out of the verified web image) and a signing job (only checkout, cosign sign-blob and the verifier). `base-images.mjs --check` refuses a package manager in any job with `id-token: write`.
  - The offline Helmfile refuses to render unless `images.yaml` pins all seven digests, and lists `timescaledb-image.yaml` after the site's database file.
  - verify.mjs requires `--version` (and `--from-main` for a main build). It verifies the exact identity and trigger first, then the manifest's version, then the signing run's commit. Images must be signed at the manifest's commit (bundle.mjs: at the checkout's).
  - verify.mjs regenerates and compares both values files, starts programs in a private folder, refuses to run inside the bundle, opens files without following links or blocking on pipes, and prints the two hashes to record.
  - Every new control is mutation-checked: hand-made mutants are killed, after one surviving mutant led to the main-bundle version case.
  - Self-tests: verify 101 checks, bundle 53. chart-security gained the dry-run refusal and the planted database image. The story gate passed before the review; the security gate, docs and scan pass after the fixes.
- Security review round 2 (2026-10-16): FAIL, narrowly. Every round 1 High and Medium was confirmed fixed, and the reviewer re-ran the key probes by hand (a dry run with planted site digests is refused by the Helmfile and by `verify.mjs --version`; the verifier refuses to start inside the bundle). Two blockers remained:
  - Medium: the signing-job lint saw only job-level `id-token: write`. It missed the workflow-level permission (inherited by jobs without their own) and `write-all`, and had no lasting test.
  - Low, required by the test rule: nothing proved that programs start in the private folder. On Windows the inside-the-bundle comparison was case-sensitive.
- Round 2 fixes:
  - The lint is now `signingJobProblems` in `scripts/base-images.mjs`, run on every workflow. A job can sign through `id-token: write` or `write-all`, its own or the workflow's when it has none of its own, and only `run:` step bodies are read; the comment names what it cannot see (uses: actions, bun, corepack, `node_modules/.bin`). Its self-test, run by `--check`, holds five bad samples and three good ones; it caught a split regex of mine that had lost its multiline flag. Planting workflow-level `id-token: write` plus npm in the real workflow is reported.
  - The cosign stand-in records the folder each program starts in. The verifier self-test requires one private, empty folder under the temporary folder that is not the current folder (removing `cwd` from `run()` now fails it). The inside-the-bundle comparison uses `realpathSync.native` and folds case on Windows.
  - Advisories taken: the dry-run PASS line reads "an unsigned CI check, not a release: never install it". The in-site recheck compares both `SHA256SUMS` and `manifest.json` with the recorded hashes and counts files against `SHA256SUMS` (+3). A link at the web image's path is refused (`lstat`, stand-in case, mutant killed).
  - Advisory not taken, accepted as Low: the signing job signs before it verifies, so a manifest that then fails verification is already in the public Rekor log. The bundle job that produced it runs no third-party package code, and the bundle is never published (the artifact upload comes after the verification). Revisit if the bundle job ever runs a build.
  - Self-tests: verify 103 checks, bundle 54; security gate and docs pass.
- Security review round 3 (2026-10-16): PASS. Both round 2 blockers were confirmed by the reviewer's own probes:
  - Lint: npm in the sign job, a quoted `'npx foo'`, a folded `run: >-` block, workflow-level `id-token: write` inherited by a job without its own permissions, and job-level `write-all` are all reported; the real workflow is clean.
  - Private folder: the mutant without `cwd: privateRunFolder()` fails the verifier's self-test.
  - CWE-78/77, 94, 501, 269, 494/345/347, 22/59 and 427 are covered, each with a control and a test. Data boundary, secrets, logging and allowlist pass. ASVS V15.1.2 stays Partly with accurate evidence; V13.1.1 stays Met (wiki 05 row 25).
  - Informational Lows, handled before the commit: the lint now also reads quoted values (`"id-token": "write"`, `'write-all'`, with a self-test sample), and its comment names the one remaining limit, job keys indented other than two spaces.
  - The keyless path stays To confirm on the first real bundle, as the wiki and ASVS row say.
- Status: passes set; committed (signed) and pushed. The checkpoint (full suite plus mutation) is due now: 5 stories since f87ea8a.

## 2026-10-17 ARV-145 Advertising policy per site, off by default

- Owner decision (2026-10-16, docs/product/decisions.md): advertising stays off by default; only a SystemAdministrator with a second factor turns it on per site; the reason names who authorised it (the border authority or the airport operator) and the audit keeps it; zone exclusions; no border co-sign.
- What changed:
  - `AdvertisingPolicy` (script 0057, table `advertising_policy`): per site, allowed, up to 20 excluded queue zones, a reason of 10 to 500 characters on one line, and the published zone profile it was saved against (`confirmed_profile_id`). A site without a row has advertising off. The runtime role cannot delete a policy.
  - Permissions `AdvertisingPolicy.View` (the display roles) and `AdvertisingPolicy.Edit` (system administrators only, a critical action with step-up). `api/v1/admin/sites/{siteCode}/advertising-policy` GET and PUT, `[SiteScoped]`, audited as `AdvertisingPolicy.Changed` with the whole policy before and after.
  - The rule (`AdvertisingPolicyGuard`, used by the display service under a per-site advisory lock, class 145, by the board on each refresh, and by the view): a display may show advertising only while the site allows it, the policy was saved against the published zone profile of now, every excluded zone and every zone the display shows is a queue zone of that profile, and none of its zones is excluded. Script 0057's trigger checks the same rule for every write of a display (insert, change, restore), reading the policy row FOR SHARE, with a pinned search_path.
  - An allowing save names the profile version it was reviewed against and answers 409 when another was published meanwhile; turning advertising off needs no review.
  - A display set to advertising keeps the setting when the policy or the profile changes; its board falls back to instructions at the next poll, and the panel lists it. A site configuration import refuses displays set to advertising (a new site starts off, the policy never travels).
  - `[AdvertisingAllowed]` for the advertising endpoints of ARV-142 and ARV-143 (403 while off, 404 outside the caller's sites); `AdvertisingAllowedTests` boots every host and fails the build when an endpoint whose route names advertising, or whose controller is in an Advertising namespace, lacks it. ARV-142 and ARV-143 gained the criteria for the convention, the player's media fetch and IDOR filtering.
  - Web: the Advertising policy panel on Passenger displays (state, excluded zones, the reason as text, warnings for a newer profile or unpublished zones, the displays falling back; the form for administrators shows the profile version it confirms and offers that version's queue zones); the display form offers Advertising only where the policy allows it; the player carries the effective second region as `data-second-region`. English and Arabic.
  - Docs: wiki 11 section 9 (Advertising policy), wiki 12, 13 and 17; cwe-controls CWE-862, 863 and 269; asvs-l2 V2.3.1, V8.2.1 and V8.2.2; data inventory (the reason is "Possibly" personal free text); decisions.md (implementation points 1 to 7 and the open decisions row).
- Tests: unit `AdvertisingPolicyTests`, `AdvertisingAllowedTests` (filter and the booted-host endpoint check with its classifier), `DisplayTests`, `SiteConfigurationTransferTests`, matrix and critical-action rows; integration `AdvertisingPolicyServiceTests` (own database: off by default, change and audit, refusals without echo, site scope, displays and the board's fallback, the trigger on update, insert and restore, a padded zone, a tab, a no-break space, a key in capitals, an overflow zone, a policy with no profile, the duty manager's rename through the zone profile workflow, an unchanged republish, a stale review refused with no audit entry, a display set to advertising while the policy is turned off, by the service and by a direct write, and two first changes at once); e2e `api/advertising-policy.spec.ts` (AUH-TA: off, step-up, 403, 409 for a stale review, refusals without echo, zone exclusion and the board's fallback, another site 404, attack payloads as the site code) and `functional/advertising-policy.spec.ts` (an administrator allows advertising after a step-up with markup in the reason shown as text, Arabic; a duty manager without the change button; the form's Advertising option; warnings in English and Arabic; the screen's 409 path).
- Gotchas:
  - Exclusions by zone name are not enough on their own: the roles that edit zone profiles can rename, move or add zones, or give an excluded name to a decoy. The policy is therefore pinned to the published profile, and every new profile turns advertising off until an administrator saves the policy again, at the cost of one save per new profile (rare).
  - The Write tool turns `\u202e` and similar escapes into the characters (SEC-130 caught it again); a Bash heredoc did the same for some of them. Python replaced them with escapes.
  - Killing `node scripts/verify.mjs` leaves its integration or Playwright child running; kill the whole tree by PID, and never `pkill -f` a pattern that matches your own shell (it ended the shell once, exit 144).
  - The container restarted once mid-gate (Docker daemon and the first review lost); the gate and the review ran again from the start.
- Security review: round 1 (FAIL: Medium, a zone rename lifts an exclusion; Low, untested trigger paths and races; Low, architecture test blind spots), round 2 (FAIL: Low, a decoy zone under the excluded name; plus trimming, the form's check, ASVS evidence, IDOR criteria), round 3 (FAIL: Low, a save confirms a profile published during the review), round 4 (FAIL: Low, the panel's zone list from a separate read), all built as described above. Round 5 (2026-10-17): PASS for CWE-862, 863, 269, 79, 89 and 501; two advisories (the panel's form survives a site or profile change; a null zone dropped before the board's rule, unreachable) recorded as ARV-193 in Phase 3 under the owner's standing decision.

## 2026-10-17 ARV-142a Advertisement image library with safe uploads and two-person approval
- Split: ARV-142 was split by the lead on 2026-10-17 (CLAUDE.md, a story too big for one session): ARV-142a holds the images, the two-person approval, the display fetch and the screen; ARV-142b the MP4 and WebM container checks (two parsers that strip metadata without moving the media) and the CSP's media-src. ARV-143 and ARV-137 now depend on both.
- What changed:
  - `AdvertisingMedia` (script 0058, site-bound, audited, retired rather than deleted): the stored image (generated key, type, size, hash, pixels, the file name for people), the advertiser, campaign and the site's local days it may play (at most 731 apart), a status Draft, Approved or Retired, and who uploaded, last changed and approved it. Only an approved item within its days plays; the approver is neither the uploader nor the last changer and names the item's review token as it was shown (409 once it changed); a change of an approved item sends it back to draft; retired is final. Script 0058 holds the same rules for any writer (CHECKs and a guard trigger on insert and update; the runtime role cannot delete).
  - `AdvertisingImages` (Ariva.Infra): managed code reads the header (signature, size, APNG `acTL`, WebP animation flag) and refuses above 10 MB, 3,840 pixels a side or 8,294,400 pixels, animated images and JPEGs of more than 64 scans before any native code reads the file; SkiaSharp 4.153.1 then decodes the picture (same format and size or refused), turns it upright from its EXIF orientation, converts it to sRGB and encodes it again in its own type with low effort, one at a time per process. SkiaSharp is a private reference of Ariva.Infra: only Ariva.Api.Main and the test projects carry it and its Linux native library; a Directory.Build.props target keeps four runtimes' natives without symbols in builds without a runtime identifier.
  - `Advertising.View`, `Advertising.Manage` and `Advertising.Approve` (a new `Approve` action; Approve is a critical permission), for terminal duty managers and, through the every-permission rule, system administrators. `api/v1/admin/sites/{siteCode}/advertising/media` (list, get, content, upload, change, approve, retire) in `Controllers/AdminArea/Advertising` with `[SiteScoped]` and `[AdvertisingAllowed]`; every lookup by id is filtered by the route's site; 30 upload attempts per person in 10 minutes (`AdvertisingUploadWindow`, 429). `api/v1/display/advertising/{id}` is display-authenticated and serves only an approved item of the display's own site within its days while the display is set to advertising and the ARV-145 rule allows it, read on every fetch.
  - The bounded read of uploads (`UploadReader`) is shared with floor plans; the storage key pattern takes `webp`.
  - The library on the Passenger displays screen (`AdvertisingLibrary.svelte`) while the site's policy allows advertising: upload with the advertiser, campaign and days, previews from object URLs, change (with the back-to-draft warning), approve (only offered to a person who may, sending the row's review token), retire (asked on the page); English and Arabic.
- Tests:
  - Unit: `AdvertisingMediaTests`, `AdvertisingImagesTests` (polyglot PNG, JPEG and WebP, EXIF orientation, SVG, HTML, PDF, GIF, BMP, MP4 and WebM refused, truncated, header bombs refused in managed code, side and pixel limits, JPEG scans, animated WebP and APNG, the managed header reader, a 4K time budget), `AdvertisingImagePropertyTests` (CsCheck mutations), `AdvertisingUploadWindowTests`, `PermissionModelTests`, `AdvertisingAllowedTests` (the display fetch exempt by type and asserted display-authenticated), the permission matrix and critical action registries.
  - Integration `AdvertisingMediaServiceTests` (34): upload of a polyglot and its audit, refusals storing nothing, the two-person rule, the review token, IDOR, retire, the display fetch rules, 18 writes the runtime role is refused (script 0058), an approval waiting for a change in progress, the library cap race, the per-person window counting refused files.
  - E2E `api/advertising-media.spec.ts` (upload attacks, markup kept as text, approval with and without a fresh second factor, a stale review token 409, IDOR, a site with advertising off 403, the display fetch with and without its credential, retire, advertising turned off) and `functional/advertising-media.spec.ts` (upload, XSS probes in the advertiser, campaign and file name, form refusals, approval by a second duty manager, back to draft, retire, Arabic, the library absent where advertising is off).
- Gotchas:
  - SkiaSharp's natives (13 Linux runtimes, Windows with 95 MB of symbols each) filled the session's disk in one build: keep the private reference and the trimming target in Directory.Build.props.
  - The endpoint rate limiter runs before authentication, so a per-person limit lives after it (`AdvertisingUploadWindow`, per process).
  - An upload's form is buffered before `[SiteScoped]` and `[AdvertisingAllowed]` run (action filters), as with floor plans, within the 10 MB and form limits.
  - `SKCodec.FrameCount` is 0 for an APNG: animation is read from the PNG chunks in managed code.
  - A Python rewrite that opened a file for writing before reading it emptied an untracked test file; it was rebuilt from the conversation. Read first, then write.
  - The E2E project has no Prettier configuration: formatting its existing files with defaults rewrites them; only the new specs were formatted (wide).
  - The svelte and shadcn-svelte MCP servers were unreachable (proxy 403) and the semgrep MCP unavailable: svelte-check, prettier and the security scan were the checks.
  - The disk filled again during the first story gate (8.4 GB of old E2E logs on top of the SkiaSharp natives): every integration failure was PostgreSQL's "No space left on device". The old logs were compressed (8.4 GB to 681 MB); check `df` before a full gate.

Decision point (10), whether the decoders may stay in the host that signs tokens, is open for the owner in docs/product/decisions.md. The semgrep MCP was unavailable in this session.
- Gates (2026-10-17): `node scripts/verify.mjs story --specs` with the advertising media and policy, displays, step-up and floor plan specs, widened to the full suites (a new script and a wide change): unit 6,182, integration 650 passed and 1 skipped, E2E 811 passed and 1 skipped, every build, security, chart, offline bundle, audit, docs and web step passed. The run before it failed: integration on the full disk, and E2E on the smoke role's action list, the matrix answer for a site that does not exist and the policy spec's library 403 (all fixed above). After the A1 and A2 edits, `AdvertisingAllowedTests` (20) passed again.

## 2026-10-17 ARV-142b Advertisement videos: MP4 (H.264) and WebM within a configured length and size
- What changed:
  - `AdvertisingVideos` (Ariva.Infra/Storage): managed readers of the MP4 (ISO base media) and WebM (EBML) containers, no decoder. A file that starts with an `ftyp` box or an EBML header is a video; every box and element lies within its parent and the file, at most 12 deep and 4,096 read, nothing allocated from a declared size, the media data never walked. MP4: an MP4 brand (QuickTime refused), one `moov`, not fragmented, picture tracks `avc1` or `avc3` with `avcC`, sound `mp4a` version 0 carrying AAC, the movie's length known. WebM: document type `webm`, one segment of known size ending at the file's end, VP8, VP9 or AV1 and Opus or Vorbis, no `ContentEncodings`, a `Duration`. One picture track, at most one sound track, a picture within 3,840 pixels a side and 8,294,400 in all. Metadata stripped in place (`udta`, `meta`, `uuid` to zeroed `free`; free space, handler and compressor names and creation times zeroed; WebM `Tags`, `Attachments`, `Chapters`, titles, dates, track names and CRCs to `Void` of the same length); `MuxingApp` and `WritingApp` kept.
  - Stated values cross-checked: no MP4 track or media header more than a second past the movie's length, every WebM cluster opening with its start and none past the stated length, WebM timed in milliseconds. The picture data is not decoded: the size and length are what the container states (residual, decisions.md point (9)).
  - `Advertising:Videos` (`AdvertisingVideoSettings`): 20 MB and 30 seconds by default, at most 100 MB and 120 seconds (`AdvertisingMedia.MaxVideoBytes`, `MaxVideoSeconds`), checked at start-up. The upload endpoint declares the ceiling plus framing; `AdvertisingUploadLimitAttribute` (a resource filter) lowers the body limit to the larger of 10 MB and the setting plus 64 KB, answers 413 for a larger declared body, reads the form itself so a chunked body is cut off at the limit with the same 413, answers 400 or 408 with fixed text for an unreadable or too slow form, and sets 32 KB a second over HTTP/1.x. The service holds the file again on its declared length and in the read (`UploadReader` sizes its buffer from the declared length), then to the setting for a video (413 "The file is larger than N MB.", 400 "The video is longer than N seconds.", 400 `UnsupportedVideo`).
  - Script 0059: `duration_milliseconds` (null for an image, required for a video, at most 120,000), the CHECKs widened to the two video types, their extensions and 100 MB, and the guard trigger replaced with the length among what an item keeps. The storage key pattern takes `mp4` and `webm`.
  - Web: the library takes videos, shows their length and loads a video only when asked, playing it muted from an object URL; the CSP gains `media-src 'self' blob:` (shell spec asserts it). English and Arabic. The display player's playback is ARV-143's (its notes now say how).
  - Fixtures: `Platform/Testing/Media` (five two-second ffmpeg test patterns and a README of how they were made), linked into the unit and integration test outputs and read by the E2E specs.
- Tests:
  - Unit: `AdvertisingVideosTests` (74 cases on the fixtures: every container and codec, stripping checked byte for byte, every refusal, lying sizes, 64-bit sizes, the box and element limits, stated lengths of tracks, media and clusters, WebM timing, settings), `AdvertisingVideoPropertyTests` (CsCheck mutations of every fixture and of their headers), `AdvertisingUploadLimitTests` (11: the limit lowered for 20, 5 and 100 MB, 413 for a declared larger body, 400 for a form cut short, 408 for a slow body, the rate over HTTP/1.1 only, never raised, the attributes on the action), `AdvertisingMediaTests` (video file rules, the length in the audit), `FloorPlanFilesTests` (keys).
  - Integration `AdvertisingMediaServiceTests` (50): MP4 and WebM kept stripped with their length and audit, eight video refusals storing nothing, an approved video served to a display with its type, seven more runtime-role refusals for script 0059 and a video's length kept.
  - E2E `api/advertising-media.spec.ts` (videos typed by their container whatever their declared type, stripped, markup in free and uuid boxes zeroed, approval and display fetch of a video; ten container attacks, 30.001 s, over 20 MB, a 25 MB body, 60 MB streamed without a length cut off near 20 MB with nothing stored), `functional/advertising-media.spec.ts` (a WebM through the screen, its length, loaded only when asked, played from a blob: URL, Arabic), `functional/shell.spec.ts` (`media-src 'self' blob:`).
- Gotchas:
  - A WebM SeekHead names its targets' identifiers as data: the first `12 54 C3 67` in a file is the SeekHead's reference to the tags, not the tags. Walk the segment's children to find an element.
  - The `ftyp` box lists `avc1` among its compatible brands: patching the first `avc1` in a file changes the brand, not the codec; patch after `stsd`.
  - Playwright's Chromium has no H.264 or AAC: the functional test plays the VP9 and Opus fixture; MP4 is proven at the API and with ffmpeg (every stripped fixture decodes without an error).
  - The Docker daemon stopped mid-session again (container restart): restart it with `setsid nohup dockerd` before integration tests.
  - The chart's ingress for Ariva.Api.Main takes 21 MB: the 20 MB default fits; raising the setting needs the ingress raised too (wiki 11). The files claim is 2Gi, about 90 videos at 20 MB: sizing is open for the owner (decisions.md point (8)).
  - A request size limit declared as an attribute is static: to hold an upload to a setting, lower `IHttpMaxRequestBodySizeFeature` in a resource filter (after the size limit's authorization filter, before model binding) and read the form there, or a chunked body is held only to the attribute's ceiling.
  - Kestrel takes a per-request minimum body rate only over HTTP/1.x; on HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 setting one throws.
  - The form reader skips the body when the declared length is 0: a unit test of a body that fails while read sends no length.
  - Building a host while the E2E hosts run from the same output can disturb them: stop or wait for the run first.
  - Large theory data loses results silently: two rows of 20 MB byte arrays in `AdvertisingMediaServiceTests` made the full integration run report 388 of 645 tests, "Passed!" with no failure. Every class after them in the shared Postgres collection went unreported (a filtered run of the class alone passed all 50). The rows now name their files by a key and the test makes them. Check the total against `--list-tests` after adding theory data.
  - A server that answers 413 before taking a large body closes the connection: Node's fetch then fails with EPIPE instead of reading the answer. The specs send such bodies through `http.request` and stop writing when the answer comes (`streamUpload`).
  - Each person may attempt 30 uploads in 10 minutes, and a retry of a serial group attempts every upload again: a spec keeps each account under 15 per attempt (the path tricks and the video attacks have accounts of their own), or the retry of one failure turns into 429s.
- Security review: round 1 (FAIL: Medium, the cut-off of a body sent without a length untested, now read in the filter and tested end to end with a 60 MB stream; Low, the CWE-79 row overstated which CRCs and metadata are voided; Low, the pixel and length limits are what the container states, now said so with the residual; recommendations taken: track, media and cluster lengths cross-checked, a minimum upload rate, the double click on Load the video, 413 for both kinds of oversize), round 2 (FAIL: the minimum rate untested and throwing on HTTP/2, now set over HTTP/1.x only and tested; WebM timed in milliseconds and the doc counts taken from its notes; the Ingest push endpoint's same pattern recorded as ARV-195 in Phase 3), round 3 (PASS, on the gate passing, for CWE-434, 79, 400 and 120, and 501, 863, 89 and 269 where touched; the reviewer's own harness ran 696,288 mutated inputs through the check with no exception and no broken invariant). Scan 1,501 files, 0 errors; no ASVS status changed. The semgrep and Microsoft Learn MCP servers were unavailable in this session.
- Gates (2026-10-18): `node scripts/verify.mjs story --specs` with the advertising media and policy, displays, shell, floor plan and step-up specs, widened to the full suites (a new script and a wide change): unit 6,288, integration 666 passed and 1 skipped (667, every test reported), E2E 812 passed, 2 flaky and 1 skipped, every other step passed. The two flaky tests:
  - The streamed upload's own race: the server closes the connection before its answer is read. The helper now sends `Expect: 100-continue` for a declared length and tries the chunked case up to three times; the video attacks then passed twice running and both advertising-media specs passed 15 of 15 with retries off.
  - `validation-rehearsal.spec.ts`: a random airport code collided with another spec's (not this story's; recorded as ARV-196 in Phase 3).
  - The runs before: the first failed in E2E (fetch's EPIPE on the early 413, then the image attacks' 429 on the serial retry) and reported 388 integration tests (the 20 MB theory rows); the second, after the fixes, is the one above.
- Status: passes set; committed (signed) and pushed.

## 2026-10-18 ARV-143a Advertising playlists and schedules, with a timeline preview

- Split: the lead split ARV-143 on 2026-10-18 into ARV-143a (the plan: playlists, schedules, the timeline preview and the Advertising screen) and ARV-143b (the board playing it: the player, the wait threshold in minutes with hysteresis, the fallbacks to instructions, a bounded cache). The player is a risk of its own (the display host, its cache, the fetch with the display credential) and the two did not fit one story; ARV-144 and ARV-137 now depend on both (prd-phase2.json, prd-phase1.json).
- What changed:
  - Domain (Ariva.Core): `AdvertisingPlaylist` (name, 1 to 40 items of kind Media or Slide with seconds and weight, status), `AdvertisingSchedule` (playlist, the slides' Site, Zone or Display targets, days, a local window as `OperatingInterval`, status) and the pure `AdvertisingSchedules` (Resolve: a display's schedule before a zone's before the site's, then the window opened last, then the newest; Timeline: minute by minute from the site's local midnight, merged into stretches). `DisplayTargets` extracted from the slides' values so both use the same target rules.
  - Services (Ariva.Infra): `SvcAdvertisingPlaylists` and `SvcAdvertisingSchedules` within the caller's sites, every lookup by id and the route's site together (404 otherwise), items and playlists checked against the site, video slots from the stored length capped at the installation's `Advertising:Videos:MaxSeconds`, caps of 100 playlists and 200 schedules under advisory locks 1431 and 1432 (409), row locks on change, audit of every change, a timeline per live display with its second region.

## 2026-10-18 ARV-144 follow-up: a play is completed only when it filled its slot

- Found by CI on d70b353 (PR #67, Playwright): on a slow runner an advertisement's bytes came late in its slot, the player still reported the play completed at the slot's end, and the server (completed needs the slot less 2 seconds) refused it, so an honest play was lost; the proof of play functional test also anchored the plan's end on the first board, so a late first image left time for fewer plays. Reproduced locally by delaying the advertisement fetch 3 seconds: {accepted 2, refused 1}.
- What changed: `play-log.ts` takes the slot's seconds at `start` (nothing starts without a positive slot) and reports a play completed only when it lasted to the slot's end and was on screen for the slot within `playLimits.slotToleranceMilliseconds` (2,000, the server's tolerance); `AdvertisingRegion` passes the item's seconds, the display page passes them on. The server is unchanged. The functional test warms the player's cache (the boards play B then A until both images are held), then restarts the plan in the playlist's order and anchors its end on that board; it checks the server accepts every play, the warm-up ones included, and that none is completed without filling its slot. `api/advertising-play-log.spec.ts` covers a late image cut short, 1.5 seconds late still completed, and invalid slots. Docs: wiki 11 (the play's definition), decisions.md ARV-144 point (1).
- Gotcha: a play's "completed" must be judged by the same rule as the server's, or a slow network turns honest plays into refusals.
- Gates: the proof of play test with the 3-second delay passed (the old one failed); the player and play log specs 20 of 20; `verify.mjs web` and `quick` passed. Security reviewer: PASS (the player reports completed less often, never more; the server stays the authority).

## 2026-10-18 ARV-144 follow-up: a slot that ends no longer ends the next slot's play

- Found by CI on PR #67 (e69765c, 690f3dd, 4d2740c: the proof of play test failed on both tries every time, with only one play after the plan's restart where three were expected). The test's failure message was made to print its timeline (690f3dd), then every image the region inserts, its load and the page's play counters (4d2740c); CI's trace cannot be fetched from the agent's session. The cause, read from CI's timeline: Chromium 153 (CI) shows an image whose blob: URL already loaded complete at insertion, where Chromium 141 (this repository's local browser) loads it again first. The region's picture action then calls `appeared` synchronously and starts the next slot's play inside the same update, before the ended slot's `$effect` teardown runs; that teardown called `gone(false)` unconditionally and ended the new play at about 0 ms, which the play log drops (under a second). Every play after an image's first repeat was lost: a product bug on current Chrome, not a test artifact.
- What changed: `AdvertisingRegion.svelte` `gone(completed, fromSlot)` ends the play on screen only when it belongs to the slot that is leaving (the slot effect's teardown, `advance` and `mediaFailed` pass theirs; the region's destruction and the page's pagehide still end whatever is on screen). The proof of play test installs `showLoadedImagesAtOnce` (an init script: a blob: image that loaded once reports complete with its size at insertion, as Chromium 153 does), so local runs cover the path; the timeline diagnostics stay in its failure message.
- Gates: reproduced locally with the helper before the fix (the play counter stuck at 3, as on CI) and 2 of 2 passed after; the advertising player, play log, plays, displays and display slides specs 41 of 41; `verify.mjs web` passed. Security reviewer: PASS (no play can run on or count twice: the play log's start ends any open play, `playedSlot` stops a second start, the teardown clears the slot timer; the server stays the authority). svelte-autofixer was unavailable (the svelte MCP server could not connect).
- Gotcha: never end "whatever is on screen" from a teardown that belongs to one slot; scope it to that slot, because a browser can show the next one first.

## 2026-10-19 ARV-085: Network policies, trusted proxies and private probes

- What changed: the chart ships NetworkPolicies (`templates/networkpolicies.yaml`, `networkPolicies.*`): a default deny for every Ariva pod (the five API hosts, the web pod, the migration and topics jobs, the simulator) and exactly the firewall matrix's flows. In: the ingress controller (namespace and pod selectors, `ingressController.*`) to each routed pod's serving port, the sensor networks to Ingest's MQTT port, the simulator flows in dev and demo. Out: DNS, the database, Kafka, Redis, the OTLP collector and Loki for the pods that use them, the SMTP relay for api-integration and api-cronz (`ariva-smtp-egress`; Cronz sends the scheduled reports itself), and each outbound endpoint for api-integration only. No rule renders without peers and ports; the prd values ship no peers for OTLP, Loki, SMTP or outbound, so those stay closed until the site gives them. In k8s-prd the chart and both Helmfiles refuse the policies off, ipBlocks wider than /8 or /16, every-namespace selectors and malformed CIDRs.
- Trusted proxies: `appsettings.base.k8s-prd.json` lists no network; the chart passes `ingressController.podNetworks` as `Security__ForwardedHeaders__KnownNetworks__<n>` to every host, and in k8s-prd a host refuses to start (`ForwardedHeadersExtensions.EnsureProductionTrust`) when it trusts nobody, everybody, a network wider than IPv4 /14 or IPv6 /48, an entry it cannot read, address bits after the prefix, or an IPv6 network that would trust IPv4-mapped clients (prefix mod 32 under 14, or /96 or wider holding ::ffff:0:0/96). The chart refuses the same values (`ariva-platform.mappedClientsRefusal`, an agreement test over 697 networks). use-forwarded-headers stays off on the controller (ARV-084).
- Private probes: every host's server-snippet answers `/health`, `/health/*` and `/healthz` 404 at server level, case-insensitively, before any location, with HSTS, nosniff and frame-ancestors 'none'. The chart refuses `rewrite-target`, `use-regex` and any annotation value that writes an nginx rewrite, in every environment (the shipped `rewrite-target: /` on "/" Ingresses applied no rewrite and are removed). In k8s-prd the Cronz Ingress needs `sourceRanges` (`allowlist-source-range`; the `whitelist-source-range` alias refused). tls-check reads `/health/readiness` and needs 404 or 403 with the generated headers; a weak protocol or suite answered with a certificate that does not verify now counts as accepted. The release smoke suite against a deployed site requires the probe 404 with the ingress's headers, then proves each host up with an anonymous read the host itself refuses (its own 401 problem); locally it still reads readiness.
- Files: chart (networkpolicies.yaml, _helpers.tpl, validate.yaml, api-*.yaml, values and the four environment values), helmfile-k8s and helmfile-offline, tests/checks.mjs, chart-security.mjs and fixtures (network-policy-*, ingress-privacy-*, bad.yaml), Ariva.Api.Common (ForwardedHeadersExtensions, SecurityBaselineExtensions, ClientCertificateExtensions and ForwardedHeadersSettings comments, appsettings.base.k8s-prd.json), Ariva.UnitTests (Security/ForwardedHeadersTests.cs, Setup/ArivaHosts.cs), scripts/ops/tls-check.mjs and README, Ariva.E2E tests/smoke/health.spec.ts, docs asvs-l2 (V13.2.5, V4.1.3, V15.3.4, V13.4.5 Met in production; summary 135 Met of 203), cwe-controls (CWE-918, CWE-306, CWE-501), security/README.md, wiki 04, 05, 10, 13, 18.
- Gotchas: a NetworkPolicy cannot block the kubelet's probes from the pod's own node, so the probes need no rule; on a CNI that does not enforce NetworkPolicy the policies are accepted and silently inert (wiki 13 checklist item 4), and then any pod can send an X-Forwarded-For the hosts believe, because the shipped trusted network is the whole pod CIDR. .NET masks address bits after the prefix silently and matches an IPv4-mapped client against an IPv6 network with a prefix mod 32 mask, so Cilium's default IPv6 pool fd00::/104 is refused (use fd00::/96 or the IPv4 pod network). Behind SNAT every client arrives as a node or load balancer address: the Cronz source range and per-address limits need `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` or the PROXY protocol. ## 2026-10-19 ARV-091: Security event logging

- Scope after the split: ARV-091 keeps the request context, the security events for refused requests, the log protection levels and the log inventory; ARV-091a takes production log shipping and the pseudonym key secret; ARV-091b takes the sign-in, logout and refresh events (login freeze). No frozen authentication file was edited; the frozen flows are only observed when a request ends.
- Request context (`Ariva.Api.Common/Logging/RequestLogContext.cs`, `Middlewares/RequestLogContextMiddleware.cs`, inside UseAppForwardedHeaders): every line written during a request carries CallerAddress and CallerUserId (a GUID, anonymous or unknown) with CallerSessionId, or CallerClientId, CallerDeviceId or CallerDisplayId, identified at the authorization decision; never names, emails or credentials; the enricher overwrites these names, so a line about a target account keeps the target in {UserId} and the administrator in the Caller fields. Serilog 4.3 already writes TraceId and SpanId.
- Security events (`Logging/SecurityEvents.cs`, `SecurityEventLog.cs`, `Security/SecurityEventResultHandler.cs` decorating StepUpResultHandler with unchanged answers): 9114 forbidden, 9115 challenged, 9116 rate limited (policy and partition kind, never the key), 9117 invalid model, 9118 strict JSON, 9119 repeated query, 9127 NUL, 9128 site scope, 9129 RequestRefused (any 401, 403 or 429 no other event recorded, which covers the revoked session, the pending account, service 403s such as BorderOnly and the integration and upload 429s), 9130 EventsSuppressed; Warning, pinned in code; no refused input, member names, query or route values. Throttle: 60 a second per kind per process, 3 a second per source (the caller, else the address, IPv6 by /64), 1,024 sources plus an overflow share, summaries every 10 s and at shutdown; metric ariva.security.events {kind, outcome}; a failed event never changes an answer.
- Protection levels (`Logging/LogProtection.cs`, `RedactionEnricher.cs`): omit credentials and keys; mask emails and recipients (a***@example.com, also inside text, a NonBacktracking regex); hash track ids and desk codes with HMAC-SHA256 under a per-UTC-day key derived from `Logging:PseudonymKey` (environment only outside vm-local) or a random per-process key; dictionary keys take their dictionary's level, colliding keys kept as `<key>~<n>`; the enricher fails closed per property ([REDACTED], counted in ariva.security.log_protection_failures).
- Logging configuration: only Serilog:MinimumLevel is read; any other Serilog key stops the host; Serilog.Settings.Configuration removed; the file sink (LogFile:Path) refused outside vm-local, the simulator's too; hosts own their logger (preserveStaticLogger).
- Ingress (chart and controller values): SecAuditEngine Off on every Ariva Ingress; the hosts without the hub Ingress answer /hubs 404 at server level in any case, and the web host every non-lowercase spelling; log-format-upstream without the query string; enable-modsecurity, enable-opentelemetry and log-format-escape-none off and error-log-level notice or higher controller-wide, no logging directives in the controller's snippets; enable-opentelemetry pinned off on the hub Ingress; validate.yaml refuses site snippets that re-enable the audit or debug log, copy request values into rule messages, or write logging directives.

## 2026-10-20 CI: CommitRaceTests' stray test budgets its attempts (PR #67, branch story/mvp-phase1; test and CI only)
- PR #67's CI on 33f86f2 failed `CommitRaceTests.Host_Should_LeaveNoConsumerRunning_When_ItStopsWhileAnEndpointIsBetweenRestarts` on its 300 s timeout: four told attempts in a row were still Ready 65 s after the cut (`PremiseBound` then), about 72 s each, and every attempt kept its group empty after the stop (at most 0 members). Integration 720 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped; unit 7,143 passed; E2E did not run.
- Change (test only, `Ariva.IntegrationTests/Faults/CommitRaceTests.cs`):
  - `PremiseBound` 90 s (was 65). The stray test has its own budget (`StrayBudget`, 560 s) and `[Fact(Timeout = 600_000)]`; an attempt starts only while the budget still holds `AttemptBound` (135 s: the premise bound, the 20 s watch after a stop between restarts, and 25 s for the start, the race, the stop and the dispose), so the test ends on its own assertion with its steps, never on the timeout. `StrayAttempts` (8) stays as a cap. The health and stop tests keep their 270 s budget and 300 s timeout.
  - Diagnostics: `StrayHostLog` (replacing `ConsumerErrorLog`) still counts the consumer's local or fatal error and keeps MassTransit's Debug lines and Ariva's messaging lines, merged when they differ only in numbers, bounded (2,000 distinct lines of 300 characters; a line naming a password is dropped). A told attempt whose endpoint stays Ready writes up to 40 of them to the test output, with times from the cut. The stray test's hosts register `Confluent.Kafka.ClientConfig { Debug = "cgrp,consumer" }` in their container, which MassTransit.Kafka 8.5.11's rider takes as its base when `UsingKafka` is given none: librdkafka's consumer group lines (coordinator, deferred commits, rebalances) reach the capture without any Ariva setting, for the rider's consumers only.
- CI: the backend job's timeout is 40 minutes (was 30). The failing job took 23 minutes with the stray test at its old 5 minute timeout, and the test may now take up to about 10 minutes before failing; a job timeout would lose the test's output.
- Why a told consumer can stay Ready (confirmed locally with the `cgrp` log): at the cut the record's commit is deferred ("no coordinator available"), the consumer is told (`Local_AllBrokersDown`) and MassTransit closes it; librdkafka hands the revoke to MassTransit's partition revoked handler, which waits for the partition's checkpointer, that is for the synchronous commit, while librdkafka waits for that commit before terminating. The endpoint is between restarts only when the commit returns. Locally it fails at the session timeout (45.3 s); in CI it was still waiting at 65 s and went through within 3.2 s of the restore. Not proven (librdkafka's source is out of reach through the proxy): a commit sent just before the loss that waits for `socket.timeout.ms` (60 s) and is deferred again, or a late expiry check. The new output tells them apart: look for "Deferring", "OffsetCommit failed", "Consumer group session timed out" and the group's state changes.
- Not a product defect: readiness, the stop and the dispose are bounded on their own (ARV-165), and the health and stop tests pass.
- Evidence: the class three times on the final code (the stream-engineer), 3 of 3 each: attempt 1 told, between restarts 45.3 s after the cut, the group empty for 20 s. A forced miss (told attempts waiting 1 s and a 165 s budget; temporary, reverted) ended with "no attempt 4: 132 s of the budget left, less than an attempt may need (135 s)" and the test failing on its assertion after 32 s, each attempt writing its host log. After a container restart (2026-10-20), a clean build and the class once more: 3 of 3, the stray test 1 m 8 s.
- Gotchas: CI keeps no trx file, so the host log lines show only when the test fails. A MassTransit upgrade that stops taking `ClientConfig` from the container would drop librdkafka's lines silently; the test itself would still work.

## 2026-10-20 ARV-157: Trojan Source check covers every text file (ASVS gaps, branch story/mvp-phase1; scanner, fixtures, allowlist, docs)
- SEC-130 (`scripts/security/scan.mjs`) reads the path of every file git tracks or would add (`git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard`, beside the old walk) and the content of every one that is text, whatever its folder or type: the prototype, the chart tests' fixtures and node_modules, dotfiles, files without extension. The other rules keep their mapped types outside SKIP_DIRS (`textOnly`), and an explicit or `--changed` scan (now `git status --porcelain -z`) reads other fixtures folders with SEC-130 alone; nothing is checked less than at HEAD.
- What it refuses: C0 and C1 controls but tab and line feed (a lone carriage return or U+0085 ends a line in C#, JavaScript or YAML where the scanner saw one, so code after a comment passed every rule; NUL), bidirectional controls and U+061C, zero-width, invisible and format characters, U+2028 and U+2029, the Hangul fillers, tag characters and supplementary variation selectors; and as a whole a file in UTF-16 or UTF-32 (or behind a false byte order mark), a file that is not valid UTF-8 (only a binary type whose bytes carry its signature is skipped; 26 tracked files), and a file that declares another encoding (Python coding lines, XML prologs, CSS @charset, every HTML meta charset from the first meta tag on, and failing closed any C# code page in a project file but `<CodePage>65001</CodePage>` or in a response file but 65001). Findings show hidden characters as escapes.
- Allowlist: the two immutable scripts' CHECK constraints (0020_alert_rule.sql lines 11, 14, 28; 0022_alert_lifecycle.sql lines 25 to 27) hold the characters on purpose: six entries, `approvedBy: PENDING: Ahmad` (the PRD notes record an in-session approval of 2026-10-13; only the owner records it), each scoped to its exact line by a new `line` field that must equal `contains` (the approval guard, `.claude/hooks/guard-paths.mjs`, compares `contains` and not yet `line`; the whole-entry key is the owner's change in ARV-225). A SEC-130 entry needs `line`. `backlog/progress.md`'s three raw U+202E are now the text `\u202E`.
- Self-test: 89 hidden-character fixtures in `fixtures/bad/trojan` (every mapped type, each firing by itself), each whole-file refusal asserted for its own reason, every refused and visible character one by one, hidden characters in file and folder names, exact-line allowlist matching and its rules, `git status -z` parsing, and the `--changed` and full-scan git lists in a scratch repository isolated from the caller's git environment (`isolatedGitEnv`: no GIT_ variables, no global or system configuration; run again with a hook's GIT_DIR naming a decoy repository, and with a global configuration whose pre-commit hook must not run after a control run proves it would). Over 60 mutants across the review rounds; each fails the self-test but four equivalent ones (a second layer behind the isolation, a message that another refusal stands in for, an empty label, the control's throw).
- Gotchas: the harness decodes some `\uXXXX` escapes in tool input into the raw characters (`\uFEFF`, `\u2028`, `\u202E` at times, not always), so an Edit or a heredoc meant to write an escape can write the character itself, which SEC-130 then refuses (or, for U+2028, breaks a regular expression). Write such text through a patch file and convert any raw hidden character back to its escape with a script built from code points before applying it. Git's `*.ps1 text eol=crlf` would corrupt a UTF-16 fixture of that type; UTF-16 fixtures use types left to `text=auto`. Local Playwright reports are walked too (gitignored folders outside SKIP_DIRS): their bundled scripts write `charset=` before an expression, so an empty label declares nothing.
- Gates (2026-10-20): `node scripts/security/scan.mjs --self-test` PASS (44 rules; 89 SEC-130 fixtures; 0 false positives; 14 checklist items); `node scripts/security/scan.mjs` 2,170 files, 0 errors, 12 warnings (the six PENDING SEC-130 entries and six older ones), 26 binaries skipped by signature; `--changed` 0 errors; `verify.mjs docs` PASS; `node scripts/verify.mjs backend` exit 0 (build; reference golden; unit 7,159 with `AllowlistTests` on the new entries; the security scan and self-test; the E2E check self-tests; ops, TLS, base image, published runtime and offline bundle checks; chart security; NuGet and three npm audits). Before the new patterns went in, each was run over the 2,185 files git lists: no false positive.
- Security review (security-reviewer, CWE-94): round 1 FAIL (High: many tracked text files never read; Medium: UTF-16; Medium: the self-test proved only 20 types; four Low); round 2 FAIL (Medium: U+0085 and a lone carriage return as line ends hiding code from SEC-001; Medium: a NUL hiding a script; six Low); round 3 FAIL (Medium: one invalid UTF-8 byte hiding an unmapped file, an .editorconfig among them; Medium: the approval guard not holding `line`; four Low); round 4 FAIL (Medium: the self-test's scratch repository not isolated from a hook's GIT_DIR; Medium: an untested refusal; five Low); rounds 5 to 7 FAIL on Lows in the declared encoding check (spaces in a meta label, the C# code page, conditions, quoted and repeated forms), closed by making it fail closed; round 8 PASS (2026-10-20) with three Low judged not needed before the pilot (character references, MSBuild escapes and evaluated property names in declarations), filed in ARV-225 with the deferred items of every round. ## 2026-10-20 ARV-200: Site CA trust for the log and telemetry collectors (ASVS gaps, branch story/mvp-phase1; backend, chart, docs)

- What changed: a host trusts a site CA for Loki or the OTLP collector when the site names one, and that CA alone. `Otlp:RootCertificate` and `Loki:RootCertificate` name a PEM file (the chart mounts `ca.crt` from the Secrets of `otel.caSecretName` and `logging.lokiCaSecretName`). `Platform/Backplane/Ariva.ServiceDefaults/CollectorTrust.cs` reads it (bounded to 1 MiB; a missing file, a device, a file without a certificate or with a private key stops the host, naming the setting and the path only) and pins named IHttpClientFactory clients through `UseSocketsHttpHandler`: `SslOptions.CertificateChainPolicy` with custom root trust (the file's certificates alone), server authentication, no revocation check and no certificate download, no validation callback (so the handshake's own check, the host name included, decides), no redirect, no cookie, no request logging. The trace, metric and log exporters take the pinned client through `OtlpExporterOptions.HttpClientFactory` under every options name (a `ConfigureNamedOptions` with a null name), with OpenTelemetry's own export deadline and a 1 MiB answer buffer; Serilog's OTLP sink takes the pinned handler (`options.HttpMessageHandler`) and its Loki sink a `LokiHttpClient` over the pinned client, both from `CollectorClients` (`Ariva.Api.Common/Logging/CollectorClients.cs`): a client factory of their own holding the two pinned clients only, without the resilience pipeline (the sinks batch and retry by themselves, as their own clients did before), built by `ArivaLogging.AddCollectorClients` (called by `AddAppLogging` before the logger is built) and registered through a factory, so the host disposes it after the logger and the last batch is still sent; the logger refuses a CA file without it. With a CA file set, that collector's address must be https in every environment (`Otlp:Endpoint` and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, `Loki:Uri`). OpenTelemetry's own certificate variables (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE`, `_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE`, `_CLIENT_KEY`, shared or per signal) are refused outside vm-local: the pin replaces the exporters' own client and the Serilog sink never reads them. Every other client keeps the image's public roots.
- Chart (devops-engineer): `otel.caSecretName` (the five API hosts and the simulator) and `logging.lokiCaSecretName` (the five API hosts), each a secret volume projecting `ca.crt` only, mode 0444, not optional, mounted read-only at `/app/secrets/otlp-ca` or `/app/secrets/loki-ca`, with `Otlp__RootCertificate` or `Loki__RootCertificate`; nothing in the web pod or the jobs. Guards (`validate.yaml`, `ariva-platform.collectorCaRefusal`): a Kubernetes secret name; `otel.caSecretName` needs an https `otel.endpoint`; `logging.lokiCaSecretName` needs `logging.collector` loki; where the release can see the namespace, the Secret must exist and hold `ca.crt` and nothing else (a cert-manager Certificate Secret, a DER key or a keystore beside it are refused), and its `ca.crt` must hold a PEM certificate and no private key, so no private key sits in Ariva's namespace for a collector. `checks.mjs` `collectorCaFindings` and `chart-security.mjs` (real renders of dev, demo and prd, 10 release guard cases, 25 stand-in Secrets for the lookup guard, 25 self-test cases).
- Docs: asvs-l2 (V12.3.1, V12.3.2, V12.3.4 evidence; V16.4.3 residual removed; gap rows ARV-200 Done, ARV-226 Open), log inventory (sinks, startup refusals, transport row, item 8 closed), crypto inventory (K47 collector CAs, A15, item 16 closed), key management (4.12, decision 19), cwe-controls (CWE-918, CWE-287), wiki 04 (Secrets, settings, values, creating and rotating the CA Secret, the `openssl s_client` check), wiki 10 section 4.17 (the new refusals, and nothing arriving), wiki 13 (shipping paragraph; checklist item 15 records the CA each collector chains to, its subject and fingerprint), remaining-work.
- Found by the host test the second review asked for: in a real host the standard resilience pipeline every factory client carries resolves the logger factory through Polly's telemetry, so taking the Loki client from the host's factory inside Serilog's factory callback built the logger again (`ValueFactory attempted to access the Value property`): every k8s-prd host with a collector CA would have refused to start. The unit tests had built bare service collections without that pipeline. `RemoveAllResilienceHandlers` (experimental) does not help, since the handler is built before it is removed; taking the client at the first batch started the hosts but lost the last batch, since the provider is disposed when the final flush runs. Hence `CollectorClients`.
- Filed: ARV-226 (Redis's pinned chain check and its handshake, and the collectors' default clients when no site CA is set, may download a missing intermediate; PostgreSQL and Kafka to be checked; Medium, pre-pilot).
- Tests: `CollectorTrustTests` (57 cases) against a Kestrel TLS collector on loopback (`Fixtures/TlsCollector.cs`, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, a test CA issuing its certificate; options for a certificate naming another host and for a leaf behind an intermediate it does not send) and `Fixtures/IssuerSite.cs` (a plain HTTP issuer address that counts requests). Trusted CA: traces and metrics over http/protobuf and gRPC, the simulator's exported logs, Serilog's OTLP sink over both, Loki all arrive; another CA, no CA file, another host name, or a missing intermediate: nothing arrives, and the issuer address is never fetched (a control chain allowed to download does fetch it). Each of the five hosts started in k8s-prd with a site CA ships its lines through Loki and through OTLP, the line written just before the host is disposed included (the collector records the bodies), and `CollectorClients` hands out its pinned clients only. Mutants: downloads re-enabled (4 tests fail, the behavioural one among them); a callback accepting a name mismatch (8 fail).
- Gotchas: OpenTelemetry's exporters use a factory client of their own over http/protobuf only unless their options name one; setting `HttpClientFactory` covers gRPC too. `RemoveAllResilienceHandlers` is experimental (EXTEXP0001), so the pinned clients keep the standard pipeline (no POST retry). Kestrel's `UseHttps(certificate)` builds a chain online, so a test that needs a leaf served alone uses `TlsHandshakeCallbackOptions` with `SslStreamCertificateContext.Create(leaf, [], offline: true)`. Helm and Helmfile are not installed in the cloud session and get.helm.sh is blocked: Helm 3.19.0 was built from source with `go install` and Helmfile 1.1.7 checked against the checksum in ci.yml (scratchpad only).

## 2026-10-20 ARV-092b: Upload safety: malware scanning in the hosts (ASVS gaps, branch story/mvp-phase1; backend, containers, CI, E2E, docs)

- What changed: every upload Ariva.Api.Main takes is scanned with ClamAV before anything parses, stores or imports it. `Ariva.Infra/Storage/ClamdScanner.cs` is an in-house clamd INSTREAM client over TCP (`MalwareScan:Host`, `Port`, `TimeoutSeconds`, `MaxStreamBytes`; chunks of at most 64 KB, the whole file or nothing: a file over `MaxStreamBytes` is never sent, a stream of unknown length is cut before the limit and the connection dropped without the end mark; the reply read to the first NUL, at most 1 KB; `stream: OK` clean, `stream: <name> FOUND` a detection with the name kept only when it matches `\A[A-Za-z0-9._:/-]{1,128}\z`, anything else no verdict with a fixed reason). `UploadScreening.cs`, called by every upload service after its size check (floor plans and advertisements once read, SSIM and CSV on the preview and again on the import or commit, before the token check, and every decoded part of a site configuration bundle in name order): a detection is refused with 400 and a fixed text in every environment, audited as `Upload.MalwareRefused` in a transaction of its own (who, the kind, the signature, the size and the SHA-256 from a counting and hashing stream, never the file or its name) and logged as security event 9131; no verdict refuses the upload outside vm-local with 503, `Retry-After: 60` and a fixed text (event 9132 with the reason); only vm-local takes it unscanned. Settings are validated at start: `MaxStreamBytes` must cover the largest upload (the advertisement video setting, at most 100 MiB), and a k8s-prd Ariva.Api.Main does not start without `MalwareScan:Host` or with anything but a canonical loopback IP literal (`127.0.0.0/8` or `::1`; not the name `localhost`, which depends on the resolver), since clamd has no TLS (ASVS V12.3.1; the loopback rule added by the main session after the backend agent's report named the plaintext hop, narrowed to IP literals by the security review). A site configuration bundle's parts share one scan deadline (`UploadScreening.ScreenAllAsync`), so a bundle holds the one upload slot no longer than one file. The SSIM service takes a seekable stream only (`RequireSeekable`), scans it and rewinds it to the same start for the reader.
- Containers and CI (devops-engineer): `Platform/Cloud/clamav/clamd.conf` (the image's defaults plus `StreamMaxLength` and `MaxFileSize` 105M, `MaxScanSize` 400M, `AlertExceedsMax yes`, without which clamd reports content over its limits as clean); `clamav/clamav:1.4.3` pinned by digest and run offline (`CLAMAV_NO_FRESHCLAMD`, the image's signature snapshot) in docker-compose (`dev-up` writes the address; `dev-check` proves PING, EICAR and a clean file), the Aspire AppHost (a `ClamdPing` health check, so api-main waits until clamd answers; only api-main gets the address), the CI e2e and ZAP jobs and the Azure DevOps copy (a step after checkout, since GitHub services cannot mount repository files, and a bounded wait for PONG); `ARIVA_E2E_CLAMD` required in CI by the E2E config; `scripts/base-images.mjs` holds one digest across compose, the AppHost, the workflows and the integration fixture.
- Found: clamd's defaults take 100 MiB streams but report content over `MaxFileSize`, `MaxScanSize` or the recursion limits as clean unless `AlertExceedsMax` is on (a 25-level gzip gives `Heuristics.Limits.Exceeded.MaxRecursion FOUND` with it). EICAR is detected only as a file's first bytes: embedded in other bytes (inside a JSON string, for example) clamd answers OK, which is why the bundle's parts are scanned decoded. The Azure DevOps E2E already fails without Kafka (outside this story; for the Azure move).

## 2026-10-20 ARV-092c: Upload safety: ClamAV in the chart (ASVS gaps, branch story/mvp-phase1; chart, backend monitor, offline bundle, docs)

- What changed (chart, devops-engineer): every api-main pod runs clamd beside it on `127.0.0.1:3310` only, and api-main gets `MalwareScan__Host` and `MalwareScan__Port` (no other workload has either). From the pinned `clamav/clamav:1.4.6` image (bumped from 1.4.3 by the security review, below; every copy outside the chart with it), as its own user (uid 100, gid 101), read-only root, no privilege escalation, every capability dropped, RuntimeDefault seccomp, resources per container (clamd request 1200Mi, limit 1600Mi: on 1.4.6, 990 MiB once its 3,628,169 signatures are loaded, 952 MiB resident; it answers 18 s after start on one core, 43 s on half a core); clamd's configuration from a ConfigMap (the repository's limits with `AlertExceedsMax`, `OfficialDatabaseOnly yes`, `MaxThreads 2` and `MaxQueue 4` so its temporary files fit their volume, `ConcurrentDatabaseReload no` so a reload never doubles the memory, `SelfCheck 600`, `CompressLocalDatabase yes`, kept in UTC since Ariva reads its signature date as UTC). Volumes: the signatures 1Gi (a worst incremental update 420 MiB compressed against 760 uncompressed), clamd's /tmp 1536Mi (4 x 105M + 2 x 400M = 1220 MiB); going over either evicts the whole api-main pod, so checks.mjs bounds the arithmetic. Signatures by `uploadScan.signatures.source` (Proposed, the site chooses; k8s-prd has no default and is refused without one): `public` (freshclam from ClamAV's mirrors, dev and demo), `mirror` (freshclam from the site's mirror, `mirrorUrl` checked against a strict pattern since it is written into freshclam.conf, https only in production, and `mirrorCaSecretName` through `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, which in the pinned image is trusted alone: the image keeps no hashed CA files in /etc/ssl/certs, tested with throwaway images), `mounted` (a site claim, read-only, no freshclam); with `public` or `mirror` an init container copies the image's snapshot first so clamd starts at once. A liveness probe only (`clamdscan --ping`, 60 s delay, 90 s window, longer than a reload's 19 s silence), no readiness or startup probe, so a clamd down refuses that pod's uploads but never takes the API out of service; api-main's pod has no service account token; its HPA reads api-main's own container (ContainerResource) on Kubernetes 1.27 or later and the pod's resources below (`.Capabilities.KubeVersion`, both rendered in the chart test). A clamd that runs but is unwell only refuses that pod's uploads; one that cannot start at all leaves the pod NotReady (Kubernetes counts a container that is not running as not ready), as the docs now say. Guards: k8s-prd without `uploadScan` or a source, `mirror` without its URL, `mounted` without its claim, policies on without `networkPolicies.clamavMirror` peers; both Helmfiles' prd state value `uploadScan` forces it on. Alert rules `scannerSignaturesStale` (over 48 hours for 15 minutes, warning) and `scannerNotAnswering` (20 minutes, critical). The offline bundle carries the image; `scripts/base-images.mjs` ties compose, the AppHost and CI to the chart's pin.
- Backend (backend-engineer): the staleness alarm. `IMalwareScanner.SignaturesAsync` asks clamd's VERSION (`ClamAV 1.4.6/28157/Sun Oct 18 06:24:14 2026` from the pinned image, verified against its daily.cvd header), parsed by one anchored pattern (ASCII digits, a real date whose day name matches, nothing around it; a build time over a day ahead counts as no answer). `ScannerSignatureMonitor` in Ariva.Api.Main checks a minute after start and every `MalwareScan:SignatureCheckMinutes` (10, 1 to 60): meter `Ariva.Uploads` with `ariva.uploads.scanner.signature_age` (s) and `ariva.uploads.scanner.answered`; security event 9133 `UploadScanSignaturesStale` over `MalwareScan:MaxSignatureAgeHours` (48, 6 to 168), at most hourly while stale; a throttled Warning when clamd does not answer; never stops the host.
- Found by the security review: the pinned ClamAV 1.4.3 had memory-corruption CVEs fixed in 1.4.5 and 1.4.6 (PE unpackers, 7z, GPT, an extraction limit bypass), in parsers clamd runs on every upload, and nothing in the repository noticed (Trivy scans Ariva's own images only; Dependabot watches Ariva's Dockerfiles only). Bumped to 1.4.6 everywhere, and ARV-227 filed (third-party images: patch releases and known vulnerabilities noticed; High by origin, before the pilot). The fake clamd's reset raced the client's connect (the unit test reported `ConnectFailed` about once in six runs): it now resets after the command arrives.
- Decided in the main session: no startup probe (a pod whose clamd restarts would leave its Service); regular containers, not native sidecars (an upload caught in api-main's drain answers 503 and is retried); the HPA on api-main's container only (clamd's resident memory would keep the host scaled out).

ARV-157 added the fixture; nothing in Linux CI could notice. Renamed to `nul-first.cs` (same bytes, same `.cs` type, so SEC-130's self-test still covers a NUL byte in a mapped type: 89 hidden-character fixtures). It was the only such path in the repository.

It refuses a reserved device name (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, CONIN$, CONOUT$, COM0 to COM9, LPT0 to LPT9, the superscript ones), with or without an extension, a character Windows does not allow in a name, a name ending in a dot or a space, and two paths that differ only in case. It reads the index only, never untracked files. It proves itself first on 11 bad names, 6 good ones and a case clash. It failed on the tree before the rename and passes after.

## 2026-10-21 ARV-096b: Availability bounds on the request path (ASVS gaps, branch story/mvp-phase1; backend, docs)

- What changed:
  - Slots before authentication: the user concurrency policies (`upload`, `backtest`, `validation-results`, `reports`) count every request that sends credentials, read as JWT authentication reads them, the Authorization header's values joined (`RateLimitingExtensions.PresentsCredentials`, `SessionConcurrency`); a request that sends none goes to an unlimited partition (`without-credentials`), since authentication refuses it 401 at once, so it neither takes a slot nor waits for one.
  - Request timeouts on every host: Ariva.Api.Ingest, Stream and Cronz run the default (120 s) after authorization as Main does; on Cronz after `UseTickerQ`, whose dashboard branch ends there, so the dashboard and its hub keep none. Ariva.Api.Integration runs it just before the call audit (after the session checks, which stay untimed), so the audit's read of a batch or AIDX body (with the request's token) ends at the timeout (503) and frees its permit. The Integration token exchange keeps no timeout while the login freeze lasts (`WithoutRequestTimeout<AuthController>`, TEMPORARY like `WithLenientInput`, ARV-089a removes both); AIDX takes the `transfer` timeout (15 minutes), since 5 MB at the slowest rate allowed takes about 170 s.
  - Slow bodies: the alert rule backtest and the validation results' recompute read their bodies with the request's token and, over HTTP/1.x, at 32 KB a second or more (`SteadyUploadAttribute`, with their own 413 texts); the Integration API's batches and AIDX messages get the same rate before the call audit reads them (`SteadyIntegrationBodies`). `SteadyUploadTests` holds every concurrency policy to it, on Main and on Integration.
  - The live hub's total per replica: `Security:Hubs:MaxConnections` (1,000 Proposed, 10 to 20,000, refused at start beyond; `HubSettings`), every session together beside the 8 a session may hold. `HubSessionRegistry` counts every connection, those without a session too, and refuses one past the total at its handshake (`hub_full`, aborted); `UseHubConnectionLimit` answers a negotiate 429 with Retry-After and security event 9116 (policy `hub-connections`) when the replica is full, after authorization.
  - The backtest at its bound, measured (integration `BacktestBoundTests`, test-engineer): a 64-zone rule over a day (92,160 minutes; a sensor rule 1,000 devices over 1,441 minutes), seven metrics, took 0.4 to 1.8 s and 3.1 s at the most against the 120 s default, so it keeps the default.
- Found on the way: Ariva.Api.Ingest's push set a per-request minimum rate on any protocol; Kestrel refuses one (throws) on HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, so a push over HTTP/2 failed. It now sets it over HTTP/1.x only (`SteadyUploadAttribute.RequireRate`); the request timeout ends a slow push on any protocol.
- Found by the measurement (ARV-228, Phase 3, Low): memory, not time, is a backtest's cost at the bound (146 to 397 MB allocated, NHibernate's `AliasToBean` per row, about 0.8 GB at once under the policy's two running and two waiting); the `lane_staffing` read touches the whole day's chunk; the P90 read reaches back a day where 150 minutes would do; `zone_outage` has no time index and no retention, so its reads (the sensor backtest, the daily and weekly reports) grow with the table's history (a synthetic year turned 3 ms into a 65 ms full scan).
- Docs: costly-operations (status, sections 1, 2, 6, 8, 9 rows, 13 hub row, section 15 items 2, 3, 9, 10, 12 closed, new item 14), asvs-l2 (V15.2.2 evidence, still Partly for ARV-096c to ARV-096e), log inventory (9116 `hub-connections`), wiki 04 (`Security:Hubs:MaxConnections`, the timeouts on every host), wiki 10 (4.8a `hub_full` and the 429; 4.8e a batch's 503 or 408), architecture/integration.md, remaining-work.
- Decided: the token exchange is held out of the new timeout rather than changed, for the login freeze; the hub's total is checked twice, at negotiate for a clear 429 and atomically at the handshake (a WebSocket may skip negotiate); a failed start leaves the web client's feed disconnected until the screen next sets its zones or is reopened (no timer), as wiki 04 says.
- Gotchas: read a header as the handler that uses it reads it. Counting "exactly one Authorization value" let a valid token plus an empty second value go uncounted while JWT authentication, which joins the values, still signed the caller in (review H1); the test that proves it runs on the real JWT scheme, since the test authentication handler never reads Authorization. The test authentication handler sends no bearer, so the saturation tests of those four policies now send `Authorization: Bearer test-session` (`TestAuthenticationHandler.Bearer`) as a real caller would. Kestrel's per-request minimum rate is HTTP/1.x only; setting it on HTTP/2 throws. ## 2026-10-21 ARV-096e: Run timeouts: jobs, background loops and Kafka handlers (ASVS gaps, branch story/mvp-phase1; backend, docs)

- What changed:
  - `RunBound` and `IBoundedRuns` (new, `Ariva.Infra/Resilience/RunBound.cs`): one run of a job or loop gets a token that its run timeout cancels as well as the host's stop. A run cut there is reported as `RunTimeoutException` (a `TimeoutException`), which each loop logs as a failed run before its next tick; this holds also when the cut ends in another error or the run swallows its cancellation and returns. A stop stays a cancellation. Run timeouts are bounded to two hours.
  - Every periodic loop of the hosts runs each iteration through it (`RunOnceAsync`):
    - alert evaluation 2 minutes;
    - the device heartbeat and flight feed sweeps 1 minute;
    - the desk feed 2 minutes;
    - the idempotency sweep 5 minutes;
    - the AMAN and ACRIS polls 5 minutes;
    - the malware scanner's signature check 1 minute;
    - the email round 10 minutes;
    - the validation results freeze 65 minutes, derived from its settings (20 computations and 5 minutes), so a pass within its bounds is never cut.
  - The five Cronz jobs wrap their round:
    - availability and staffing 10 minutes;
    - report deliveries and secret re-protection 30 minutes;
    - retention an hour.
  - What a cut keeps:
    - The heartbeat, flight feed and idempotency sweeps roll their unit of work back when cut (a promised unit would otherwise commit as its scope ends).
    - A pull the poll's timeout cuts is recorded on its endpoint as a failure, with the host's token, so the endpoint backs off and the screen says why.
    - The email round and the report deliveries are cut only between messages. `IEmailTransport.SendAsync` now returns an `EmailBatch` (the failures and the emails not tried); the transport finishes a message once begun and stops between messages when its token is cancelled. What the relay took is committed as sent with `CancellationToken.None`, so a cut never sends an email or a report twice.
    - The secret re-protection round is one transaction, so a cut one rewrites nothing.
  - The hosted services without a run timeout are named with their reasons in the inventory test:
    - the outbox relay, bounded by its pass time;
    - the stream engine's consume loop;
    - the live relay's Redis lease;
    - the hub session sweep, session code left as it is under the sign-in freeze;
    - the start and stop services.
  - Kafka: `HandlerTimeoutFilter` sits in every rider endpoint's pipe after the dead-letter filter and before the inbox. It gives the inbox, the unit of work and the consumer a `ConsumeContextProxy` whose token `Kafka:Consumers:HandlerTimeoutSeconds` cancels (70 s; 65 to 120, refused at start, so it stays above the archive consumers' wait for a database that refuses connections). A cut attempt fails with `HandlerTimeoutException`: rolled back, retried, and the last one dead-lettered.
  - `Database:ConnectTimeoutSeconds` (new, 15 s, Npgsql's default said explicitly; 2 to 60, refused at start by every host and the migration job), set as Npgsql's `Timeout` on the hosts' and the migration job's connections and on the validation reader's. Found by the tests: Npgsql 10 does not take the token while it opens a connection, so against a server that accepts and never answers a run ended at Npgsql's 15 s connect timeout, not its 1 s run timeout. - What changed:

  - `--list [--json]` prints one entry per image, tag and digest with every place it is pinned (12 today); `--json` is the workflow's matrix.
