    - a version tag x.y.z has a newer patch on x.y;
    - its tag (ZAP: its stable tag) names another digest;
    - TimescaleDB has a newer `pgN-tsA.B` line, since the ha image stops moving an older one.
    A newer minor line elsewhere is a note. It exits 1 when one is behind or cannot be read. The Playwright image reads `-`: Dependabot proposes its releases on the dev container, with `@playwright/test`.

  - Npgsql keeps one pool per distinct connection string, so a copy of the runtime string with other timeouts (the desk term reads) is a pool of its own, with the runtime pool's maximum unless it sets its own.
  - Unbounded, one replica of each host filled PostgreSQL's 97 non-superuser connections at the pilot rate (Stream 44, Ingest 31, Integration 15, Main 9, Cronz 2).
  - A private setter is not bound by `ConfigurationBinder`, so a derived setting cannot be set from a file or the environment.
  - A gate failed `RunTimeoutInventoryTests` for Integration's AmanPoller once: Npgsql's synchronous connection open (NHibernate's) failed at the test's 2 s connect timeout while the run's 1 s timer callback had not yet run on the busy thread pool, so `RunBound` passed the driver's error on instead of the cut. Not reproduced in three runs of the class under six `yes` loops. Fixed in its own commit before this one: `RunBound` counts an error after its timeout has passed as the cut whether or not the timer has fired (the stop is checked first), worded "ended in an error before its cancellation"; `RunBoundTests` prove both, and the stop past the timeout, with a clock whose timers never fire. Security review: round 1 FAIL (the stop guard on the new path untested; the message said cancelled), round 2 PASS.
  - Stopping a gate during its E2E step: kill the Playwright process and the E2E hosts too, not only `verify.mjs`. An orphaned run kept going, the next gate's service reset replaced its database (its hosts then failed every new connection with 28P01), and it wrote its failures into the next gate's log file (same path, so interleaved with NUL bytes): read the gate's own summary and `.verify/last.json`.
- Status: passes set; committed (signed).

## 2026-10-22 ARV-233: A push gets its answer, not a connection reset, under load (Phase 3, pulled before the pilot; branch story/mvp-phase1; Api.Common, load harness, E2E, docs)

- Cause (criterion 1), found with a reproduction outside the pilot run:
  - Ingest's push actions carry `[RequestSizeLimit(256 KB)]`, and `PushController` answers a push that declares more with 413 before reading it.
  - After the answer Kestrel drains the unread body for the next request, refuses to read past the request's limit, turns keep-alive off and closes the connection. The 413 had already gone out without `Connection: close`.
  - The pilot harness sends every device's pushes through one connection pool, so another push (the flooding device's, or a measured sensor's) could take that connection before the close reached it. It then ended in HttpRequestError ResponseEnded (an HttpIOException) or Unknown (an IOException, SocketError Shutdown): the two kinds ARV-124a's runs saw, only during the burst, when the run sends its 20 oversized pushes.
  - The reproduction (scratch, not committed): a bare Kestrel with the same limit and answer, one shared HttpClient pool, rounds of one oversized push and two normal ones. Without the action's limit Kestrel drained the body and nothing failed (the earlier idle reproduction's blind spot); with it, about one push in ten after a 413 was reset, idle and under six `yes` loops (for example 1,551 of 12,800 normal pushes and 427 of 6,400 oversized ones). Draining the body first, or `Connection: close` on the 413, gave none: 0 resets in 86,400 pushes over three loaded runs.
- What changed:
  - `SecurityHeadersMiddleware` (every host, ahead of rate limiting, in its OnStarting callback) adds `Connection: close` when `CannotBeDrained`: HTTP/1.0 or 1.1, a declared Content-Length, and a request maximum body size smaller than it (the endpoint's `[RequestSizeLimit]`, or the server's 1 MB). The server closes exactly the connections it closed before; the answer now says so, so a client opens a new one. HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 refuse such a stream alone and are untouched.
  - The pilot harness: `FloodRule` excuses no reset any more (any transport error on the flooding device is a problem, the over-count case kept in its table), a 413 without `Connection: close` is a problem, and the report has no findings section. `pilot-load.spec.ts` asserts the oversized pushes' close and no flood failure.
- Tests:
  - Unit `SecurityHeadersTests`: `CannotBeDrained` over protocol, declared length and limit (8 rows); `Post_Should_AnswerEveryPushOnTheClientsConnections_When_OversizedPushesAreRefusedUnread` on Kestrel: 8 clients x 50 rounds of an oversized push and two normal ones through one IHttpClientFactory client, expecting 400 "413 close" and 800 "202", no reset. With the header line removed it failed 3 of 3 (both client versions).
  - E2E `api/device-push.spec.ts`: the 413 carries `connection: close` and the next push answers 202.
  - The pilot load run (criterion 3), 2026-10-22 09:58Z, 4 cores: no reset in 24,935 pushes (steady 9,000, burst 6,000 and recovery 9,015 all 202; the 20 oversized pushes 413 with `Connection: close`; the flood exactly 600 accepted and 300 refused with 429 and Retry-After); the report's problems none. Its first test then failed further on, on the hall's queue minutes: Stream stopped at 133 s, out of its heap (ARV-230), before writing them (the earlier runs never reached that assertion, stopping on the reset first). Capacity, the second test, fails as before until ARV-230.
- Docs: wiki 05 (the cause and the run), wiki 09 and `docs/architecture/sensor-adapters.md` (413 with `Connection: close`; behind the ingress the header is hop-by-hop and closes the ingress's connection to Ingest; a device may see a reset instead of the 413 and must split the batch, not resend it unchanged), costly-operations (the push row and its tests), asvs-l2 (line citations moved), test-cadence and wiki 16 (resets are problems again), remaining-work.
- Security review (security-reviewer, CWE-400, with CWE-120 on the 413 path and CWE-918 for the test's client): PASS (2026-10-22), no High or Medium. Lows, applied: the flood self-test's over-count case; the ingress caveat in wiki 09 and sensor-adapters; the new tests in costly-operations; the asvs-l2 line citations; the mutation proof repeated for the IHttpClientFactory client. Low left as recorded: three reset paths remain that the check does not cover, none exploitable and each affecting only its own client: a chunked body past the limit answered before it is read; a body within the limit whose drain outlasts Kestrel's 5 s drain timeout under load (the pilot run's flood checks it: none); and a reset replacing an oversized push's own 413 on a real link (the docs tell devices). Info: no host sets Kestrel's MaxConcurrentConnections (the ingress limits connections; with V15.2.2's Partly row); the scanner does not see a terminal `app.Run` in a host. The semgrep MCP was not connected.
- Gates (2026-10-22):
  - `node scripts/verify.mjs story` with fresh E2E services, every step passed: build; reference golden; unit 7,648; the security scan and its self-test; the E2E message and artifact self-tests; ops and TLS self-tests; base images; published runtime and offline bundle self-tests; chart security with Helmfile; NuGet and three npm audits; docs; Windows paths; integration, the full suite: 765 passed, 1 skipped; E2E, the full suite (Api.Common changed): 910 passed, 1 skipped, 1 flaky; no secret in the artifacts.
  - The flaky test was ARV-233's own area: `site-configuration.spec.ts`'s 21 MB body against the 20 MB import limit ended once in `fetch failed` (write EPIPE) before its retry answered 413. A body far past the limit is refused unread and the connection closes while the client is still sending, so the client can lose the 413; measured with the reproduction and Node's fetch, 21 MB against 20 MB, 40 each: 6 EPIPE without the change, 3 with it. It predates ARV-233, and `aidx.spec.ts` and `flight-schedules.spec.ts` already accept it. The spec now does the same (413 with `connection: close`, or the connection closed), and the two touched specs passed on fresh services (`--repeat-each=3`: site configuration 3 of 3; device push 2 of 2, its third repeat stopped in its setup by the sign-in's TOTP replay guard, a single code reused within one step).
  - `node scripts/verify.mjs quick` PASS.
- Gotchas:
  - The quick gate's scanner applies to tests too: a test that needs a real client takes it from IHttpClientFactory (`AddHttpClient(name)`) rather than `new HttpClient` or a handler (SEC-020, SEC-023), and a test host answers through `app.Run` rather than a mapped endpoint without authorization (SEC-051).
  - Node's fetch exposes the `connection` response header, so an E2E test can assert it.
- Status: passes set; committed (signed).

## 2026-10-22 ARV-230: Queue engine: track positions out of the checkpointed state, so Stream fits its pod at the pilot rate (Phase 1, High; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Core queueing, load harness, E2E, docs); ARV-124a closes with its run

- Cause (from ARV-124a): the queue engine held every track position in its reorder buffer for the zone's lateness (90 s), though a position only marks an open entrant's track as seen (its hand-over deadline, F6). A hall zone of 6 T3 sensors held 82,440 positions, 18 to 23 MB of state written at every checkpoint, and Stream ran out of its pod's heap minutes into the hall.
- What changed (Ariva.Core):
  - `QueueStateEngine`: each track's samples are kept in a run (`SightingRun`): its anchor (the latest sample applied or buffered) and one pending sample (the latest within the hand-over window after the anchor), held outside the buffer until the watermark reaches it (`FlushSightings`) or a later sample past the window ends the run (the pending sample, buffered, anchors the next). A sample between two that are applied and at most the window apart changes no outcome. Samples ahead of the reference clock, without a track, behind their run's anchor, or of a track without a run when the runs are at their bound are buffered as before. `BufferedEvents` counts the pending samples; the full check and the forced advance see them (`TryOldestHeld`); runs are forgotten once the watermark is a window past their anchor (`EndRuns`, on a full step's early return too).
  - Two rules make the outcomes independent of which samples are applied: `Expire` resolves censorings and fragmentations merged in the order of their times (a censoring first at the same time), and a position sample neither moves the cursor nor narrows an interval reading's spread.
  - `QueueEngineSettings.MaxSightingRuns` (20,000 a zone, 0 to 1,000,000; security review M2) bounds the runs apart from the buffer. `CoalescePositions` (internal, default true) lets tests compare with the engine that applies every sample; `Ariva.Core` gives `InternalsVisibleTo` to Ariva.UnitTests, as Ariva.Infra does (an existing `ComparisonTests` call then bound to an internal overload and now casts to `ComparisonInput`).
  - `ZoneProcessor` offers a push's track samples in time order (stable within an instant, which is all the engine's order depends on), so a device listing a one-minute push newest first coalesces too (security review M1).
  - Snapshot: runs in `QueueEngineState.Runs` (`QueueRunState`), zone snapshot version 11 (`SightingRunsSinceVersion`; an earlier snapshot carrying runs is refused, one without them restores with its samples in the buffer). Restore checks each run (CWE-501): a track once, at most `MaxSightingRuns`, pending samples within the buffer's bound, an anchor that is plausible, not after the clock and, after the watermark, held in the buffer as that track's sample except at the instant a full step stopped inside (watermark plus one tick with the event it stopped at first in the buffer, where the anchor's sample may have been applied), and a pending sample after its anchor within the window, after the watermark and arrived before the snapshot's next sequence; `SnapshotChecks` refuses runs before version 11, implausible times and a pending sample after the zone's receive clock.
- Tests (`QueueEnginePositionRunTests`, 15):
  - Steps equal to the engine that applies every sample: random 5 Hz scenarios with pauses past the window, reordering up to 6 s, interval readings, occupancy, anonymous crossings and censoring (4 seeds); restores at random points with runs held (2 seeds).
  - Hall zone of 20 T3 sensors at 30 people and 5 Hz (3,000 positions a second) for 10 minutes: every entry and exit counted, no BufferFull, no forced advance, largest zone state 730,607 bytes (buffer 2,226, runs 838); the engine that buffers every sample refused 1,390,376 events and counted 273 of 1,198 entries (criterion 2).
  - A one-minute push listed newest first: the zone holds 120 events, identical to the in-order push; the engine offered the same samples newest first directly holds 13,500.
  - A flood of 3,000 unique 81-character tracks a second for a minute at the default bounds: runs stop at 20,000, steps equal to the engine that buffers every sample, engine state 32,035,940 bytes against 28,078,185.
  - A forced advance through a pending sample; the restore refusals (window, watermark, sequence, duplicates, bounds, anchor after the clock or not held, one tick after the watermark where no step stopped); a step split inside an instant holding an applied anchor restores and continues identically; the zone snapshot's version gate and times; the settings' range and default.
  - Mutants checked: without the sort, without the anchor check, without the split allowance and with round 1's wider allowance, each fails a test.
  - The reference golden and the locked replays are unchanged; unit 7,662 before the round 2 fixes.
- The pilot load run (criterion 3, `node scripts/verify.mjs pilot-load`, 4 cores, each host with its pod's heap limit):
  - Run 1 (12:45Z): the first test passed (Stream alive throughout, 550 MB at most, lag back 4 s after the burst, hall zone state 265 to 269 KB); the second failed on the counts, each hall zone 96 percent of its entries and 69 percent of its exits. Two harness causes, not Stream's, proven offline with the harness's own `PilotTracks.Body` through the engine at Stream's timing (251 entries and 175 of 252 exits counted, 77 duplicates, the same with and without the runs): the spec read the counts 150 s after the last push, exactly the lateness plus the push interval; and the walks run on the wall clock, so about 180 people a hall zone were already inside at the start, and their exits, whose entries Ariva never received, paired by FIFO with the earliest people other sensors held (F5's `FifoPartner`), whose own exits then counted as duplicates.
  - Harness fixes: `PilotTracks.Body` sends an exit only once its walk's entry was accepted (positions for everyone, as before), `PilotRun` records the accepted entries per device; the spec waits until every zone's stored watermark is past the harness's end (at most 5 minutes) and records it; a zone that sent no exits (the burst zones, whose walks outlast the burst) must count none.
  - Run 2 (13:19Z) passed both tests: every zone counted every crossing it was sent (each hall zone 252 or 253 entries and 78 or 79 exits; the burst zones 35 to 43 entries), every watermark past the run's end in 170 s; Stream 247 to 512 MB, 47 percent of a core on average and 115 at its peak, its queue engine back to its steady lag 2 s after the burst (peak 2,097 records), the archive in 20 s; hall zone state 208 to 211 KB (60 to 62 KB stored), burst zones 25 to 29 KB, AUH-TA 5.5 to 14 KB; connections at most 67; the request path as before (steady p95 27.8 ms, burst p95 127.4 ms, every push 202, 413 with `Connection: close`, the flood exactly 600 and 300 with 429), no problem, no reset. Recorded in wiki 05.
- ARV-124a closes with run 2: its last condition was `pilot-load` passing both tests with the catch-up recorded in wiki 05.
- Docs: formulas F6 (position samples), cwe-controls (CWE-120 and CWE-501), asvs-l2 (V15.2.2 evidence, the gap table: ARV-230 done, V15.2.2 stays Partly for ARV-089a), costly-operations item 15, wiki 04, 05, 10, 16 and 18 (migration note: snapshot version 11; a rollback to an earlier build starts the zones afresh), test-cadence, remaining-work.

Round 3 Info, applied: the test comment of the one-tick case (refused by the clock rule; the instant rule has its own case); wiki 18 and 10 say that after any fresh start (go-live, a rollback, a refused snapshot, a new profile version) exits are undercounted for about one queue dwell time (F5's pairing), filed as ARV-237 (Phase 3, Low, a domain choice for the owner); the per-device buffer share added to ARV-231's criteria; the restore of hand-over deadlines filed as ARV-238 (Phase 3, Low). The same review closes ARV-124a's CWE-120 and CWE-400 on run 2: rate and body limits held, Stream inside its pod, each zone's saved state bounded; the harness changes are test code only (no endpoint, the spec's database reads read-only with bound parameters). Info left as recorded: samples out of order across pushes still take a place each, and one flooding device can fill the buffer and the runs' bound for its zone (ARV-231, the refusals' visibility and per-device fairness); restore trusts hand-over deadlines without checking each is a sighting plus the window (before this story; a follow-up). The semgrep MCP was not connected.
- Gates (2026-10-22):
  - `node scripts/verify.mjs story` (wide: Ariva.Core queueing), fresh services, every step passed: build; reference golden; unit 7,663; the security scan and its self-test; the E2E message and artifact self-tests; ops and TLS self-tests; base images; published runtime and offline bundle self-tests; chart security; NuGet and three npm audits; docs; Windows paths; integration, the full suite: 765 passed, 1 skipped; E2E, the full suite: 911 passed, 1 skipped; no secret in the artifacts.
  - Its first run failed on the disk, not the change: the session's disk allowance ran out (PostgreSQL 53100, then Kafka exited, then the hosts' readiness), 170 integration tests and 12 E2E tests failing on it. The E2E host logs of this session's earlier runs (`Platform/Testing/Ariva.E2E/logs`, gitignored, 2.4 GB) were compressed with gzip (reversible; 253 MB after) and the scratch probes' build output removed: 4.5 GB free, and the second run passed.

- Gotchas:

  - A step split inside an instant leaves the watermark one tick before it with part of the instant applied: any restore check of "after the watermark means still held" needs that one-tick exception, tied to the event the step stopped at.

## 2026-10-22 ARV-231: Queue engine refusals visible: buffer full, forced advances, late and invalid events (Phase 1, Medium; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Core queueing, Ariva.Infra streaming, chart monitoring, docs)

- Cause (from ARV-124a): each step of the queue engine counted what it refused or applied early (`QueueRejections`), but only the late events reached anything; a zone at its buffer's bound lost crossings without a log line, a metric or a flag on its minutes, and one flooding device could fill the buffer for every device of its zone (added to the story by ARV-230's security review).
- What changed:
  - Engine: `Offer(input, reference, device)`; each held event (buffered, or a run's pending sample) counts for its device (an anonymous event's device from the batch, a tracked one's from its key). A device holds at most its share of the buffer: the bound over the devices sharing it (those holding events with the offering one, `ZoneDevices`, which the zone processor sets from its device liveness, and at least two, so one device never holds more than half), at least `DeviceShareFloor` (10,000, 1 to 1,000,000). The tenth of the buffer for events ahead of the clock stays the zone's (a per-device share of it cost a sensor within Ingest's clock tolerance most of its crossings: review M3; ARV-239 filed). Past its share, or with the buffer full, forced advances apply events that were due anyway while that frees room; otherwise the event is refused, `DeviceShareFull` for a device past its share, `BufferFull` for the buffer. `QueueRejections` gains `DeviceShareFull`, `FullBufferMinutes` (the minutes of events refused for a full buffer or share and those a forced advance processed early, at most two days a step) and `Counts()`.
  - Zone processor: passes the batch's device; carries the refusals by kind in `ZoneOutputs.Refusals` (not rows, not in the replay ledger; subtracted on acknowledge); marks a live minute that a full buffer touched `LengthDegraded` and its nowcast input degraded.
  - Snapshot: zone version 12 (`BufferSharesSinceVersion`): an anonymous buffered event's device (a tracked one's is its key's), a run's pending device when its key does not name it, the twelfth counter and the full-buffer minutes (engine and zone, at most two days, whole minutes); a device must be a device code; an earlier version carrying any of these is refused, and a version 11 snapshot restores with its tracked events counted for their devices. Tests downgrade through `WrittenBefore12`.
  - Stream: after a checkpoint commits, each zone's refusals go to the counter `ariva.stream.queue_refused` (meter `Ariva.Stream`, tags kind and site) and to a warning per zone and kind at most once a minute (`RefusalWarnings`: zone, kind and count only).
  - Chart: the SigNoz rule `queueRefused` (critical, any `BufferFull` or `DeviceShareFull` in 5 minutes; `monitoring.alerts.queueRefused.kinds`, validated against the twelve kinds).
- Tests:
  - `QueueEngineRefusalTests` (11): one of seven devices flooding 2,000 positions a second for five minutes: no BufferFull, every other device's entry and exit counted, where without shares the flood cost the zone its crossings; a device flooding a quiet zone for a minute before six sensors push (default bounds): no BufferFull, every crossing counted; restores with pending samples while shares bind, the steps equal the engine's that kept going; a sensor 500 ms fast (within Ingest's tolerance) in a seven-device zone keeps every crossing; the full-buffer minutes; twin zones (only the zone with a refusal marks that minute); restore during a flood; the version gate and the device-code refusal; the settings' range; the warning limiter's minute; the counter by kind and site. The round 1 tests of M1 and M2 failed before their fixes.
  - Changed: ARV-230's flood test (one device holds at most half the buffer: 18.0 MB of engine state against 14.0 MB for the engine that buffers every sample), seven version downgrade tests, the version 12 expectation, `MetricTagTests` drives the new counter, `chart-security.mjs` (an injection-like kind, an empty kind, a non-list; 322 PASS).
- Docs: wiki 10 section 4.22 (kinds, meaning, action) and the watch table, wiki 05, wiki 18 (migration note: version 12, the new rule to import, the share rule and a single-device zone's half-buffer cap), formulas (the Degraded causes), asvs-l2 (V16.3.4 Met again: 158 met, 78 percent; V15.2.2's evidence and the residual; the gap table), cwe-controls (CWE-120 and CWE-400), costly-operations item 15, remaining-work.
- Security review (security-reviewer, CWE-400, CWE-778, CWE-501): round 1 FAIL (M1 a device flooding a quiet zone took the whole buffer; M2 a restore dropped pending samples from their device's count; L1 the floor's residual undocumented; L2 the ahead tenth shared by every device), fixed: M1 by dividing by the zone's devices and at least two, with a device past its share given room from due events first (a device sending due events in bulk is not refused; `Work_Should_StayLinear` caught a cap without it), M2 by counting the derived device, L1 in the docs, L2 by a per-device share of the ahead tenth; round 2 FAIL (M3: that ahead share refused a sensor within Ingest's 500 ms clock tolerance, 60 to 162 of 300 crossings counted at 500 to 100 ms fast), fixed by dropping it (the tenth stays the zone's, as before) and filing ARV-239 for the uncoalesced ahead samples; round 3 PASS (2026-10-22), probes: an honest sensor 100 to 500 ms fast counts 300 of 300, a lone flooder then six sensors 1,446 of 1,446, restore counts equal. Residuals as documented: ten or more devices at the floor fill the buffer together; the ahead tenth is the zone's (ARV-239); a flooder's forced advances mark the zone's minutes degraded during its flood; samples out of order across pushes take a place each, within their device's share. The semgrep MCP was not connected.
- Gates (2026-10-22): story gate `node scripts/verify.mjs story` (32 changed files; wide through the queue engine, so the full suites), 18:40 to 19:41 UTC on b9e90aa with the ARV-231 changes uncommitted, on fresh services, detached, with the b9e90aa checkpoint's mutation run beside it until 19:27: PASS, exit 0: unit 7,674 of 7,674, integration 765 passed and 1 skipped of 766, E2E 911 passed and 1 skipped, none flaky, the log scan of 5 host logs (128,190 lines) clean, no secret in the test artifacts; it notes 4 stories since the last checkpoint. `node scripts/verify.mjs quick` (the security scan of the changed files and the docs rules) PASS after this entry.
- Gotchas:
  - A share that only binds against devices currently holding events lets the first flooder of a quiet zone take everything: divide by the zone's known devices and at least two.
  - Refusing a device past its share without a forced advance turns a device's bulk catch-up of due events into data loss; give it room from due events first, as for a full buffer.
  - Writing a derivable field (a tracked event's device) into every buffered event cost 1.9 MB at the bound: write it only when the key does not name it.
- Status: passes set; committed (signed).

- Gates (2026-10-23): `node scripts/verify.mjs e2e --specs tests/functional/advertising-media.spec.ts` on fresh services: with the screen as it was, FAIL on both tries at the spec's first test (the library missing, the same race; the new test not reached in the serial group); with the fix, PASS, 7 of 7, the new test included. `node scripts/verify.mjs web` PASS (svelte-check, lint, build). The svelte MCP (autofixer) was not reachable from this session. The full suites run in ARV-239's story gate. No security-relevant change (no input, output or authorization changes; the server still refuses what a user may not see).

## 2026-10-22 ARV-239: Queue engine: position samples ahead of the receive clock coalesced, so fast sensors within the clock tolerance never fill the ahead tenth (Phase 1, Medium; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Core queueing, docs)

- Cause (ARV-231's security review, M3): Ingest leaves a device clock within 500 ms uncorrected, so a T3 sensor a little fast stamps the latest samples of each push after its receive time. ARV-230 coalesced only samples that were not ahead of the reference clock, so each of those took a place of the tenth of the buffer kept for events ahead of the clock for about the lateness; a few such sensors filled the tenth and the zone refused every event ahead of the clock, crossings and readings included. Before this story, the hall zone of 20 T3 sensors 500 ms fast (below) counted 766 of 1,199 entries and 359 of 599 exits and refused 651,320 events for a full buffer.
- What changed (Ariva.Core):
  - `QueueStateEngine`: samples ahead of the reference clock are coalesced in their track's run like the others. A place one of them takes (an anchor in the buffer, or the pending sample, `SightingRun.PendingAhead`) is one of the ahead tenth, counted until it is applied (a pending sample keeps its mark when the buffer takes it); a sample that replaces a pending sample which was not ahead takes one, one that replaces a pending sample ahead of the clock takes none (`TakesAheadPlace`). Such a sample moves the clock only to its reference, as before, so the watermark never passes the receive clock (ARV-148).
  - Each device holds at most its share of the ahead tenth (`AheadShareOf`: the tenth over the devices sharing the buffer, as ARV-231's share, never below a tenth of `DeviceShareFloor` and one place; 1,000 at the defaults). The tenth is freed as the watermark reaches its events, and the engine runs no forced advance to make room in it: past its share the event is refused (`DeviceShareFull`), with the tenth full (`BufferFull`), checked before any forced advance as before. A per-device share of the tenth hurt fast sensors in ARV-231 only because their samples were not coalesced: now such a sensor holds a few places a track.
  - Snapshot: zone version 13 (`AheadRunsSinceVersion`): `QueueRunState.PendingAhead` (written only when true). Restore (CWE-501): a run's anchor at most `MaxAhead` after the engine's clock (in a quiet zone the watermark follows the receive clock, so an applied anchor may be after the clock: security review M1), held in the buffer when not yet applied (as before, and then as an event ahead of the clock, which the events' check already demands); a pending sample marked ahead at most `MaxAhead` after the clock (one not marked, as before, never after it); every buffered event ahead of the clock at most `MaxAhead` after it, when the snapshot has a clock, and no more events ahead of the clock than the tenth (review L1); the places ahead of the clock counted per device; `SnapshotChecks` lets a pending sample marked ahead be after the zone's receive clock (the engine bounds it) and refuses, before version 13, a pending sample marked ahead or a run anchored after the engine's clock. A version 12 snapshot restores as it is.
- Tests (`QueueEngineAheadRunTests`, 11 tests, 14 cases):
  - The hall zone of ARV-230 (20 T3 sensors, 30 people each, 5 Hz, 10 minutes, walks starting on each sample of a second so crossings are ahead too) with every sensor 500 ms fast: 721,320 events ahead of the clock, every entry (1,199) and exit (599) counted, no event refused, late, applied early or invalid, at most 3,040 events held (12,862 before) (criterion 1). It failed before the change (above).
  - Steps equal to the engine that applies every sample with device clocks 600 and 250 ms fast and 100 ms slow, pushes offered within 600 ms (3 seeds; more than 10,000 events ahead, runs holding pending samples ahead); restores at random points with runs ahead of the clock continue identically (2 seeds), with two quiet minutes in which the watermark follows the receive clock past runs anchored after the event clock and a restore 80 seconds in.
  - A device four minutes ahead (within `MaxAhead`) flooding 3,000 unique tracks a second beside six sensors 500 ms fast: refused past its share alone, every fast sensor's entry and exit counted, at most 1,428 places ahead held by it, the watermark never past the receive clock; with the share turned off (floor at the bound) it fills the tenth and the zone loses crossings (criterion 1's second half).
  - The share's floor and bounds (half the tenth for a lone device, a tenth of the floor, never below one); a replaced pending sample counted once in the full tenth and after a restore; the restore refusals (a pending sample past `MaxAhead`, one after the clock not marked ahead, an event after the clock not held as ahead, an anchor after the clock not held; an applied anchor or a buffered event further after the clock than `MaxAhead`, more events ahead of the clock than the tenth); a quiet zone's run whose applied anchor is after the clock restores and continues identically, in the engine and through the zone processor's idle ticks and `ZoneProcessor.Restore` (review M1: the first version refused it); the zone snapshot's version gate.
  - Changed: `QueueStateEngineTests`' future flood names a track per sample (samples of one track at one instant are one reading, now coalesced), the version 13 expectations, `SnapshotVersions.WrittenBefore13`.
  - Hand mutants of the new rules, each killed by a test (the queueing tests, 658 then): ahead samples not coalesced (12 tests), no per-device share of the tenth, the share's floor without one place, a replaced pending sample ahead not released, a buffered pending sample losing its mark, a restored pending sample not counted, a replaced pending sample ahead taking a place, a pending sample past `MaxAhead` accepted, the version 13 gate removed, a pending sample ahead counted on the clock at restore, a new pending sample never marked ahead.
- The golden replay and the locked replays are unchanged (criterion 2: the story gate's golden check and the replay tests).
- Docs: formulas F6 (position samples ahead of the clock) and the engine's bounds, wiki 10 section 4.22 (`BufferFull` and `DeviceShareFull` rows), wiki 18 (migration note: zone snapshot version 13, the share of the ahead tenth), cwe-controls (the CWE-501 row's restore checks and the CWE-120 row's residual), asvs-l2 (V15.2.2 residual) and costly-operations item 15, remaining-work; the residuals name ARV-240.
- Security review (security-reviewer, CWE-400, CWE-501, CWE-120): round 1 FAIL (2026-10-22):
  - M1: the new restore check refused a snapshot the engine writes. In a quiet zone the idle ticks move the watermark from the receive clock while the event clock moves only with events, so a run anchored by a sample ahead of the clock has that sample applied and stays after the clock for a hand-over window; a checkpoint then could not be restored, and the zone started afresh (open entrants, liveness, de-duplication and bins lost). My test of a "forged" state was exactly that state. Fixed: an anchor is at most `MaxAhead` after the clock, and held in the buffer only when not yet applied (ARV-230's rule); the separate "held as ahead" rule was implied by the events' check and is gone. Tests: the engine and the zone processor restore such a state and continue identically; the random restores include quiet minutes.
  - L1: restore bounded the pending samples ahead of the clock but not the buffered events ahead of it nor their number. Fixed: each at most `MaxAhead` after the clock (when the snapshot has one) and no more than the tenth, tested.
  - L2: the runs are one pool a zone, so a device flooding unique tracks can use it up, and a fast sensor's new tracks then take a place of the tenth a sample until its share (no worse than before). Recorded as a residual (cwe-controls, asvs-l2, costly-operations, wiki 10) and filed as ARV-240 (Phase 3, Low).
  - Info: "never due" corrected (the tenth is freed only as the watermark reaches its events, never by a forced advance); wiki 10's `BufferFull` action names the runs' `pendingAhead` too; this entry named the CWE rows wrongly. I4 to I7 confirmed the removed second check, the counts on every path, the clock rule and the shares.
  - Mutants of the round 1 fixes, each killed: the first version's anchor check back (seven tests, the two quiet-zone tests among them), the anchor's `MaxAhead` bound removed, the buffered events' bound removed, the tenth's bound removed.
  - Round 2 PASS (2026-10-22): M1 and L1 fixed and tested (the reviewer confirmed that an unapplied anchor after the clock held in the buffer is held as ahead of it, with a clock or without one, and that no new rule refuses a state the engine writes: the sites tune only Lateness and PushInterval, never MaxAhead or the buffer's bound), L2 recorded and filed, the Info items done. New Low L3: a snapshot that leaves out the engine's clock (any before version 9, or a forged one) skips the bound on buffered events ahead of the clock, so up to the tenth of them, a day ahead, could hold the tenth full for a day (the tenth's own bound still applies; the clock derived from such a snapshot is older than ARV-239). Low, so Phase 3 by the owner's rule: added to ARV-238 (Phase 3, the queue engine's restore checks): refuse a snapshot from version 9 on without the engine's clock; cwe-controls says "when the snapshot has the engine's clock" and names ARV-238. Wording done as the reviewer suggested (the version 13 summary covers an applied anchor; "no forced advance to make room in it"). All 660 queueing tests pass.
- Gates (2026-10-22 and 23):
  - Story gate, first run (22:36 UTC, before the security review): stopped by the lead in its unit step to fix review M1.
  - Story gate, second run (23:05 to 00:18 UTC, 17 changed files, wide through the queue engine, so the full suites; the ae28447 checkpoint's Stryker run beside it): FAIL, exit 1, on E2E only: unit 7,688 of 7,688, integration 765 passed and 1 skipped of 766, E2E 907 passed, 1 skipped, 1 flaky and 1 failed, both in `advertising-media.spec.ts` (the advertisement library missing). Not this story's: a race on the Passenger displays screen, root-caused in Main's log and fixed apart in 7a6ba97 (its own entry above), with ARV-241 filed for seven other screens.
  - Story gate, third run (00:32 to 03:27 UTC, on 7a6ba97 with these changes and the round 2 wording uncommitted, fresh services, Stryker beside it): FAIL, exit 1, on the unit step only, which the lead ended: `RunTimeoutInventoryTests.Loop_Should_EndItsRunAtTheRunTimeout_When_ItsDatabaseOrScannerStalls` (ARV-096e) hung in the unit step (from 00:37) for about two hours at load 16, two stacks minutes apart the same: the AMAN pull loop's run opening its database connection with Npgsql's synchronous open, blocked in a socket read during authentication against the test's silent server, which the run bound cannot cut. Not this story's; filed as ARV-242 (Medium, before the pilot). The test host was killed at 02:36 (6,589 unit tests had passed, the rest did not run); every other step PASS: integration 765 passed and 1 skipped of 766, E2E 912 passed and 1 skipped, none flaky (the displays race test included), the log scan of 5 host logs (112,669 lines) clean, no secret in the test artifacts.
  - `node scripts/verify.mjs backend` for the unit step the third run lost (03:28 to 03:44 UTC, same tree, ARV-242 filed in the backlog): PASS, exit 0: unit 7,688 of 7,688, the security scan 2,242 files with 0 errors. `node scripts/verify.mjs quick` PASS after this entry.
- Gotchas:
  - A per-device share of a pool fails honest devices when their events are not coalesced: fix the coalescing first, then the share costs them nothing.
  - A check repeated after the forced advances can only refuse less: they release places and the devices sharing the buffer only fall. A second ahead check there was dead code, removed.
  - The engine's watermark is not bounded by its event clock: a quiet zone's ticks move it from the receive clock. A restore check that compares a held time with the event clock must allow what the watermark has already applied.
  - An engine whose cursor never moved writes it without a DateTime kind, and a restored one as UTC: compare captures with the cursor aligned.
- Status: passes set; committed (signed).

## 2026-10-23 ARV-226: No certificate downloads while a chain is built: Redis, and the collectors without a site CA (ASVS gaps, Medium; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Infra, Ariva.ServiceDefaults, Ariva.Api.Common logging, Ariva.Api.Ingest MQTT, docs)

- Cause (ARV-200's reviews, M1 follow-up and L4): a TLS chain built with the platform's default policy downloads a missing intermediate from the address the peer's certificate names, and fetches revocation data, during the handshake, before the peer is authenticated (CWE-918). Measured on Linux with a loopback server that sends its leaf alone and names a loopback issuer site: StackExchange.Redis's own handshake, Npgsql's (four requests in one open: Npgsql gives the handshake no chain policy), MailKit's SMTP client and a server handshake asking for a client certificate with Kestrel's defaults all fetched it; the collectors' default clients did too; librdkafka (OpenSSL) fetched nothing.
- What changed:
  - Redis (`RedisConnection.cs`): `RedisSettings.Options()` sets `ConfigurationOptions.SslClientAuthenticationOptions` (`Handshake`): StackExchange.Redis then takes Ariva's options for the whole handshake, in place of its own TLS settings (its validation event and its revocation check included): a chain policy with no download and no revocation, server authentication usage required, the pinned CAs as custom root trust (then `IsIssuedByPinnedCa` judges, as before) or the system's CAs when none is named, the host name checked (`SslHost` when set). The old `CertificateValidation` registration is gone (with the handshake options both would be given to SslStream). `IsIssuedByPinnedCa` also disables downloads.
  - PostgreSQL: every connection is made by `PostgresConnections.Create` (22 call sites in Ariva.Infra and Ariva.Di) or hardened by it (`NHibernatePostgresClientDriver.CreateConnection`), which sets `NpgsqlConnection.SslClientAuthenticationOptionsCallback`; Npgsql's own check (VerifyFull against `Database:RootCertificate`) still decides the trust, on the same policy. `NHibernateSessionFactoryProvider` refuses a configured driver or provider other than Ariva's (review L4).
  - `CertificateDownloads.Refuse` (Ariva.Infra/Settings): one policy for client and server handshakes (no download, no revocation), used by PostgreSQL, SMTP and MQTT.
  - SMTP (review M3): `SmtpRelayClient` overrides MailKit's protected virtual `GetSslClientAuthenticationOptions` (MailKit 4.18.1; confirmed by reflection) and `MailKitTransport` turns MailKit's online revocation check off; MailKit's own check of the relay's certificate is kept.
  - MQTT (review M2): the listener's TLS options set `CheckCertificateRevocation = false` and give every handshake, on every OS, the policy for the client certificate's chain, which SslStream builds before any device is known (the pin still decides alone, ARV-022).
  - Collectors without a site CA: the exporters' client (`ServiceDefaultsExtensions`), the Loki sink's client and the OTLP log sink's handler (`ArivaLogging`, `CollectorClients`) are pinned through the factory whenever the collector is reached over https (`CollectorTrust.Pin` with no roots: the image's public CAs, no download); `CollectorTrust.PublicHandler` was dropped for factory clients (SEC-020, SEC-023). A logger built without the host's collector clients for an https collector refuses to build, as with a CA file.
- Tests: `CertificateDownloadTests` (Redis: no download in Ariva's handshake or through ConnectionMultiplexer, StackExchange.Redis's own as the control; pinned CA accepted and another refused; system CAs without downloading; PostgreSQL: no download with Npgsql's own as the control, a server the root issued still completes, the NHibernate driver's and Ariva's connections both take the policy, a source scan for any other connection path (a regular expression: constructed, target-typed, data source, factories), the NHibernate refusal; Kafka: librdkafka fetches nothing; SMTP through `MailKitTransport`, MailKit's own client as the control); `MqttTransportTests.Listener_Should_DownloadNoCertificate_When_ADeviceCertificateLeavesOutItsIntermediate` (the client presents its certificate through an offline context, so any request is the server's; it failed with the fix commented out) and the TLS options' policy; `CollectorTrustTests` (64 cases: public-CA clients, Loki, OTLP logs and traces over gRPC and http/protobuf download nothing; a logger without the pinned clients refuses an https collector); `ProductionTransportTests` (the Redis checks read the handshake options' callback; the live hub's backplane takes the no-download policy); `LogShippingTests` and the production transport logging cases build the logger as the host does (`HostLogger` fixture). 460 related cases pass.
- Docs: asvs-l2 V12.3.2 (Met, evidence), V12.3.4 (Partly for its other items; the Redis download item removed) and the ARV-226 row (Done); crypto-inventory A14 (MQTT client certificate chains) and A15 (PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, SMTP, the collectors; the ARV-226 open item closed); cwe-controls CWE-918; wiki 04 (database and Redis certificates, the collectors and the SMTP relay send their intermediates; the openssl check also for a collector on a public CA); remaining-work (ASVS 27 of 43).
- Operational note: no host downloads an intermediate any more, so PostgreSQL, Redis, the SMTP relay and every https collector (on a public CA too) must send theirs in the handshake; one that sends its own certificate alone is refused. Redis's handshake used to check revocation online (StackExchange.Redis's default) and now checks none, as K32 and A15 document for every connection (review Info 7).
- Security review round 1: FAIL. M1 the docs claimed every chain a host builds, while SMTP and the MQTT listener still downloaded; M2 the MQTT listener built device certificate chains with downloads and online revocation, before authentication; M3 MailKit checked revocation online and gave SslStream no chain policy; L4 a configured NHibernate driver could skip the hardening; L5 the source scan matched one spelling; Info 6 the backplane test checked only the callback; Info 7 Redis's revocation change to record. All fixed here (L4 and L5 too, being small and needed for the claim).
- Security review round 2: PASS (the scan 2,247 files, 0 errors; the 12 warnings all older and outside the change). Its three leftovers done too: Low, the SMTP test covered TLS on connect only, so it is now a theory with STARTTLS (the default) through a stub that answers up to STARTTLS; Info, the source scan also matches an initializer without parentheses; Info, a comment says the NHibernate check may follow the build because building opens no connection (keyword quoting off).
- Gates:
  - Story gate, first run (from 04:49 UTC, before security review round 1 came back): stopped by the lead in its unit step to fix the review's findings.
  - Story gate, second run (to 06:18 UTC; 48 changed files, wide through Ariva.Infra, so the full suites): FAIL, exit 1, on integration and E2E only, both from a full disk (2.5 GB free at the start): integration 696 passed, 69 failed and 1 skipped of 766, every failure after the suite's PostgreSQL container restarted 20 minutes in (connection refused, then "not yet accepting connections"); E2E 891 passed, 12 failed, 1 flaky, 8 did not run, after the E2E stack's Kafka broker failed to append to its log directory at 05:49. Every other step PASS: unit 7,708 of 7,708, the security scan, chart security, the audits, docs.
  - Disk freed (the build output of the stale mutation worktree the killed checkpoint left, the E2E host logs gzipped): 4.3 GB free.
  - `node scripts/verify.mjs integration` (06:22 to 06:46 UTC, same tree): PASS, exit 0: 765 passed and 1 skipped of 766. Free disk fell to 1.5 GB during it (a trace a minute), so the second run's 2.5 GB could not hold it.
  - `node scripts/verify.mjs e2e` (06:47 to 07:10 UTC, fresh services): PASS, exit 0: 912 passed and 1 skipped, none flaky; no secret in the test artifacts. `node scripts/verify.mjs quick` PASS after this entry.
- Gotchas:
  - StackExchange.Redis's `SslClientAuthenticationOptions` replaces every TLS setting of its own, the `CertificateValidation` event included: give the handshake options the validation callback, and do not register the event beside them.
  - Npgsql gives its handshake no chain policy; `SslClientAuthenticationOptionsCallback` gives it one without touching Npgsql's own VerifyFull check.
  - MailKit's `GetSslClientAuthenticationOptions` is protected virtual (4.18.1): a subclass sets the chain policy for STARTTLS and TLS on connect alike.
  - A TLS client that presents a certificate builds that certificate's chain to send its intermediates, and may download for it: a test of the server side presents through an offline `SslStreamCertificateContext`, or the client's own request passes for the server's.
  - The integration suite takes about 3 GB of disk while it runs; start a story gate or a checkpoint with 4 GB free at least.
- Status: passes set; committed (signed).

## 2026-10-23 ARV-241: Screens with a site selector keep the chosen site when an earlier site's load answers last (Phase 1, Medium; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Web, E2E)

- Cause (ARV-239's story gate, the Passenger displays screen fixed in 7a6ba97): a screen loads its first site (DMO) as it opens; choosing another site before that load answered let the late answer replace the chosen site's data. The server's site scope already refuses what a user may not see, so nothing crossed a boundary; the risk was one site's figures, rows or actions shown under another site's name.
- Found on reading the seven screens: Live operations, Zones and Immigration already compared the site of each answer with the site shown (left as they are: after A, B, A an older answer of A may land, which is still A's); Devices, Display instructions, Alert rules and Validation capture had no guard.
- What changed (`routes/(modules)`):
  - Devices, Display instructions, Alert rules, Validation capture: a load number per site load (`generation`), as the displays screen; a load a later one superseded drops its answers, and the refreshes after an action keep the current number, so they drop theirs too after a site change.
  - On a site change the previous site's rows and their actions leave the screen at once: Devices clears its list, health, zones, levels, plans and plan (and the issued credential, before any request); Display instructions its list, displays and zones; Alert rules its rules and zones (only when the site changes: a reload after a save keeps its rows until the answer); Validation capture its campaigns (security review round 1, M3: an observer could pick the previous site's campaign while the next site loaded).
  - Devices: a credential is shown only under the site it was issued at (`reveal`): a registration or a new credential that answers after another site was chosen is not shown, and a warning says to issue it again from its own site (new message `devices.messages.issuedElsewhere`, English and Arabic); `registered` and `changed` set no level or selection of another site (review M1 and round 2 L1).
  - Display instructions: a reorder that answers after another site was chosen changes nothing (review M2).
  - Zones: the plans reloaded after an upload are kept only while the same site is shown (`reloadPlans`).
- Tests (Playwright functional; each holds a request with `page.route` and checks the chosen site after the late answer):
  - New `site-switch.spec.ts`: Live operations, Devices, Zones, Display instructions (first load and a late reorder, answered by the test so DMO's order does not change), Alert rules, Immigration, switching DMO to E2SW, an empty site the seed makes.
  - `devices.spec.ts`: a registration held and answered by the test with a DMO device after E2SW was chosen shows no credential (never sent: no step-up, no device made; the held answer carries no credential shape).
  - `validation-capture.spec.ts`: a held first list (E2EO, with a running campaign) answered after E2SW was chosen; and no E2EO campaign offered while E2SW's list is held.
  - New E2E accounts: `switchAdmin` (SystemAdministrator, every site, password only, like `webAdmin`) and `webSwitchObserver` (ValidationObserver, E2EO and E2SW; the vm-local seed creates E2SW for it).
  - Each first-load test failed with its guard removed (the three existing guards removed too) and passes with it. The first Devices test passed without the guard twice: the E2E database has no device at DMO, so DMO's late list looked like an empty site's, and then the test released DMO's answer before E2SW's load had ended; it now holds DMO's levels and waits for E2SW's answer, and every test waits for the chosen site's answer before releasing.
- Security review round 1: FAIL. M1 Devices showed a credential whose registration or rotation answered after the site changed under the new site; M2 a late reorder replaced the new site's slides; M3 the previous site's campaigns stayed clickable while the next site loaded; L4 the previous site's rows stayed with their actions while the next site loaded; L5 no test for the reload paths; Info: a purpose comment for `switchAdmin`. All fixed here with tests (Zones' plan reload has none: it needs an upload, and its guard is the screen's own site comparison, which the reviewer accepted).
- Security review round 2: PASS (scan 11 files, 0 errors). Its two Lows done too: `changed` ignores a panel action of another site, and Devices clears its levels, level, plans and plan on a site change.
- Docs: remaining-work (Phase 1 75 of 88). No wiki page describes the site selectors' loading.
- Flake seen (recorded on ARV-164): validation-capture.spec.ts 'the tablet layout works on touch in English and Arabic (800x1280)' failed once and passed on its retry (Enter then Space on the tally button counted one press), with the checkpoint's Stryker run beside it; not this story's code (after a campaign is chosen).
- Gates:
  - The story's three specs alone, before review round 2: 37 passed, 1 flaky (the tablet layout one below).
  - Story gate (09:22 to 10:34 UTC; 15 changed files, wide through the E2E accounts, so the full suites; the checkpoint's Stryker run beside it; two Docker images the repository no longer uses removed first, with the owner's approval, for disk): PASS, exit 0: unit 7,708 of 7,708, integration 765 passed and 1 skipped of 766, web check, lint and build, E2E 921 passed, 1 skipped and 1 flaky (below), no secret in the test artifacts, every other step PASS. Free disk fell to 768 MB during the integration step. `node scripts/verify.mjs quick` PASS after this entry.
  - Flaky in the gate (recorded on ARV-164 with the tablet layout one): validation-capture.spec.ts 'the desk log never places a minute without Ariva's clock ...' stored no desk minute on its first try (expected OD01 Serving for one bin) and passed on its retry; the desk log after a campaign is chosen, not this story's code.
- Gotchas:
  - A late-answer test proves nothing unless the chosen site's own load has answered before the first site's answer is released: otherwise the chosen site's answer lands last and a screen without a guard passes. Wait for the chosen site's response, then release.
  - A first site with nothing to show (no device at DMO in the E2E database) makes its late answer look like the empty site's: hold a request whose answer differs (DMO's levels).
  - Clearing a screen's rows on every reload makes a save flash an empty list: clear them only when the site changes (the site of the rows shown).

## 2026-10-23 ARV-242: A run ends at its run timeout while a database connection opens: no synchronous open the run cannot cut (ASVS gaps, Medium; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Core, Ariva.Infra, docs)

- Root cause, confirmed (the hypothesis of ARV-239's entry): NHibernate's `ISession.BeginTransaction` opened the session's connection with Npgsql's synchronous `Open()`, and Npgsql 10.0.0 bounds each synchronous read by the socket's receive timeout, which it sets from the connection timeout left: `NpgsqlTimeout.CheckAndApply` gives the read buffer the time left (`CheckAndGetTimeLeft`, positive below a millisecond), and the read buffer's `Timeout` setter writes `(int)value.TotalMilliseconds` to `Socket.ReceiveTimeout`, so less than a millisecond left becomes 0, which a socket takes as no timeout. On a loaded machine the startup reached its first read with that little left, and the read against the test's silent server never ended (the path in ARV-239's stacks: AmanPoller, SvcAmanPull.ClaimDueAsync, SvcDb.InTransactionAsync, NHibernateStorageProvider.BeginTransaction, DriverConnectionProvider, NpgsqlConnection.Open).
- Measured (a scratch program, Npgsql 10.0.0, a TCP server that accepts and never answers): `OpenAsync` does not take a token cancelled while the server holds the startup (it waits the whole `Timeout`, pooled or not: 60.1 s for a 1 s token), returns at once for a token already cancelled (no connection), and the synchronous `Open` waits the `Timeout`. So the run's token alone cannot end a stalled open; the asynchronous open's own timer always does.
- What changed:
  - `IStorageProvider.BeginTransaction` became `BeginTransactionAsync(isolation, ct)`: `NHibernateStorageProvider` opens the session's connection first through NHibernate's connection manager (`GetConnectionAsync`, the hardened driver, so ARV-226's handshake policy holds), then begins on it. Every caller moved (SvcDb.InTransactionAsync now takes the token, the unit of work's commit, the inbox, alert emails, alert evaluation, report deliveries, the site configuration export, the seeds, break-glass accounts, the development seed), and the synchronous begin is gone from the abstraction.
  - The Data Protection key store (`PostgresXmlRepository`, a synchronous interface reached by a bounded run when it unprotects a stored secret) waits on Npgsql's asynchronous open, reader and command (security review M1).
  - `RunBound.MinRunTimeout` (60 s, the longest connection timeout a host may set): every loop's and job's run timeout is at least it (the smallest declared is 1 minute; none is configurable), so a run whose first step is the open fails within its timeout; any run ends at most one connection timeout past its own (an open that starts late runs out its timeout; the opens after the cut see the cancelled token and open nothing).
- Tests:
  - `TransactionOpenTests`: a cancelled token opens no connection (it failed with the old synchronous begin: 5 s, then NHibernate's TransactionException); a stalled open ends at the connection timeout, with the synchronous begin as the control on a thread of its own, waited on with a bound; the Data Protection key read ends at the connection timeout; the abstraction has no synchronous begin.
  - `SynchronousDatabaseCallTests` (new, Architecture): a source scan of the Platform's production code refuses any synchronous open, command, transaction begin or NHibernate `List`/`UniqueResult` (only `NHibernateStorageProvider`, with its reason), with cases that prove the pattern finds them and passes the asynchronous calls.
  - `RunTimeoutInventoryTests`: every loop's and job's run timeout at least `MinRunTimeout`; the stalled database tests kept (a 2 s connection timeout, so a run ends by its timeout or the connection timeout). Run five rounds in a row beside four CPU hogs and the checkpoint's Stryker run (load 6 to 11 on 4 cores): 25 of 25 each round, none past its bound.
  - Unit and integration fakes and call sites moved to the asynchronous begin.
- Docs: asvs-l2 V15.2.2 (the evidence, and the false claim that a stalled open always ended at the connection timeout corrected) and an ARV-242 row; costly-operations (opening a connection); wiki 04 (`Database:ConnectTimeoutSeconds`); remaining-work (ASVS 28 of 43).

- Security review round 2: PASS (scan 2,250 files, 0 errors). Its two Lows done here: L1 NHibernate's lazy collection loads open synchronously outside a transaction, reached by the validation results freeze (a bounded run): `SvcValidationResults.CampaignByIdAsync` loads the campaign's zones, lines and desks asynchronously (`NHibernateUtil.InitializeAsync`), the docs say "every connection the code opens" and name the lazy loads as the remaining exception, filed as ARV-243 (Phase 3, Low); L2 the scan's allowance covered the whole storage provider file: it now excuses only its one `.BeginTransaction(`. The scan's summary states its scope (Info).
- Gotchas:

  - The synchronous path's "no timeout" comes from a millisecond conversion: a positive time below a millisecond cast to an int socket timeout is 0, and a socket takes 0 as infinite.

## 2026-10-23 Fix: the checkpoint's mutation step, Stryker's per-test coverage limit raised (no story; Ariva.UnitTests/stryker-config.json, docs/harness; branch story/mvp-phase1)

- Cause: the 3821542 and 45edc08 checkpoints passed every suite but their mutation steps could not end. Stryker 5.0's MTP runner captures coverage one test at a time and allows each test 1.5 times its initial run time plus `additional-timeout` (then 10 seconds), at least 30 seconds (read from the runner's decompiled `CalculateSingleTestTimeout` and `RunSingleTestForCoverageInReusedProcessAsync`). A test past that has its test server killed, but the runner keeps waiting for the dead server's coverage relay file, which it clears only once per assembly: every later test on that runner waits 10 seconds for an acknowledgement that never comes and is marked Dubious. Measured at debug verbosity on a quiet machine (load 1.7 on 4 cores): `QueueEnginePositionRunTests.HallZone_Should_KeepEveryCrossingWithItsStateUnderAMegabyte_When_TwentySensorsSendThreeThousandPositionsASecond` (ARV-230, 4.9 seconds alone) ran past 30 seconds with the queue engine's coverage recorded, from 17:21:42 to 17:22:12 UTC, and every later test of that runner went Dubious. With all three runners in that state a checkpoint marked about 1,025 tests an hour Dubious, and each mutant would then have run the whole suite: days. The 2026-10-22 note that put this on a story gate beside Stryker was wrong; load only made it come sooner.
- Changed: `additional-timeout` 120,000 ms in `Ariva.UnitTests/stryker-config.json` (was 10,000). The same diagnostic run then captured all 7,070 tests in 23 minutes with none Dubious, and went on to test 913 mutants of `QueueStateEngine.cs` (stopped there; the checkpoint runs the step). The cost: a mutant that loops is counted as a timeout up to two minutes later. docs/harness/test-cadence.md says how to find the test when "Test run timed out while capturing per-test coverage" appears again.
- Gotchas:
  - xUnit v3 test ids in Stryker's log differ between a worktree and the checkout (the path is part of them): name a test from an id with `Ariva.UnitTests --filter-uid <id> --output Detailed` in the same tree that produced the id.
  - Stryker writes a mutated `Ariva.Core.dll` into the unit tests' output: never build the unit tests while a Stryker run uses this checkout, and build them again after it.
- Gates: the diagnostic run above (coverage capture complete, 0 Dubious); `node scripts/verify.mjs quick`. The checkpoint on this commit is the proof.

## 2026-10-23 ARV-175: Dead letters: text PostgreSQL accepts and a per-topic relay hold (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Infra messaging, tests, docs)

- Text (finding 1 of the ARV-171 review): `DeadLetters.Create` now passes the key, every header name and value and the error message through `DeadLetters.Printable` after cutting them (a cut can split a surrogate pair): each NUL character and each unpaired surrogate becomes U+FFFD, a surrogate pair is kept. The parts that held one are named in the new `ariva-dead-letter-text-replaced` header (`error`, `headers`, `key`, sorted; never the characters), also when the headers are dropped to fit, and the last-resort cut is made printable too. The topic, partition, offset and consumer stay exact. `OutboxKeyOf` keys a letter whose key was replaced by the key's digest (`sha256-...`). A record's own header whose name starts like a flag (`ariva-dead-letter-`, any case) is kept under `record:`, so a record cannot set the letter's flags. The last-resort cut flags a surrogate pair it splits, and `ariva-dead-letter-headers-dropped` counts only the record's headers, not the letter's own flag. A flagged letter's key and headers are no longer the record's: a replay reads them from the source topic (the `DeadLetter` and `KafkaDeadLetterSink` summaries say so).
- Relay (finding 2): a pass claims up to a batch of event rows and then up to a batch of dead-letter rows (one constant statement, the kind and the held topics as parameters: `(topic LIKE '%.dlq.v1') = @deadLetters AND topic <> ALL (@heldTopics)`), so a dead-letter backlog cannot crowd events out, and sends the events first (rows of different topics are independent; per-key order is unchanged). Dead letters get at most `OutboxRelay.DeadLetterPassBound` (5 s) of the pass: each send is bounded by what is left of that share (the row's error names it), and the rest wait untouched. A dead-letter row's failure that is not its own (the broker unavailable, the dead letters' share, a non-row error such as a refusal) holds back its topic for `DeadLetterTopicHold` (1 minute): the rest of the pass skips the topic, and one constant statement in the pass's transaction makes every unsent row of the topic due no earlier than the hold's end, so no relay claims them meanwhile, whichever leads, also after a restart; the events and the other dead-letter topics carry on. A dead-letter send cut short by the pass's own time (the events used it) is not the topic's fault: the pass ends without a hold and the letter is due after the broker retry. So a dead-letter topic that cannot be reached delays the events written meanwhile by at most 5 s once a minute, and once more each time a letter for it is kept meanwhile at a host's stop (that try holds the topic again); an event row's broker failure still ends the pass.
- Filed: ARV-246 (Phase 3, priority 41), from review round 3: the relay loop's wait skipped only when a pass sent something, and a host's own producer failure (disposed, `Local_Destroy`, fatal) holding no dead-letter topic; wiki 10 states the second meanwhile.
- Filed: ARV-245 (Phase 3, priority 40): a broker-unavailable streak escalated as an Error and a metric, and passes skipped while the cached broker probe answers false (the ARV-165 review's F1, parked in this story's notes and outside its criteria); an event topic without a leader still ends each pass at its first row.
- Tests: `DeadLetterOutboxTests` (NUL in the key and a header, a lone surrogate in the error, a cut splitting a pair, the last-resort cut splitting the key's pair with the dropped count excluding the flag, no flag when nothing was replaced, a record header named like a flag kept apart, `Printable` cases; 26), `OutboxRelayTests` (the away dead-letter topic held within the pass and on its rows, so another relay claims none of it until the hold has passed; a refused topic held with its attempt counted and the event control ending the pass; a hung dead-letter send ending at the dead letters' share with another relay's next pass skipping the topic; three letters before two events with a batch of two, both events claimed and sent first; a dead letter cut by the pass's own time on a stepped clock, no hold and due after the broker retry; a NUL and lone-surrogate letter kept and sent; 17), `DeadLetterKeptAtStopTests` (the unreadable variant's record now carries a NUL in its key and a header value: kept at the stop, keyed by its digest, relayed with U+FFFD and the flag "headers,key"). Mutation checks: with `Printable` a no-op the unreadable variant fails ("left unacknowledged" found 1); without the hold's statement the away-topic and hung-send tests fail (the rows not held, another relay trying the topic again).
- Docs: overview section 5 (Producing: the relay's claims, share and hold; the residual), ADR-0018 note 2026-10-23, wiki 10 (the hold's Warning and what it means; the keep's residual), cwe-controls CWE-501 and CWE-400, asvs-l2 V1.3.3 and V16.5.2, ConsumeFilters comments.

F1 the relay's claim and bound (a dead-letter backlog could crowd events out, an away topic could cost every pass up to its bound; "never delays an event" overclaimed); F2 no tests for the general-failure and bound holds; F3 no end-to-end test of a NUL record kept at a stop; F4 a record header could spoof the flag; F5 stale residual text. All fixed as above.

## 2026-10-24 ARV-154: Site configuration import: creates take the site lock so an empty site stays empty (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Infra services, tests, docs)

- The ARV-122a review's N2 (accepted residual): the import takes the site's row for update while it checks that the site is empty and writes, but the creates took no lock on it before their flush. Measured: each create's insert locks the row by its foreign key (key share) only at its flush, at commit, so a create already waited for an import at commit; the gap was between a create's checks and its commit, when an import could find the site empty and import beside the hand-made record.
- New `SvcDb.ShareSiteAsync(siteCode)`: one constant statement (`SELECT 1 AS "Value" FROM site WHERE code = :code FOR SHARE`, the code bound) in the unit of work's transaction, held to its end. Called after each create's own scope and validation checks (a caller outside the site, or an unknown code, never holds the row) and before its first write and any other lock: `SvcTopology` terminal, level, checkpoint, desk and desk range; `SvcDeskCodeMappings.CreateAsync`; `SvcFloorPlans.UploadAsync` (after the malware screen, before the level's row); `SvcAlertRules.CreateAsync` (before its per-site advisory lock); `SvcDisplays.CreateAsync` (before its checks, which can take the site's advertising lock). Unchanged, already taking the row for update: the zone profile draft, device registration, the two CSV imports (which call the mapping and device creates while holding it), the seeds and the import. Creates do not wait for each other; an import waits for the creates in flight and they wait for it.
- Tests (`SiteConfigurationTests`): `Creates_Should_HoldTheSitesRowUntilTheyCommit_When_TheyAddConfigurationToASite` (each of the eleven creates with its unit of work held open after the service returns: the row cannot be taken `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` (55P03) until it commits, and can after); `Create_Should_WaitForAnImportAndSucceedAfterIt_When_TheImportStartedFirst` (an import held open after writing; a terminal create waits, then both succeed, two terminals); `Import_Should_WaitForACreateAndRefuseTheSite_When_TheCreateStartedFirst` (a terminal create held open; the import waits, then answers SiteNotEmpty and writes nothing). Diagnostic with the helper a no-op: every one of the nine changed creates held nothing (the row free), the draft and the device held it; with the terminal's call removed the create-first test fails (the import-first test passes either way: the foreign key's flush lock already made the create wait).
- Docs: decisions.md (the ARV-122a residual closed, dated note), asvs-l2 V2.3.4 (the concurrency evidence), cwe-controls CWE-89 (the share lock's constant SQL), wiki 11 (the import row: a create during an import waits, an import during a create answers 409).

Its Low: the display create's checks could take the site's advertising lock before the site row (no deadlock: nothing holding that lock asks for the site row), moved so the site row comes first everywhere; Info: the integration hosts connect as the admin login, so the runtime role's FOR SHARE (it needs UPDATE on a column of `site`, which script 0046 keeps) is proven by the E2E hosts (`ariva_app`).

## 2026-10-24 ARV-169: Subdivision flag emoji allowed in display texts and names (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Core, Ariva.Infra, tests, docs)

- Owner decision 2026-10-13 (decisions.md, point 2, reversing ARV-158 point 2): the England, Scotland and Wales flag emoji are allowed, only as the three well-formed RGI subdivision sequences; every other tag character stays refused.
- `DisplayText` (Domain/Components, so the story gate was wide): the three exact sequences (U+1F3F4, the tags for gbeng, gbsct or gbwls, the cancel tag U+E007F), written as escapes; `NextOffender` steps over a sequence whole when U+1F3F4 starts one of them (ordinal), and judges every other tag character as before. So every display text, topology and site name, floor plan file name, the site configuration import and `--check-stored-names` take the three flags, and nothing else: an unknown or malformed subdivision, upper case tags, a sequence without its cancel tag, a truncated one, a tag or cancel tag after a flag, the tags without the waving flag, a flag split by a space, a variation selector or a joiner, a lone surrogate inside, before or after a flag.
- Found by the review: user display names removed the zero-width joiner and non-joiner before the check and stored the original, so after this change a joiner could split a flag's tags through (and, older, a surrogate pair split by a joiner). `DisplayText.IsClean` and `Offenders` take `allowJoiners` (U+200C and U+200D taken where they stand, nothing removed); `SvcUsers.IsUsableDisplayName` (account administration's name rule, not sign-in) and `StoredNameCheck` (the person rule and its positions) use it, so the name judged is the name stored.
- Tests: `DisplayTextTests` (a table of 19 subdivision cases, lone surrogates around a flag, `Offenders` after and around flags, `Require`, names, user display names with flags and joiners), two `StoredNameCheckTests` person rows and a positions case, `topology.spec.ts` (a tag after a flag and a flag without its cancel tag refused with the fixed text on every topology create and rename; a level named with the Wales flag created and read back).
- Docs: the CWE-501 and CWE-79 rows (the decision, its scope, the joiners; the ARV-158 sentence limited to control and format characters), decisions.md (built), wiki 10, 11 and 13. Filed: ARV-248 (the invisible code points outside the control and format categories that still pass, variation selectors, Hangul fillers and others; an owner decision on U+FE0F).
- Security review (CWE-79, CWE-501): round 1 FAIL (Medium: the display name check judged a copy without the joiners; Low: wiki 11 said no tag character), both fixed, with the recommended edge case tests, the E2E read back and ARV-248 taken; round 2 PASS (ASVS V1.1.1 restored for display names, V2.1.1 accurate; nothing weakened).
- Gotchas:
  - A check that edits a text before judging it must store what it judged, or judge what it stores: removing characters can join two halves of a refused sequence into an accepted one.
  - A theory row with a lone surrogate is serialised to a replacement character: build such strings in the test body.

## 2026-10-24 ARV-170: Zone outlines have a minimum width of 1 cm (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Core, unit tests, docs)

- Owner decision 2026-10-13 (decisions.md, point 4; from the ARV-161 review): zone outlines have a minimum width of 1 cm. Before, a triangle 10 m long and 1 mm wide passed `Geometry.IsSimplePolygon` (simple, area 5e-3 m2, above the 1e-4 m2 minimum).
- `Geometry.IsSimplePolygon` (Domain/Components, so the story gate was wide): after the area check, every vertex is checked against each edge it is not part of (`DistanceToSegment` at least `Tolerance`, 1 cm), the edge's ends put in order first (`Ordered`, ARV-161), so a rotated or reversed ring computes the same distances. Two edges that share no vertex come closest at a vertex of one of them; for a triangle the rule is its smallest height. A taper towards a sharp corner is not refused (every acute corner narrows to nothing), and the docs say so rather than "1 cm wide everywhere". With four or more vertices the edge pair checks already implied it; a triangle has only neighbouring edges, so only triangles were missing it; the check runs for every ring anyway. A ring with a non-finite vertex is now refused by the predicate itself (NaN passed every comparison; unreachable before, as `ParseRing` and `Zone.RequirePolygon` refuse one first). It holds wherever `IsSimplePolygon` does: zone add, move and rename, the site configuration import and export (409 `ProfileNotImportable`), `ZoneProfile.Validate` at publication and `--check-stored-names`' outline rule. A sliver stored before blocks publication, named (`OutlineNotSimple`), until it is moved; no stored data is changed. The add and move refusal names the 1 cm width.
- Tests: `GeometryTests` rows in every rotation and direction (a 10 m by 1 mm triangle, apexes 9 mm, 11 mm and exactly 1 cm from the base, near a base end, almost over a base end, a taper 11 mm at its widest, slanted strips 9 and 11 mm with corners over 2 cm apart, notches 9 and 11 mm, a 3 by 2 m zone, an L shape) and non-finite vertices; `ZoneProfileLegacyTests` (a stored sliver refuses validation and publication, cannot be added or moved into, moving it to a rectangle validates); `SiteConfigurationTransferTests` (export and import of a sliver refused); a `StoredNameCheckTests` outline row; `zone-profiles.spec.ts` (a sliver answers 400 with the fixed text); a property of thin triangles on a millimetre grid against the rule in integers, in every rotation and direction, both answers counted (shown to fail when triangles skip the check, a temporary change reverted). The seed profiles (NBJ BC1, the demo topology, AUH Terminal A) still validate.
- Docs: formulas.md (the F22 publishability bullet, a section on the minimum width after the ARV-161 one), wiki 07 (geometry validation rules), wiki 11 (the profile API table, the draft paragraph, the controls table), decisions.md (point 4 and the open points table: built), the CWE-501 row.
- Security review (CWE-20): round 1 PASS with six Lows and four Infos, all taken: the export left out of the docs' list; "the narrowest part is at a vertex" and "1 cm wide everywhere" inaccurate (a taper to a sharp corner passes; now said so); the 9 mm strip row was refused by the distinct vertex check, not the width (now slanted strips); no move, import, export or E2E sliver case (added); NaN accepted by the predicate (now refused); wiki 11 silent on the width (updated); the property generators could not make a triangle the rule refuses (the thin triangle property); the CWE-501 row's traceability. Not changed: `OutlineNotSimple`'s text, already accurate for a sliver (a vertex within 1 cm of an edge it does not end). Round 2 PASS (the property's integer oracle matches the triangle rules exactly and its 0.1 % skip margin cannot hide a disagreement, every caller path has a sliver test, the docs accurate); its notes taken: the property's orders described as they are (as given, a random rotation, reversed), the CWE-501 row names the new tests, a doubled reference in decisions.md.
- Gotchas:
  - A rule enforced through pairs of edges leaves out what has no non-neighbouring pair: a triangle. Check the smallest case of every polygon rule.
  - A test row is proof of the rule it names only if no earlier check refuses it: a 9 mm strip's corners are 9 mm apart, so the distinct vertex check refused it first.
  - Every comparison with NaN is false, so a predicate written as a chain of "refuse if below" checks accepts NaN unless it refuses non-finite input first.

## 2026-10-25 ARV-155: CSV imports: lock and upload contention, tokens kept out of test messages, absent optional columns (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Api.Common, Ariva.Api.Main, Ariva.Core, Ariva.Infra, Ariva.Web, tests, docs)

- From the ARV-123a review (N1, N4, N5): a preview's dry run and a commit hold the site's row lock and the host's one upload permit while they run (a preview about 3 s at 500 devices, 12 s at 10,000 mappings), so one user looping them delayed every registration, calibration and publication at the site and turned other uploads away.
