The global rate limiter runs before authentication, so a per-user key is not there to be had; the filter runs after authorization and, at order -1, before `SteadyUploadAttribute` reads the body. A refusal is 429 with Retry-After (the refused lease's own: the window's length, never shorter than the wait) and a fixed text; the request log records it as a refused request (LimitReached). The key is the caller's user id; the test scheme's principals, which have no sub, count by their name (a principal without sub gets no stored grants); with neither, 403. E2E raises the limit (`playwright.config.ts`), as for the other limiters.
- Lock wait: `SvcDb.TryLockSiteAsync` sets the transaction's own `lock_timeout` (5 s, `CsvImportLimits.SiteLockWait`), takes the site's row for update, and puts back the value it read first (`current_setting`, not `pg_settings.reset_val`, which would drop a value set earlier) once it holds it, so the registrations' own waits are as before; a lock_not_available (55P03) answers `CsvImportErrors.SiteBusy`, 409. Both imports, preview and commit, use it. The bound: one user holds a site's lock for at most 12 runs per 10-minute window per replica, under 3 minutes at the mapping bound (up to twice that in 10 minutes across a window's end; users' allowances add up), and the host's upload permit for those runs' transfers, scans and waits too.
- Absent optional columns: `CsvTable.ColumnOrNone` gives null for a column the file does not carry (a declarative device without `mappingName` answered column 0 before); both imports use it.
- Tokens out of test messages (CWE-532): token absence asserted as booleans in DeviceImportTests, DeskCodeMappingImportTests, csv-imports.spec.ts, and the token's shape in flight-schedules.spec.ts, the commit's credentials by their count (a failing `toBeNull`, `toMatch`, `Should().BeNull()` or `Should().HaveCount()` prints the value it got); the rule in wiki 16, for the import tests (the older assertions elsewhere and a checker are ARV-249).

## 2026-10-25 ARV-164a: Test counts: the unit suite's runner in CI, a guard against cases left out, and Stryker's count (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; scripts, CI workflows, docs)

- Why: CI's unit step still ran the suite through `dotnet test`, where the VSTest adapter reads the xUnit runner's messages from standard output and drops a line it cannot read without a failure (the Pact verifier's native report and display names with raw control characters reach the same stream; ARV-164). A dropped line can be a failing test, the security tests included, so a failure could pass CI unnoticed: a gate integrity gap. Split again on 2026-10-25: the E2E races and the integration stream are ARV-164b.
- CI (`ci.yml`): the unit step runs the test executable as the unit gate does (`dotnet <Release dll> --no-ansi`, Microsoft Testing Platform in process, the xUnit TRX in `TestResults` for the test counts step); the failure report reads the platform's own lines (`failed <name> (<time>)`, the error below) for the unit tests and dotnet test's for the integration tests; a new step "Unit test count guard" (`if: !cancelled()`) runs the guard's self-test and the guard on the Release dll and its TRX.
- Guard: `scripts/test-counts.mjs` (a library, nothing runs on import) and `scripts/test-count-guard.mjs` (a command line only, no main condition). It lists the cases with `dotnet <dll> --list-tests --no-ansi` (an argument array, no shell, 256 MiB and 5 minutes at most) and compares them with the TRX's results method by method (the name before the first parenthesis, since the listing and the TRX format arguments differently; character references decoded, unknown entities and code points past U+10FFFF left as they are): a method with fewer results than listed cases, a result for a method not listed, an empty listing, no results, and a TRX that is not a whole run's (no result summary, no `</TestRun>` end, or a stated total that is not its number of results) each fail it. A theory whose rows are not enumerated at discovery is listed once and runs as many rows (59 methods with 716 results on this tree), so the totals differ and the comparison is per method. Not caught, and stated in the library's header and wiki 16: a theory listed once that loses some of its rows while others ran (ARV-251), and a loss hidden by another method's extra rows when two custom display names share the text before their parenthesis (the unit tests set none). Self-test: 16 checks. The unit gate (`verify.mjs`) deletes the last TRX before the run, then runs the self-test and the guard after the unit tests.
- Stryker: `scripts/mutation-run.mjs --tests <dll>` lists the worktree's unit test build (the library's listing) and fails the run when Stryker's "Number of tests found" (summed over its test projects) is below it, when none is reported, or when the listing fails or names no case; `verify.mjs mutation` and the weekly `mutation.yml` pass it (the Debug build Stryker makes). Self-test: 15 cases.
- `scripts/security/scan.mjs`: its main check accepted only a path equal to the module's, so a run through a link exited 0 having scanned nothing; it now runs main when argv[1]'s own path or its real path is the module's (imported, as the post-edit hook does, it still does not).
- Docs: wiki 16 (the unit runner and the guard, what it cannot see, the Stryker runner and gate lines, the run snippet without `dotnet test`), wiki 04 (local development), docs/harness/test-cadence.md (the unit row, Stryker's tests found), the layer-4 row of docs/security/cwe-controls.md and wiki 13, the PRD (ARV-164a reworded, ARV-164b and ARV-251 filed).
- Security review (test integrity; CWE-78 and CWE-94 touched by the scripts): round 1 FAIL: (1) the guard's and the scanner's main checks compared paths, so a run through a link exited 0 having done nothing; (2) mutation-run accepted an empty listing (0 listed passes any count); (3) a TRX cut short inside a theory listed once passed (every method still had a result); (4) the weekly mutation workflow did not pass `--tests`; (5) colour codes could reach the listing and CI's unit.log; (6) docs: wiki 16 overstated what the guard sees, the layer-4 rows, and wiki 04 and 16 still recommended `dotnet test` for the unit suite. All fixed as above. Round 2 PASS; its Lows: the wiki 16 Gate bullet did not name the tests-left-out check (fixed); skipped tests unverified in the TRX (checked: a class run with 3 skips has `total="44"`, 44 result elements and `notExecuted="3"`, and the guard passes it); the scanner's main check under `--preserve-symlinks-main` (fixed: either path counts, and that run fails closed on its fixtures).
- Shown to fail: dropping one result of a method with three (`PasswordTests`) from the real TRX fails the guard (the total and the method's 3 against 2); a link to the guard with missing files exits 1; the self-tests' refusals.
- Gates: on the real run the guard reads 7,212 cases in 3,161 methods and 7,869 results, none left out. The full mutation run on 8007434 (beside two backend gate runs, with Docker down) found 7,212 tests, equal to the worktree's listing, so the new check passed on a real log; Stryker then ended after its initial test run without a score or an error line (the step failed, as it should). Story gate `node scripts/verify.mjs story` (13 changed files, wide: none, so no integration or E2E) on the final tree: run 1 (08:35 to 09:00 UTC, on 8007434 with the changes uncommitted, Docker up) passed every step but one unit test this story does not touch, `UploadScreeningTests.ScreenAllAsync_Should_RefuseAsNoVerdictAtTheBundlesDeadline_When_ThePartsTogetherTakeLonger` (the deadline met, the stopwatch at 2.07 s against its 1.5 s bound: it measured the full run's thread pool, not the deadline; fixed on its own, 9c1667e, test only); run 2 (09:04 to 09:18 UTC, on 9c1667e): PASS, exit 0: build, unit 7,869 of 7,869, the guard's self-test and the guard (7,212 cases in 3,161 methods, none left out), security scan 2,258 files, 0 errors (the 12 standing warnings), every self-test and audit, docs text rules. Earlier, `node scripts/verify.mjs backend` run 2 (08:24 to 08:34 UTC) failed only the 9 `AppHostModelTests`, with Docker down after the container restart (below); every other step, the guard included, passed. `node scripts/verify.mjs quick` PASS after this entry.
- Gotchas:
  - JavaScript's `.` does not match U+2028 or U+2029 without the `s` flag: a display text test's arguments hold one, so the listing parsed 7,211 cases against 7,212.
  - A main condition that compares `argv[1]` with the module's path fails open through a link (the loader resolves `import.meta.url`); a command line that only runs as one needs no condition, and a module that is also imported compares both paths.
  - A global regular expression's `test()` moves its `lastIndex`, so a second call on another text can miss; use `matchAll` or a regex without `g` for tests.
  - A step that fails does not stop the ones after it in verify.mjs, so a check that reads a run's output must delete the last run's output first.
  - After a container restart, `dockerd` can refuse to start on a stale `/var/run/docker.pid` whose number a boot-time process holds; check `docker info` after starting it. With Docker down the 9 `AppHostModelTests` fail (Aspire waits for the container runtime), in a gate and in Stryker's initial test run alike.

## 2026-10-25 ARV-164b: Test determinism: the E2E races, and the integration suite's runner stream (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; E2E tests, the integration gate, CI, docs)

- Oversized bodies read as resets (site-configuration.spec.ts, security-baseline.spec.ts, aidx.spec.ts, and flight-schedules.spec.ts the same way). Cause: fetch and Playwright's request stream the body; once the host has answered 413 or 401 from the head and closed the connection (Connection: close, ARV-233), a later write of the body fails (EPIPE, or a reset) and the client destroys the socket before reading the answer already received, so the test saw "fetch failed" or EPIPE instead of the status the host sent (probed in ARV-191 with curl and a paced client). Three specs had taken "closed: fetch failed" as an alternative answer. Fix: `announced()` (Platform/Testing/Ariva.E2E/scripts/raw-http.mjs, with its types in raw-http.d.mts; the specs reach it through tests/support/raw-http.ts) sends the request head with the Content-Length and none of the body (net or tls, verification on; the length a whole number, the method and header names tokens, values without a line break, Host, Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding its own, http and https only, an IPv6 host's brackets stripped), reads the whole final answer (Content-Length, chunked or to the close; an interim 1xx skipped), and rejects on a close, a reset or no answer within 15 s; the four specs assert the status, the headers they asserted before (problem+json, Connection: close, no leak) and no longer accept a closed connection. An answer now proves the host decided without the body, which was never sent. `node Platform/Testing/Ariva.E2E/scripts/raw-http.mjs --self-test` (run by the security step of verify.mjs and by CI) proves it against local servers: a 413 with Content-Length and a chunked 401 over two writes read whole, an answer followed by a reset read 20 of 20 times, an interim 100 skipped, the head as sent; a reset before the answer, a close inside it, a silent server, a refused connection and every malformed request refused (the IPv6 case runs where ::1 exists).
- The tablet tally's count 2 where 3 was expected (validation-capture.spec.ts, "the tablet layout works on touch", 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-23; the "key press not counted" was the same case). Cause: the tally's bins are Ariva's UTC quarter hours, and `Tally.tap` ticks first, so once the quarter hour has passed it closes the bin and starts both counts at 0; a test that tapped In once before a quarter hour and Enter and Space after it read 0 + 2. Fix: `roomInThePeriod` (tests/support/clock-room.ts) reads Ariva's clock (a host's Date header) before the line is chosen and, with less than 60 s left of the quarter hour, waits until 3 s past the next quarter hour (the Date header stands on a whole second, and the page's own reading of Ariva's clock can differ by about half a second plus a round trip), adding exactly that wait to the test's own time. Shown with a temporary copy of the test (reverted) brought to the helper 50 s before a quarter hour: it waited 52 s and the counts 1, 2 and 3 held in the new bin. The test took at most 12.2 s from sign-in to its end in 18 runs under load.
- The portrait desk log's scroll width (2026-10-18, once): no cause could be named, so it moved to ARV-164c (split recorded in the PRD). Ruled out, with temporary instrumentation (reverted) that sampled the page's width 0, 16, 50, 100, 250, 500 and 1,000 ms after the tap and listed every box outside the viewport: a transient after the tab switch (19 runs, both viewports, under four CPU hogs: never wider than the screen); the desk log's bin closing during the test (one run started 6 s before a real quarter hour, so the history appeared: no overflow, since the app's main area clips what overflows it, `overflow-x-clip`); slow or missing web fonts (runs in both viewports with every font file refused, so the fallback fonts throughout: no overflow). The test body and the layout are unchanged since the failure (a cookie name aside). The four sideways scroll checks of the tablet tests now go through `expectNoSideScroll`, the same bound (the page no wider than the screen) with a failure that names the elements outside the viewport and their edges, so a recurrence names its cause.
- The desk log minute stored late ("the desk log never places a minute without Ariva's clock", 2026-10-18 in CI and 2026-10-23): the test counted the bin's POST on Playwright's request event, which fires when the page sends it, before the test's own route (`TabletClock.serveDates`, which can hold a request while a clock move finishes) has passed it to Ariva, and it read Ariva's stored minutes right after; the read could reach Ariva first. Fix: the test also records the POST's answers and reads the stored minutes once the bin has its 201. The other reads after a post in the file already waited for the unsent banner to clear, an answered send.
- The AMAN pull past its 30 s (aman-pull.spec.ts, 2026-10-23 twice): the test registered the endpoints before it played the minute that fills the mock AMAN's feed; the Integration host claims a new endpoint at its poller's next tick (15 s), so a tick in between pulled an empty feed, kept the position at 0 and made the next pull due only `poll_seconds` (30 s) later, past the test's 30 s. Fix: the minute is played first; the waits are bounded by what the poller allows (25 s: a tick plus the pull) within a test time of 45 s; the old order would still fail at 25 s.
- The integration suite's stream: CI and the gates ran it through `dotnet test`, where the hosts' JSON console logs share the xUnit runner's message stream that the VSTest adapter reads and drops a line of. It now runs as the unit suite does: `UseMicrosoftTestingPlatformRunner` on Ariva.IntegrationTests, `verify.mjs` runs `dotnet Ariva.IntegrationTests.dll` with its TRX (the last one deleted first; the project built when no solution build ran before) and then the ARV-164a count guard; the story gate's `--integration` filter keeps dotnet test's `FullyQualifiedName~A|FullyQualifiedName~B` form and nothing else (`methodFilter` in scripts/test-counts.mjs: `--filter-method *A*` per term, which matches a method whose fully qualified name holds A, ignoring case, as `~` does: `*csvimportlimittests*` lists the same 8 cases; a name may have its wildcard only at the start or the end), and the guard lists the same selection (`test-count-guard.mjs --dll <dll> --trx <file> -- <filter options>`, only method, class and namespace filters with plain names). CI's integration step runs the Release executable, then a count guard step; its failure report reads both suites' output in the platform's form. The Azure DevOps pipeline still runs both suites through dotnet test: noted on ARV-217, which brings it to ci.yml's level.
- The immigration screen's e-gate count (found by this story's second full E2E run: immigration.spec.ts 'a border shift supervisor sees each lane, the desks and the e-gates of the arrival hall', 33 on the screen against 46 read before the page loaded, passed on the retry): the test took the count to lie between an API read before the page loaded and one after it was checked, but the view's figures are those of the last 15 whole minutes (`SvcImmigrationView`: `[to - 15 min, to)`, `to` the minute in progress), so at each minute's start an interval leaves them and a later read can be lower. Fix: both bounds kept; the reads start with room in the minute (`roomInThePeriod`, 50 s, the same helper as the tally's, now `tests/support/clock-room.ts`), and the test asserts that its two reads, and so the page loaded between them, are in one minute of the window (the view's `asOfUtc`), so a straddle fails as one.
- The outbox relay's dead letters' share (found by the first story gate's full integration run on the new runner: `OutboxRelayTests.Relay_Should_GiveDeadLettersOnlyTheirShareOfThePass_When_ADeadLetterSendNeverEnds`, 3 sent and 1 held back where 2 and 2 were expected, once): a dead-letter send's bound is a timer of the relay's TimeProvider (a System.Threading.Timer, on the coarse tick clock), while the share is measured on its time stamps (the Stopwatch); the timer can fire a few milliseconds before the time stamps show the share's end, and the next topic's letter was then sent with those milliseconds. Within the bound, but not deterministic. Fix (Ariva.Infra `OutboxRelay`): a dead-letter send cut by the share's bound spends the share for the rest of the pass, whatever the time stamps read a moment later; events, the pass's own time and the topic hold are unchanged. Test: `Relay_Should_SpendTheDeadLettersShare_When_ASendIsCutAtItsEndAndTheTimeStampsReadLess` (the relay's time stamps stand still while its timers run, so the old code always saw the whole share left); fails with the old relay (shown by restoring it, then the fix again), passes with the fix.
- Probe artefact (not a suite race): with `--repeat-each` over two workers, the serial validation-capture file's `beforeAll` ran twice at once and the validation manager's second TOTP sign-in was refused (401): `unusedTotpCode` orders the steps of one account within a run, not two sign-ins at the same moment, and the server takes a step only after the last one it took. In a normal run the account signs in only in that serial file, so once.
- Docs: wiki 16 (the integration suite's runner and filter, the run snippet, the fixture paragraph's last sentence), docs/harness/test-cadence.md (the two integration rows), wiki 04 (local development), the ARV-217 note. Filed: ARV-164c (the portrait scroll width) and ARV-252 (from the review: CI's unit and integration logs now carry the in-process hosts' console output into the public job log, unchecked for secrets; CWE-532).
- Security review (test integrity; CWE-78 and CWE-77 for the scripts' commands, CWE-120 and CWE-918 in the tests, CWE-400 for the relay): round 1 FAIL on one Medium, R1 (wiki 16 still said the integration suite ran under dotnet test), with Lows: the client's IPv6 host brackets, an unchecked length and caller-written Host, Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding, no committed self-test for a client four security specs depend on, the AMAN wait's weaker assertion, `roomInTheBin` (now `roomInThePeriod`) ending only a second past the quarter hour, the run evidence; and Infos (an interim 1xx, header lookups on a plain object, the side scroll message crowded by descendants, a wildcard inside a filter name, case sensitivity of the method filter, the .claude agents' wording, the hosts' console output in CI's public log). All fixed or answered as above (the agents' wording left generic: verify.mjs's refusal names the form; the CI log filed as ARV-252). Round 2 PASS (the relay change tightens CWE-400: the share only shrinks, per pass; TLS verification kept, probed with a self-signed certificate by name and by IP); its Lows: the new relay test's margin (it relied on the catch path taking under a second: now the stepped time stamps, as above) and this entry; its Infos: the relay comment's wording (fixed), self-test cases for a malformed answer length and an untrusted certificate (probed by the reviewer, not added), a header named `__proto__` (dropped silently; left, since the client is unchanged after its E2E runs).
- Gates (2026-10-25, on f758200 with the changes uncommitted, detached, fresh services for each Playwright run): story gate run 1 (10:45 to 11:21, wide) passed its unit and security steps and ran the full integration suite on the test executable for the first time: 778 passed, 1 failed (the relay race above), 1 skipped, the guard 769 cases in 546 methods and 780 results, none left out; stopped before its E2E (by PID) for review round 1's fixes. Story gate run 2 (11:37 to 12:39, with those fixes and the relay fix): PASS, exit 0: build, unit 7,869 of 7,869 and the guard (7,212 cases in 3,161 methods, none left out), security scan 2,260 files and 0 errors (the 12 standing warnings), every self-test with the raw HTTP client's, docs, integration on the test executable 780 passed and 1 skipped of 781 (25.2 min) and its guard (770 cases in 547 methods, 781 results, none left out), E2E 923 passed and 1 skipped with none flaky, the host log scan and the artifact check clean. The E2E run after it (12:39 to 13:04) had one flaky case (the immigration count above), so the count of runs in a row started again on the final tree; the third was stopped. Final tree: the relay class 18 of 18 through the executable with `--filter-class` and the guard over it (18 cases, none left out), the new relay test failing with the old relay; the immigration and tablet layout tests 3 of 3; `node scripts/verify.mjs backend` (13:17 to 13:29) PASS, exit 0 (unit 7,869 of 7,869, the guard, scan 2,261 files and 0 errors, the raw HTTP client self-test); then three full E2E runs in a row (13:29 to 14:45, CI settings: one retry allowed, none used): 923 passed, 1 skipped and 0 flaky in each (24.8, 25.4 and 25.5 min), every host log scan and artifact check clean. The full integration run was on the tree before the relay test moved to the stepped clock and the relay comment's wording; the class run above covers both. `node scripts/verify.mjs quick` PASS after this entry.
- Gotchas:
  - A client that streams a body the server refuses unread can lose the answer to its own write error; to test a refusal from the head, send the head alone and read.
  - Playwright's request event fires before a route handler has passed the request on: wait for the response before reading what the server stored.
  - A real-time test that counts within Ariva's quarter-hour bins must start with room in the bin, or it straddles a reset.
  - A test that registers a poller's work before preparing what the poller reads can lose a whole poll interval.
  - `--repeat-each` runs the copies of a serial file in parallel workers: accounts signed in once per file then sign in at once.

## 2026-10-25 ARV-177: The broker probe names no topic, and no Ariva client creates a topic implicitly (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Infra Kafka clients and readiness, tests, docs; first criterion split to ARV-177a, a stop's skip filed as ARV-253)

- No implicit topics: `KafkaClientConfig.Apply` sets `AllowAutoCreateTopics = false` for the producer, the admin clients and the stream consumer, and MassTransit's rider takes `KafkaClientConfig.Rider()` as its base (below) (librdkafka asks a broker to create a topic it names by default for producer-type clients, the admin client included). `ImplicitTopicTests` (Ariva.IntegrationTests, a broker of its own whose `auto.create.topics.enable` is Kafka's default) proves each case against a control: a producer and an admin client with librdkafka's defaults create the topic they name (the admin client's metadata answer `LeaderNotAvailable`, then the topic exists); Ariva's producer and admin client create nothing (the admin's answer `UnknownTopicOrPart`, the topic still absent, read with a metadata request for every topic, which creates none).
- The missing topic's failure, measured: with auto-creation off, Ariva's producer waited the whole 30 s message timeout and failed with `Local_MsgTimedOut`, which `IsBrokerUnavailable` reads as the broker being away, so the relay would have ended every pass at that row (each 30 s) and held the keys behind it. librdkafka's `topic.metadata.propagation.max.ms` (default 30 s, equal to the message timeout) is how long it takes an unknown topic for one being created; Ariva's producer now has 5 s (`KafkaClientConfig.TopicPropagationMilliseconds`): the first send fails with the broker's `UnknownTopicOrPart` after 5.5 s, later sends with `Local_UnknownTopic` at once, both the row's own failure (the existing classification test lists both), and once the topic exists the same producer's next send goes at the first try (0.4 s; a send for a topic the client took for missing asks the brokers again). A second run measured 5.4 s; the test bounds it at the propagation bound plus 3 s. Docs say the rows of a topic missing at deploy back off up to 5 minutes and resume within their backoff of the topics job's run, without a restart (the ARV-176 re-review's recommendation c: documented rather than routed through the 5 s broker retry, since a missing topic is not an outage). Ingest: any sink failure answers 503 with Retry-After (`PushEndpointTests` gained the unknown-topic case: 503, Retry-After 5, the cause not in the body).
- The relay (from the security review, M1): the row's own failure still ended an event pass (any Kafka failure that is not the broker's absence did, since ARV-165), so a frequently raised event of a missing topic would have ended almost every pass at its row, the other topics waiting a poll each time. `IOutboxTransport.IsTopicRefused` (the Kafka transport: `KafkaProduce.IsTopicRefused`, the broker's `UnknownTopicOrPart`, the client's `Local_UnknownTopic` and `TopicAuthorizationFailed`) now holds that topic until the failed row's backoff ends, on all its unsent rows (`next_attempt_on`, one constant statement in the pass's transaction, shared with ARV-175's dead-letter hold as `HoldTopicUntilAsync`), so the topic's rows cannot fill a pass's batch during the hold, and at most one pass per hold when it ends (review round 2: an in-pass skip alone let 100 or more of them take every claim) and the other topics carry on; the row counts its attempt and backs off as before, and while the topic stays missing only its oldest row tries it again at each hold's end. Dead-letter rows keep ARV-175's minute-long topic hold. `OutboxRelayTests.Relay_Should_SkipOnlyTheMissingTopicAndSendTheOthers_When_AnEventsTopicIsMissing` (the classification of the Kafka transport, two keys of the missing topic and three rows of another: 3 sent in the pass, the failed row's attempt, backoff and `last_error`, its topic's other key untouched and held as long; once the topic exists both go when the hold ends) fails with the old relay and `Relay_Should_ClaimTheOtherTopics_When_AMissingTopicHasMoreDueRowsThanABatch` (a batch of 2, three rows of the missing topic before two of another: the first pass claims only the missing topic's rows and tries one, the next, with no time passing, sends the other topic's two; at the hold's end the oldest row tries again and every row of the topic is held for its doubled backoff) fails with the in-pass skip alone (each shown with the change disabled, then restored); both pass with it. The ARV-175 test's control, a topic's authorization refused on an event, now skips only that topic, so the control uses the cluster's authorization (`ClusterAuthorizationFailed`), which still ends the pass. MassTransit's rider takes the same base config (`KafkaClientConfig.Rider()`, passed to `UsingKafka`, which otherwise starts from an empty `ClientConfig`), so its consumers and any admin client it builds carry `allow.auto.create.topics` false explicitly (review L3); a `ClientConfig` in the container, which MassTransit took as the base only without one, still gives the rider its librdkafka `Debug` contexts (CommitRaceTests' diagnostics, review round 2's L1).
- The readiness probe: `KafkaProduce.BrokersAnswerAsync` asks for DescribeCluster on a dependent admin client of the producer's handle (`DescribeClusterAsync`, `RequestTimeout` the probe's 3 s, still one at a time and reused for a second) instead of every topic's metadata: the request names no topic, so its answer does not grow with the cluster's topics and cannot create one. Measured: 122 ms against the test broker; with no broker at the address, false after 3.1 s (the check's own wait has a second more).
- The first criterion, split to ARV-177a (with its integration test). The first design held a record that failed on its host's disposal at a stop: the dead-letter filter neither retried nor dead-lettered it and awaited a task that never ends, so the record stayed in hand until the process exited (`IsHostDisposal`: the endpoint stopping and an `ObjectDisposedException` in the failure's chain, or the host already stopped). Its unit tests passed and failed without the hold. Its integration test (`DisposalAtStopTests`, Faults collection: a host with a shutdown timeout of 26 s, so the bus waits 11 s; one retry of 200 ms; a 20 s attempt that then fails; a later record of another lane completing while it was pending; the second host on the broker's direct address while the first host's proxy is cut) disproved it: the hold began (the attempt's own `TimeoutException`, after the host had stopped), but the group's committed offset, read 3 s later, was past the held record (3, the held record at 1). MassTransit 8.5.11 decompiled (ILSpy) shows when: when the bus's stop wait ends with records in hand, `ConsumerAgent.ActiveAndActualAgentsCompleted` cancels them (`CancelPendingConsumers`), the cancellation of each receive context cancels its pending confirmation (`KafkaMessageConsumer.Handle` registers `ConsumerLockContext.Canceled`), and `BatchCheckpointer`, which awaits each confirmation in offset order, treats a cancelled one as it treats a faulted one and commits the next completed record past it. So nothing a filter does after the stop wait ends keeps such a record: the dead letter the last attempt keeps is its only trace, and a hold lost it. The hold and its tests were reverted (the dead-letter path is as before); ARV-177a, behind ARV-253, keeps the criterion.
- Found on the way, filed as ARV-253 (Phase 1, proposed for the go-live gate ARV-138, pending the owner): a record waiting in a consumer's lane behind one in hand when the endpoint begins to stop is never handled (`KafkaMessageConsumer.Handle` returns at once once the consumer is stopping), its confirmation is cancelled when the consumer closes, and the checkpointer passes it the same way. Probe (`QueuedAtStopTests`: one partition, a 4 s record, a record of the same lane queued behind it, a later record of another lane already consumed, a clean stop well within the bus's wait): the queued record was consumed by neither that host nor the next (60 s), and the group's committed offset was 4 with the record at 2. A valid event lost without a trace at any stop where a lane has a backlog; the stream engine's own consumer is not affected. The fix is ARV-253's (one lane per endpoint, so records complete in fetch order, or Ariva's own consume loop), measured against the pilot rates. The two tests' sources are kept for ARV-253 and ARV-177a.
- Docs: wiki 10 (readiness, the ARV-171 paragraph's "in that case alone" corrected, a new 4.5a bullet on `Unknown topic` in `last_error`, the stop budget's edge case replaced by the two limits and what to do until ARV-253), wiki 04 (the brokers' `auto.create.topics.enable`), the overview (Producing: the residual extended, a "No implicit topics" paragraph; the Kafka outage row), ADR-0018 note of 2026-10-25, docs/security/cwe-controls.md (CWE-400: the probe, the relay, the stop residual with ARV-253 and ARV-177a; CWE-501: the rider, and what keeps other clients out), docs/security/asvs-l2.md (V13.2.2 evidence, still Partly), decisions.md (2026-10-25 entry and an open row).
- Security review: round 1 FAIL on two Mediums. M1: the relay ended its pass at a missing-topic event row while four docs said the other topics carry on (fixed in code, as above, with the relay test). M2: the CWE-400 row's stop residual and wiki 10's "in that case alone" predated the two limits (both rewritten). Lows: L1 ARV-253 named Phase 3 in decisions.md (Phase 1); L2 "within 5 s" against 5.5 s measured and a test bound of 15 s (now "about 5 s" and a bound of 8 s); L3 the rider's consumers only by librdkafka's consumer default (now `KafkaClientConfig.Rider()`); L4 the CWE-501 row said a topic exists only as the topics job made it (now: no Ariva client creates one, the brokers' setting keeps the others out); L5 no ASVS evidence (V13.2.2). Infos: I1 the ADR note and decisions said the commit had happened before the hold (now: the confirmation was cancelled, the offset read 3 s later was past it); I2 the propagation bound's cost names a lagging or restarting broker's misreport too; I3 a stale comment (fixed), and a probe that never completes stays the single one in flight (existing, not changed here: librdkafka's request timeout ends DescribeCluster, and the check's own wait has a second more); I4 ARV-138's new dependency on ARV-253 is the owner's to confirm.
- Gotchas:
  - librdkafka's `topic.metadata.propagation.max.ms` equals the message timeout by default, so without auto-creation a missing topic fails a send as a timeout, not as an unknown topic.
  - MassTransit 8.5.11's Kafka checkpointer passes cancelled confirmations as it passes faulted ones, and a stop cancels both the records in hand at the stop wait's end and the records never handled; leaving a record unacknowledged keeps it only if no later record of its partition can complete first.
  - A test that holds a consumer's record in hand keeps that host's consumer in its group until the process ends; cut its proxy so the group's session timeout lets another host have the partition.
- Security review round 2: FAIL on one Medium, R2-M1: the in-pass skip did not hold when the missing topic's due rows filled the claim batch (100), every pass then claiming only them (fixed: the hold on the topic's rows, with the batch test). Low R2-L1: CommitRaceTests' librdkafka debug setting, a container `ClientConfig`, was no longer the rider's base once `Rider()` was passed (fixed: its `Debug` copied onto the rider; the test's comment updated). Infos: R2-I1 decisions.md still said a topic exists only as the topics job made it (reworded); R2-I2 nothing refuses an explicit `CreateIfMissing` on a rider topic endpoint (not added: no endpoint sets it, and it would be an explicit creation under the hosts' principal, whose create rights a topics job with a principal of its own takes away, `kafkaTopics.adminSecretName`, wiki 04).
- Security review round 3: PASS (CWE-400, CWE-501; ASVS V13.2.2 still Partly with the new evidence). Infos: two doc phrases overstated the hold (when it ends the topic's rows are due together and can fill one pass per hold period, and a new key's row written meanwhile tries the topic once: reworded to "at most one pass per hold"); ARV-138's dependency on ARV-253 is the owner's to confirm; a probe that never completes stays the one in flight (unchanged, bounded per answer).
- Gates: `node scripts/verify.mjs story` (wide: Ariva.Infra's Kafka files) run 3 on the reviewed code: build, unit tests and their count guard, the security scan (0 errors), the chart, audit and docs checks all PASS, E2E 923 passed and 1 skipped (none flaky) with no secret in the artifacts, integration 785 of 786: `ImplicitTopicTests.MetadataRequest_Should_CreateNoTopic_When_ArivasAdminClientNamesAMissingTopic` read the topic list before the broker's asynchronous creation of the control topic had finished (it passed alone, not under the gate's load). Fixed: Ariva's request first, then the control, then a bounded wait (30 s) for the control topic before the assertion that Ariva's request created nothing (0.2 to 0.7 s measured under four CPU hogs; 3 of 3 runs). Then `node scripts/verify.mjs integration`: 785 passed, 1 skipped (`TimescaleSmokeTests`, skipped since ARV-006), count guard 775 cases in 552 methods, 786 results, none left out. Runs 1 and 2 were stopped by PID after review findings changed the relay (run 1 in its integration step, run 2 in its unit tests).
- Gotchas (more):
  - A broker creates a topic a metadata request names asynchronously (the answer is `LeaderNotAvailable` meanwhile): a test that reads the topic list at once races the creation; wait for the control first, bounded.
  - When looking for a process's descendants with awk, do not test `a[p[k]]` on an unset key: awk creates it, and the list then names every parent; `ps -o pid= --ppid <pid>` recursively is safe.

## 2026-10-25 ARV-253: A stop never passes a record: one lane per Kafka consumer (Phase 1; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Di and Ariva.Infra messaging settings, tests, docs)

- The fix: every MassTransit topic endpoint's Kafka consumer has one lane (`endpoint.ConcurrentMessageLimit = 1` in `ArivaMessagingBuilder.Consume`; `ConcurrentDeliveryLimit` 1 as before), and `EnsureProducerSettings` refuses to start a host whose `Kafka:Consumers:ConcurrentMessageLimit` is anything but 1 (the message names ARV-253 and `ConsumersPerEndpoint`). Why it holds (MassTransit 8.5.11, decompiled): with one lane a consumer's records run on one task executor in the order they were fetched, so a partition's completed records are always its first ones, and `BatchCheckpointer`, which awaits confirmations in offset order, passes a cancelled or faulted one and commits only the last completed record, never meets a completed record after an unresolved one. The records a stop cancels (the one in hand at the stop wait's end, `CancelPendingConsumers`; the ones behind it, never handled once the consumer is stopping and cancelled at its close) and a record the dead-letter loop leaves unacknowledged therefore stay uncommitted, and the next host consumes them.
- Parallelism instead: `Kafka:Consumers:ConsumersPerEndpoint` (new, 1 to `ConsumerSettings.MaxConsumersPerEndpoint` 6, default 1, refused at start outside) sets MassTransit's `ConcurrentConsumerLimit`: that many Kafka consumers in the endpoint's group, each with its own partitions, lane, checkpointers and prefetch (1,000 messages, MassTransit's). The endpoint's librdkafka fetch queue (`QueuedMaxMessagesKbytes`) is `ConsumerSettings.FetchQueueKbytesPerEndpoint` (64 MiB, librdkafka's default for one consumer) divided by the consumers, so more consumers fetch no more ahead. `appsettings.base.json`: `ConcurrentMessageLimit` 1 (was 8), `ConsumersPerEndpoint` 1.
- The alternative of the criterion, Ariva's own consume loop on the Confluent client with an ordered checkpoint (as Ariva.Api.Stream has), is not built: it would mean rebuilding the rider's retry, inbox and dead-letter pipe; it stays the route if a consumer ever needs per-key parallelism within a partition (ADR-0018 note).
- Tests:
  - Unit `ProducerHardeningTests.AddArivaMessaging_Should_RefuseToStart_When_AnEndpointWouldHaveMoreThanOneLaneOrItsConsumersAreOutOfBounds` (lanes 1 accepted; 8, 2, 0 refused; consumers 1 and 6 accepted, 0 and 7 refused; the defaults).
  - Integration `QueuedAtStopTests` (Faults collection, new): a 4 s record in hand on partition 0, two records waiting behind it (one in its old lane, one in another), a clean stop; the committed offset is not past the waiting record and the next host consumes both. Two cases: one partition and one consumer (`ariva.forecast.published.v1`), two partitions and two consumers per endpoint (`ariva.forecast.arrival-wave.v1`), where a record on partition 1 is consumed in parallel while the slow one is in hand. With the endpoint set back to eight lanes (a temporary edit, restored from a saved copy) the one-partition case failed every run: offset 4 committed with the waiting record at 2, consumed by neither host. The two-partition case passed with eight lanes too (why is not established; probably the commit at the close lost the race with the consumer's close), so it proves the parallel consumers, not the skip.
  - Integration `InHandAtStopTests` (new, `ariva.sla.evaluation-finalised.v1`): a host whose bus waits 11 s (shutdown 26 s, grace 31 s, one retry of 200 ms), a 20 s attempt that then fails, a later record of another key behind it; the stop returns after 11.0 s with the attempt still running, the host is disposed, the attempt ends at 21 s; the committed offset stays at the slow record, and the next host consumes it (its second delivery) and the later record once. With eight lanes it failed at once: the later record completed while the slow one was in hand. In the run with one lane no dead letter was kept for the slow record (the cancelled attempt's retry did not run); what that path leaves is ARV-177a's.
  - Integration `DeadLetterKeptAtStopTests` rewritten for one lane: the later record of another key now waits behind the poison record's dead-letter loop instead of completing during it (the slow third record is gone: it existed only to hold the stop open while the checkpointer committed past the poison record), the stop commits exactly past the poison record (its letter kept, ARV-171), and the next host consumes the later record once; both cases (failing consumer, unreadable record with NUL characters) pass. `DeadLetterShutdownTests` unchanged and passing.
- Measured (the criterion's throughput): `node scripts/verify.mjs pilot-load`, run of 2026-10-25 21:58Z, 6 partitions a topic, one consumer per endpoint: both tests passed; every push 202 (steady 9,000, burst 6,000, recovery 1,806), the 20 oversized 413, the flooding device 600 accepted and 300 refused with 429; every crossing counted on every zone; the sensing archive (`ariva-stream.sensing-archive-tracks`, the busiest rider endpoint) about 100 records behind in the steady phase, peak 3,413 in the burst and back 18 s after it, against 20 s and 26 s (peaks 3,813) in ARV-230's two runs with eight lanes; it drained the peak at about 220 records a second while the hall pushed 30 (Estimate); the AMAN feed's 205 records produced and its 140 desk intervals stored with none unmapped; nothing unsent in the outbox; Stream 524 MB and 41 percent of a core on average; database connections at most 50. So the default stays 1 consumer per endpoint (wiki 05).
- The cost, documented (wiki 04, wiki 10, overview, cwe-controls, costly-operations): a retrying or stalled message holds every partition its consumer reads, not only its key, for at most its attempts (`RetryCount` + 1, 4 by default), each cut at `HandlerTimeoutSeconds`, with the retry waits between them and its dead letter's send after them: about 5 minutes at the defaults (4 times 70 s and up to 15 s of waits) and about 8 at the largest handler timeout (120 s), growing with `RetryCount`, which has no bound of its own yet (ARV-254), and a dead letter the broker refuses holds them until it is accepted or the stop.
- Docs: ADR-0018 (the context line and the endpoint defaults; a note of 2026-10-25 for ARV-253), the overview (Producing: "Consuming at a stop" replaces the residual and the two open limits), wiki 10 (the stop budget's two limits replaced by what ARV-253 closes and what stays ARV-177a's; the ARV-171 paragraph's checkpointing case; a refused dead letter holds its consumer's partitions), wiki 04 (`Kafka:Consumers:*`), wiki 05 (the run), docs/security/cwe-controls.md (CWE-400), docs/security/asvs-l2.md (V15.2.2 evidence), docs/security/costly-operations.md (the consumers row), decisions.md (2026-10-25 entry and an open row).
- Security review: round 1 FAIL on one Medium, M1: five docs gave a stalled message's hold as the retry schedule (15 s) or the handler timeout (70 s), where it is every attempt (`RetryCount` + 1) cut at `HandlerTimeoutSeconds` plus the retry waits, about 5 minutes at the defaults and 8 at the largest handler timeout (fixed in cwe-controls, decisions, ADR-0018, the overview and wiki 04). Lows fixed in the story: L3 the fetch-queue comment claimed more consumers fetch no more ahead, true of librdkafka's queue but not of MassTransit's prefetch (1,000 a consumer; reworded); L4 `QueuedAtStopTests` did not assert that the group had caught up and that the slow record was in hand before the stop (asserted now); L5 the key searches had no cap and the disposals no bound (10,000 tries; 30 s); L6 stale guidance in `DeadLetterRetry`'s comment and the kafka-streaming skill (`ConcurrentMessageLimit 8`; both updated). Lows filed as ARV-254 (Phase 3): L1 no alert for a rider endpoint held by one message, L2 `RetryCount` without a bound of its own, L7 librdkafka's `max.poll.interval.ms` (300 s) against the longest hold if MassTransit stops polling with its prefetch full (duplicates, not a loss). ARV-177a's integration criterion now describes a later record queued behind the slow one (one lane leaves none completing). Round 2: PASS (CWE-400; CWE-501 and CWE-120 touched lightly, settings refused at start and the cast and division bounded; ASVS V15.2.2 still Partly with the new evidence).
- Gates: `node scripts/verify.mjs story` (wide: Ariva.Di and Ariva.Infra messaging) on the reviewed code: all 29 steps PASS, among them build, unit tests (7,886) and their count guard, the security scan (0 errors), chart, audit and docs checks, integration 788 passed and 1 skipped (`TimescaleSmokeTests`, skipped since ARV-006) with its count guard, E2E 923 passed with no secret in the artifacts. After the review's fixes (comments, docs and test hardening only): `node scripts/verify.mjs backend` PASS (unit 7,886), the three changed integration classes 5 of 5, `node scripts/verify.mjs docs` PASS. `node scripts/verify.mjs pilot-load` as above.
- Gotchas:
  - MassTransit's rider commits only completed records but passes cancelled and faulted ones on the way, so the completed set must be a prefix of each partition: one lane per consumer gives that, lanes by key do not.
  - A temporary edit that sets the lanes back is the quickest proof a stop test is discriminating; save a copy of the file and restore it from the copy, and rebuild before the real run.
  - The two-partition case passed with eight lanes too (probably the final commit lost the race with the consumer's close; not established), so the skip shows reliably in the one-partition case only.
  - MassTransit's prefetch (`PrefetchCount = Math.Max(1000, CheckpointMessageCount / 10)`) is per Kafka consumer, apart from librdkafka's queue; `ConsumersPerEndpoint` multiplies it.

## 2026-10-25 ARV-177a: A host's own disposal never dead-letters a valid message (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Infra consume filters, tests, docs)

- The case, reproduced on a real broker before the fix: `InHandAtStopTests` with no retry (`RetryCount` 0), a 20 s attempt past an 11 s bus stop wait (shutdown 26 s, grace 31 s), a later record queued behind it. MassTransit cancels the message's token and its confirmation at the stop wait's end; the attempt runs on while the host disposes its services and fails at 20 s; being the last attempt, its failure reached `DeadLetterFilter`'s dead-letter path and kept a dead letter (one `outbox_message` row) for a valid event, which the next host's relay would send while that host processed the record as well. With one retry after the slow attempt (the first case) nothing was kept: MassTransit's retry does not retry once the message's token is cancelled.
- The fix: `DeadLetterFilter` takes a failure for the stop's (`IsTheStops`) when the message's own token is cancelled, whatever the failure and the attempt, or when its endpoint is stopping (`EndpointStopping.IsStopping`) and the failure's chain holds an `ObjectDisposedException` (`IsDisposal`: inner exceptions and aggregates, to a depth of 16 and at most 256 exceptions; past either the failure is dead-lettered, a copy rather than a loss). It then logs a Warning ("Message from {Topic} partition {Partition} offset {Offset} failed after its endpoint began to stop past it; not dead-lettered, it is delivered again after restart (ARV-177a)", with the failure) and throws the message's own cancellation, which MassTransit's retry passes on without another attempt and its receive pipe does not rescue, so the record is left unacknowledged; with one lane per consumer (ARV-253) nothing after it completes and it is not committed. A failure of the message's own while the endpoint stops, before the stop wait ends, is still dead-lettered and kept (ARV-171). The new catch sits after the message's own cancellation and before the retry limit's, so it applies to every attempt.
- Tests:
  - Unit `ConsumePipelineTests`: `Pipe_Should_LeaveTheMessageUnacknowledgedWithoutADeadLetter_When_ItFailsOnADisposedServiceWhileItsEndpointStops` (the attempt waits on a gate, the endpoint's Stopping event is seen, then the attempt fails: on a disposed service the receive faults as a cancellation and nothing is kept or sent; on an ordinary error the letter is kept and the message completes); `Send_Should_ThrowTheMessagesCancellationWithoutADeadLetter_When_TheMessagesTokenWasCancelledBeforeItFailed` (Moq: the last attempt fails after the token was cancelled; the cancellation carries that token, no letter sent or kept); `IsTheStops_Should_TakeADisposedServiceForTheStop_When_TheEndpointIsStoppingAndOnlyThen`; `IsDisposal_Should_FindADisposedService_When_ItIsInTheChainWithinItsDepth`. With `IsTheStops` disabled (a temporary edit restored from a saved copy) the pipe test's disposed case and the Moq test failed, the others passed.
  - Integration `InHandAtStopTests` is a theory over `RetryCount` 1 and 0 and now asserts no kept row and no letter on the dead-letter topic after the next host has run its relay; the 0 case kept one letter before the fix and none after. `QueuedAtStopTests`, `DeadLetterKeptAtStopTests` and `DeadLetterShutdownTests` pass unchanged (9 of 9 in the run with the fix).
- Docs: wiki 10 section 4.5a (the stop budget: the duplicate letter closed, the new Warning, and that a letter of an earlier stop may be such a duplicate but is replayed as any dead letter), the overview (Producing), ADR-0018 note of 2026-10-25 (ARV-177a), docs/security/cwe-controls.md (CWE-400: the residual closed, the tests), decisions.md (2026-10-25 entry and an open row).
- Security review: round 1 FAIL on one Medium, M1: wiki 10 called a dead letter of an earlier stop that names `ObjectDisposedException` or a timeout "a duplicate, not a loss", but a message whose last attempt fails for its own reasons at a stop (a timeout among them) is still dead-lettered and completes, and before ARV-253 a letter could be a record's only trace, so an operator could dismiss a valid event (now: it may be a duplicate, nothing tells it from a genuine one, replay it as any dead letter and the inbox drops it if applied). Lows fixed in the story: L2 the disposed-service theory gained a `RetryCount` 1 row and every row asserts one attempt (the cancellation is not retried); L3 `IsDisposal` looks at most at 256 exceptions besides its depth of 16, tested at depths 16 and 17 and with a 300-wide aggregate; L4 cwe-controls said the next host processes the record "once" (now "again, at least once"); L6 the integration test's dead-letter read fails unless it reaches the topic's end. Lows filed as ARV-255 (Phase 3): L1 MassTransit's cancel sites for a receive context (whether a revoke can cancel a record while its consumer keeps the partition) to be recorded, and `IsTheStops` narrowed if so; L5 the pipeline test's fixed 100 ms wait after the Stopping event to become a wait on a condition. Round 2: PASS (CWE-400, CWE-501; ASVS V15.2.2 and V16.2.5 still Partly, V16.3.4, V16.5.2 and V16.5.3 not weakened).
- Gates: `node scripts/verify.mjs story` (wide: Ariva.Infra's consume filters) on the reviewed code: every step PASS, among them unit tests (7,891) and their count guard, the security scan (0 errors), integration 789 passed and 1 skipped (`TimescaleSmokeTests`) with its count guard, E2E 923 passed with no secret in the artifacts. After the review's fixes: `node scripts/verify.mjs backend` PASS (unit 7,892), `InHandAtStopTests` 2 of 2, `node scripts/verify.mjs docs` PASS.
- Gotchas:
  - MassTransit's retry does not retry once the message's token is cancelled, so only a last attempt reached the dead-letter path at a stop: a test of this needs `RetryCount` 0 (or the slow attempt last).
  - A host's file logger is disposed with the host, so what an attempt does after the host's disposal is not in its log; assert on the database and the topics instead.

## 2026-10-26 ARV-178: Sensing resends: late receipt-timed resends and bounded declarative names (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Infra declarative mapper, tests, docs)

- Bounded names and ids (the ARV-174 security review's recommendation 1): `DeclarativeMapper.State.Id` (track ids) and `State.Name` (line and zone names) go through `Bounded`, which reads the value's raw UTF-8 length as written (`JsonMarshal.GetRawUtf8Value`, no copy) and copies it only when it is at most six bytes a character of the limit (an escape such as `\u00e9` is the most a character takes, six bytes), then refuses a decoded value longer than the canonical maximum (`CanonicalEventRules.MaxTrackIdLength` 64, `MaxNameLength` 200) as a format error naming the mapping path ("crossings[0].line is longer than 200 characters ($.line)."). A mapping that reads a name from the group (^) or the payload ($) reads it for every item, so before the bound a 500 KB group-level name under 2,000 items was copied 2,000 times (about 2 GB, refused only downstream by the canonical checks); now the first item refuses the message and the name is never copied whole.
- The late receipt-timed resend (the engineer's finding) is kept as a residual, as the criterion allows: a receipt-timed kind with a package, resent later than the queue zone's window (a lateness past its events, about three minutes), gets the first's batch id, which the archive drops for three days, but the zone has forgotten the batch and its events carry the new receipt time, so the live minutes count it again while a replay counts it once. Recognising it live would need a window as long as the archive's for such kinds, or the batch to say it is receipt-timed (a contract change). No shipped mapping stamps crossings at receipt, but `ouster-detect-v1` stamps its occupancy at receipt with a package (the frame count): an Ouster frame resent that late re-applies its occupancy readings live: a stale reading that holds an overflow band until the next one, or, if it reads zero while people queue, re-anchors the empty queue's FIFO for the people then held (their exits get no wait, more than 2 flag the waits that follow Degraded); stated in both places. Stated in formulas F5 (residual 3) and sensor-adapters.md (the Duplicates row), pinned by a test.
- Tests: `DeclarativeConformanceTests.Map_Should_RefuseANameOrIdLongerThanTheCanonicalMaximum_When_AMappingReadsOne` (a group-level zone name and a payload-level line name of 200 accepted and 201 refused, a track id of 65 refused), `Map_Should_CountAnEscapedCharacterOnce_When_ItMeasuresAName` (200 six-byte escapes accepted as 200 characters, 201 refused), `Map_Should_NotCopyAHugeSharedNamePerItem_When_TheMappingReadsItFromTheGroupOrThePayload` (a 500,000-character name under 2,000 items, group-level and payload-level: refused, under 500 KB allocated on a warmed second call, where one copy of the name is 1 MB); `ResentPushTests.Zone_Should_ApplyAReceiptTimedResendAgain_When_ItComesAfterTheZonesWindow` (the same id, the new receipt time, the zone's memory empty after the window, entries counted twice live, no repeated batch).
- Docs: sensor-adapters.md (the Values row: the length limits; the Duplicates row: the late resend's live and replay difference), formulas F5 (residual 3 tagged ARV-178 with its test), docs/security/cwe-controls.md (CWE-120: the bounded names and ids).
- Security review: round 1 FAIL on one Medium, R1: the residual's statement said no shipped mapping stamps at receipt, but `ouster-detect-v1` stamps its occupancy at receipt with a package, so the late resend's effect there (a stale reading taken as current) was unstated and the Duplicates row's "counted again" fitted crossings only (both corrected). Lows fixed in the story: L2 asvs-l2 V1.4.2's line reference into `DeclarativeMapper.cs` (135 to 138); L3 the comment's escape was written as the character itself (the tool that wrote the script decoded `\u00e9`; now the escape as text, and no non-ASCII in the added lines); L4 a costly-operations row for the mapper's bounds; L5 a surrogate-pair theory (100 escaped pairs accepted as 200 code units, 101 refused). Filed as ARV-256 (Phase 3): L1 filter and direction values read from the group or the payload are still copied per item (`Scalar`), and such numbers parsed again per item. Round 2: PASS (CWE-120, CWE-400, CWE-501), with one Low applied: a stale zero's FIFO re-anchor is for good for the people then held, not until the next reading (formulas F5 reworded).
- Gates: `node scripts/verify.mjs story --specs tests/api/device-push.spec.ts --integration "FullyQualifiedName~Sensing|FullyQualifiedName~Ingest|FullyQualifiedName~Resend"` on the reviewed code: every step PASS, among them build, unit tests and their count guard, the security scan (0 errors), the story-filtered integration tests, E2E 344 passed (device-push with the smoke set and the permission matrix) with no secret in the artifacts. After the review's fixes: `node scripts/verify.mjs backend` PASS (unit 7,903), `node scripts/verify.mjs docs` PASS, and the declarative and resend unit classes again on the final tree.
- Gotchas:
  - Text written through the file tool has its `\uXXXX` sequences decoded into the characters; build a backslash at run time (`chr(92)`) when a script must write an escape as text, and grep the added lines for non-ASCII before committing.
  - An allocation assertion needs a warmed second call measured outside the assertion library, and nothing else costly in the same message: crossings are mapped before occupancy, so 2,000 valid crossings in the payload counted a megabyte against the occupancy case.

## 2026-10-26 ARV-179: Monitoring metrics: bounded feed tags, the outbox count off the relay's path, and the gaps the pilot can live with (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Infra outbox relay, the chart's validation, tests, docs)

- Feed tags (the ARV-125a review's finding 1): already bound, by an earlier change, to who sends rather than what a request says. Every Integration API intake (the batch endpoints through `BatchCall.HandleAsync`, AIDX through `AidxController`) passes `IntegrationBatches.FeedOf(caller.ClientId)`, `api-` and the client's id; the ACRIS and AMAN pulls pass their administrator-registered endpoint's feed; schedule imports pass `ssim`. So a client adds at most one feed value per site, kind and outcome however many names it tries, and the meter's series are bounded by registered clients and endpoints. Proven now by `MetricTagTests.FlightItems_Should_BeTaggedWithTheClientsOwnFeed_When_ARequestNamesAnother`: the real `FlightFeedController` with an intake that counts its items into `FlightMetrics` as `SvcFlightIntake` does; a body naming a feed is refused (400, the batch read strictly), a `?feed=` query is not read, and both accepted batches count under the client's own feed. The class's summary says so.
- The outbox count (finding 2): `OutboxRelay` measured the backlog (`count(*)` of the unsent rows, 10 s bound) before each pass when due, so in a large backlog (after an outage, when draining matters) a slow count could hold a pass up to 10 s every 30 s. It now measures on a loop of its own (`MeasureLoopAsync` on a `PeriodicTimer` of `MeasureEvery`, started on its own task beside the passes and awaited when the relay stops), so no measurement ever runs on the passes' path; it can hold one more of the host's pooled connections meanwhile (within `Database:MaxPoolSize`), for up to its 10 s command plus the opening of the connection (at most the 15 s connect timeout). The relay's stop waits for a measurement at most `MeasureStopBound` (5 s), whatever the measurement does, so it never eats into the time the host's later services have to stop (the review's Low 1). `MeasureBacklog` (internal) lets a test measure its own way: `BacklogMetricsTests.Relay_Should_GoOnWithItsPasses_When_TheBacklogMeasurementDoesNotEnd` (a measurement that never answers; the relay runs at least ten passes after it started, where before it would have run none; the stop ends both), `Relay_Should_StopWithinItsBound_When_TheMeasurementIgnoresItsToken` (a measurement that does not take its token: the stop returns within the bound, with the relay's task ended) and `Relay_Should_GoOnMeasuring_When_AMeasurementFails` (the first measurement throws, the next is reported; `MeasureInterval`, internal, shortens the interval for it). With the bound removed and with the loop ending at a failure (temporary edits restored from a saved copy) those two failed and the others passed.
- The gaps (findings 3 to 5), taken as residuals as the criterion allows, stated in wiki 10 section 2a with what covers each: the AMAN feed alert reads a counter without a `site` tag, so with several border sites a stopped feed at one site is not alerted while another's flows (the pilot's one site is not affected; desk states turning sensor-derived show it; a per-site feed age gauge from the desk feed's heartbeat filed as ARV-257, before a second border site); the MassTransit consumer groups' lag comes only from the broker or the site collector's Kafka receiver (the AMAN feed alert, off by default, counts the records of every transport, so a stalled Kafka group does not fire it while REST or pull records arrive; no shipped rule covers a slow but running archive or domain event group); while the stream worker's reading is paused (a zone at its bound while its checkpoint fails) `ariva.stream.consumer_lag` stays flat: the database alert covers the database being away, while a checkpoint that fails with the database answering (a statement timeout, a lock wait, a state above 64 MiB) has only the worker's Error log (a checkpoint age gauge and rule filed as ARV-258).
- The story's note (the ARV-125b re-review's nit 1): an alert's empty `namespaces` list reads the release's namespace (`monitoring.yaml`), which `helm template --namespace` takes as given; `templates/validate.yaml` now checks it with the same Kubernetes name rule as a listed one. Chart test in `chart-security.mjs`: an empty list (through a values file: `--set namespaces={}` gives a list of one empty name) with the release namespace `Ariva_NS` is refused, and with `ariva-dev` renders.
- Docs: wiki 10 (section 2a: the outbox row's own loop and its bounds, the flights row's feed values, the known gaps; section 3.1: the release namespace check), wiki 04 section 6.9 (the relay's second connection), docs/security/costly-operations.md (the outbox row: the measurement's bounds, its own loop and the stop's wait; a new row for metric series: tag keys from the allowlist, values from bounded sets, the OpenTelemetry SDK's default limit of 2,000 tag combinations per instrument past them), the backlog (ARV-257, ARV-258 and ARV-259 added; ARV-179's notes no longer carry the alarm list, now ARV-259).
- Security review (security-reviewer, 2026-10-26): PASS, CWE-400, CWE-532 and CWE-501 checked, eight Lows. Fixed in the story: L1 (the stop's wait for a measurement bounded, with its test), L2 (a test that a failed measurement leaves the loop measuring; the passes counted from the measurement's start), L3 (wiki 10: the database alert covers the database being away; other checkpoint failures have only the log), L4 (wiki 10: the AMAN alert is off by default and counts every transport; no rule covers slow running groups), L5 (the relay's second connection in costly-operations and wiki 04, the bound with the connection's opening), L8 (the metric series row). To Phase 3: L3's gauge and rule and L6 (a test pinning AIDX's feed tag) as ARV-258; L7 (the wiki 10 section 3 alarms without rules, carried in ARV-179's notes) as ARV-259.

## 2026-10-26 ARV-183: Backup restore hardening: strict allowed signers, a restore preview and wider post-restore checks (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; scripts/ops, tests, docs)

- Allowed signers (CWE-345): `ariva-ops.mjs` reads `allowed_signers` by one strict grammar (`readAllowedSigners`: printable ASCII, spaces and tabs; plain principals; the `namespaces`, `valid-after`, `valid-before` and `cert-authority` options; a known key type and its key; an optional comment). Any other line is refused outright, whatever the options: ssh-keygen splits and unquotes lines in ways a looser reading does not see (a vertical tab or a no-break space inside the principals, a byte order mark before `#`, an escaped quote inside an option, a quoted principals field), so the review's first parser could be told `ops-a` while ssh-keygen read `ops-a\v,*` and verified a foreign key. A principal pattern (`*`, `?`, `!`) or a `cert-authority` line is refused unless `--allow-signer-patterns`. The key that verified is printed by its fingerprint.
- Preview and namespace: the signed manifest now names its namespace; a restore prints the verifying key, then the set's namespace, time taken (UTC), database and file before anything else, refuses a set of another namespace (or one from before ARV-183 that names none) unless `--force-namespace`, and `--plan` does the same verification on the operator's machine and prints the preview without touching the cluster. Options a command would not use are refused (`--force-namespace` and `--allow-signer-patterns` with `--sha256`, the check options with `files-restore` and the other commands).
- Wider post-restore checks (CWE-269), `ariva-db.sh check`: roles but the bootstrap superuser and the migration login with SUPERUSER, CREATEROLE, REPLICATION or BYPASSRLS, login or not, and any role, the migration login included, that holds such a role or one of PostgreSQL's server, data or signal roles through any chain of grants (`powerful`, a recursive `held`); Ariva's group roles holding any role; role settings but the runtime login's statement timeout; ALTER SYSTEM settings (`pg_file_settings`, read as the superuser); rules but a view's; functions outside the extensions in any schema but Ariva's own with a body its scripts ship (`ARIVA_FUNCTIONS`, name:SHA-256 of every body, older bodies a later script replaced included, held equal to the scripts by `OpsScriptTests`); objects added to plpgsql; system functions replaced in place (fingerprints against template1, or postgres); publications and subscriptions; and `planted_objects` (ARV-236's functions and operators under system names and database settings). A DBA-provided server's own extension, login and setting pass when named with `--allow-extension` (which `check-dump` now takes too), `--allow-login` and `--allow-setting`.
- The superuser read (the review's High): every superuser session of the script has its search path pinned to `pg_catalog` by a startup option (`as_superuser`), which no database or role setting overrides; the read names nothing through the search path; it runs only when `planted_objects` finds nothing (a failed read of that is a FAIL too); check's own report and the restore's catalog reads run as the migration login with the same pinned path; the restore mode functions are named with their schema.
- Security review round 1 (security-reviewer, 2026-10-26): FAIL. H1 (CWE-269, CWE-427): the first version's read (`string_agg` and `LIKE`, unqualified) ran with the database's search path, which the migration login (the database owner) can set with ALTER DATABASE ... SET; the reviewer planted an aggregate in a schema of its own, set that schema first, and `check` made the login a superuser while printing ok. M1: privileged roles reached through membership and PostgreSQL's server roles (`pg_execute_server_program` on the runtime role passed). M2: the allowed-signers parser evaded by control characters, non-ASCII spaces and escaped quotes. M3: functions replaced in place, hidden in plpgsql, and Ariva-named functions with any body. M4: docs claimed more than the checks did. M5: `--allow-extension` did not reach `check-dump`; no way to allow a login or a setting. Six Lows (no preview without restoring, unused options accepted, the label printed raw, test gaps, a loose regex, settings outside `postgresql.auto.conf`).
- Fixes: as above. Residuals filed as ARV-262 and named in the CWE-269 row: an object added to the TimescaleDB extensions, settings written outside `postgresql.auto.conf`, a forged dump that also changes template1, and triggers or constraints left out (integrity, not privilege; the proposal is a schema comparison with a fresh migration).
- Security review round 2 (2026-10-26): PASS for CWE-269 and CWE-345, no new finding. The reviewer pressed the pinned session (no database or role setting a non-superuser can make steers it: every database setting is a planted line, and the bootstrap superuser's role settings are out of a CREATEROLE login's reach), the planted filter (each other line starts with a fixed word, so no setting can pass as an extension line), the template1 comparison (identical across a cluster's databases of one version; a dump restores into its own database only), the signer grammar (it accepts the documented form) and the docs (no claim beyond the checks). Observations recorded: the allow options are by name only (`--allow-setting work_mem` clears that setting for every role and the database), which is safe because the one dangerous setting, the search path, is pinned on the superuser session whatever is allowed; the grammar refuses rare but valid ssh-keygen forms with a clear message; the residuals stay behind the signed manifest (ARV-262).
- Tests: `ariva-ops.mjs --self-test` (189 checks: the grammar's cases with the review's evasions, the preview with `--plan` starting nothing, `--plan` refusing another namespace's set, a files archive of a set without a namespace refused, unused options refused, the end-to-end evasions with a manifest signed by a foreign key); `OpsScriptTests` (9: every shipped function body pinned, the extractor ignoring comments, strings and DO bodies, the five superuser statements and the pinned search path); `BackupRestoreTests` (every new line ok on a clean restore; each plant reported; the allow options; a superuser read that fails; the search path hijack reported, nothing read as the superuser, the login unchanged); `ExtensionUpdateTests` (its final check passes with the new lines).
- Mutation checks (from saved copies): without the signer refusal, the vertical-tab line lets a manifest signed by a foreign key restore as ops-a (self-test fails); with the planted guard, the pinned search path and the qualified statement all removed, the hijack makes the migration login a superuser (BackupRestoreTests fails on it); with the guard and the pin removed but the qualified statement kept, or the guard and the qualification removed but the pin kept, the login stays as it was (each layer holds alone); with check's report on an unpinned session, the planted count(*) turns the event trigger line ok (BackupRestoreTests fails).
- Gates: `node scripts/verify.mjs story --integration "FullyQualifiedName~BackupRestoreTests|FullyQualifiedName~ExtensionUpdateTests"` (build, unit 7,943, security scan, the ops self-test, chart tests, audits, docs rules, the story's integration tests, E2E smoke set), all PASS. Two earlier unscoped runs (the full integration suite) failed only because the session's disk allowance ran out: PostgreSQL's "could not extend file ... No space left on device" (53100) and crash recovery (57P03) in tests this story does not touch; the free space fell to 58 MB in one backtest seed and to 1 MB in the full suite. The owner chose to delete the E2E host logs of 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-24; the full suite runs at the next checkpoint, which needs more disk than this session has left.
- Gotchas: each E2E run keeps about 150 MB of host logs in `Platform/Testing/Ariva.E2E/logs` (git-ignored, never pruned), which filled this session's disk over five days of gates; check `df` before a full suite. PostgreSQL resolves functions and operators through the session's search path even for a superuser, and a database owner can set that path for every session of its database; a startup option (PGOPTIONS) wins over database and role settings. pg_catalog is searched first only when the path does not name it; a path that names a schema before pg_catalog shadows the system's names. ssh-keygen splits allowed-signers fields on space, tab, CR and LF only and honours quotes and backslash escapes; JavaScript's `\s` and `trim()` do not match that. Since PostgreSQL 16 a CREATEROLE login holds the roles it creates with the admin option, so role reach must count every grant.

## 2026-10-26 ARV-188: story gate runs the visual suite when the web app changes

- What changed: `scripts/verify.mjs` `VISUAL_RELEVANT`: the story gate runs the visual project, before its E2E specs as a checkpoint does (the baselines expect the demo seed), when the change touches `Platform/Frontplane/Ariva.Web`, the visual suite and its baselines (`tests/visual`), the support code it imports (`tests/support`), its browser script (`scripts/visual-browser.mjs`), the E2E configuration that declares the project (`playwright.config.ts`) or the Playwright pin the image must match (`package.json`, `package-lock.json`); otherwise it records a skipped step. Every `verify.mjs` visual step (story gate, `visual` scope, checkpoint) first runs `node scripts/visual-browser.mjs ensure`: the pinned image is reused when Docker has it and pulled otherwise (30 minutes at most), and the step fails with one printable line of the reason when Docker is not reachable or the pull is refused. A failed `start` is recorded as a failed step (it used to throw out of the gate) and stops any container it left. Docs: docs/harness/test-cadence.md (a story gate row, the paragraph on the image, fresh services and the reason for the step, checkpoint step 3), wiki 16.
- Evidence for the criteria: `node scripts/verify.mjs story --plan` with `visual-browser.mjs` changed lists `visual browser image (the pinned Playwright image, reused or pulled)` and `visual regression (pinned image)` before the E2E specs; the pattern was checked against the web app, the suite, its support code, the configuration and package files (visual) and an API spec, another E2E script and a backend file (none). `ensure` was run three ways: with the image present (reused, exit 0), with Docker unreachable (`DOCKER_HOST` at a missing socket: "Docker is not available ..." and exit 3), and from a scratch copy pinned to a digest that does not exist ("the pinned Playwright image ... is not on this machine and could not be pulled ..." and exit 3). CI's own visual step (`ci.yml`) still calls `start` directly.
- Gates: `node scripts/verify.mjs story` (build, unit 7,973, security scan and self-tests, chart tests and release guards, audits, docs rules, no persistence change, the new visual step with the image reused and 20 screenshots passing, E2E 341 in 5 spec files with the smoke set), all PASS. After the review's fixes, `node scripts/verify.mjs visual` on fresh services: the image step and 20 screenshots PASS, the browser container stopped afterwards; `ensure` re-run the three ways above.
- Security review: PASS (CWE-78/77, CWE-94, CWE-501 at Docker's error text, CWE-269 for the container; scan 0 errors). Three Lows fixed: the failed `start` now stops a container left listening (an unauthenticated Playwright server whose endpoint the error had printed); Docker's error line is printed once, at most 300 characters, with any character outside printable ASCII escaped (the text can come from a registry); the pattern also covers `playwright.config.ts`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and `tests/support` (a Playwright bump or support change would otherwise pass the gate and fail only in CI). Info: the wiki now says every `verify.mjs` visual step runs `ensure` (CI's calls `start`).
- Gotchas: `execFileSync` without a `stdio` option copies the child's stderr to the parent as well as returning it on the error, so printing `error.stderr` doubles it; pass `stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']`. The visual step adds about 3 to 4 minutes to a web story's gate and needs fresh services, as the checkpoint's does.
