## 2026-10-26 ARV-245: Outbox relay: a broker-unavailable streak escalates, and passes wait while the brokers do not answer (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Ariva.Infra messaging, chart monitoring, tests, docs)

- Streak (CWE-400 detection): since ARV-165 a broker-unavailable failure counts no attempt, so a row whose partition has no leader while the brokers answer warned for ever and never reached "stuck after N attempts". `OutboxBrokerStreaks` (in the relay's memory) notes each such failure per row and reports the row once when its streak reaches `Kafka:Outbox:BrokerStreakMinutes` (default 15, validated 1 to 1,440 at start, `MessagingExtensions.EnsureProducerSettings`): an Error naming the row's topic and the streak's length (in place of that try's Warning) and `ariva.outbox.broker_streaks` (counter, meter `Ariva.Outbox`, tag `topic` through `OutboxMetrics.TopicTag`: a `KafkaTopics` constant or its dead-letter topic, else `unknown`). A send or a failure of the row's own ends the streak; a streak not seen for an hour is forgotten and at most 10,000 rows are followed. Each relay keeps its own streaks, so a row can be reported once by each relay that leads through its streak. New SigNoz rule `outboxBrokerStreak` (warning, 15 minute window; `values.yaml`, `tests/monitoring.json`).
- Waiting for the brokers: after a pass meets the broker's absence the relay asks `IOutboxTransport.BrokersAnswerAsync` (the Kafka transport: the producer's cached probe, the readiness check's, at most one cluster description a second) before each pass and skips the pass while no broker answers (`RelayPass.WaitingForBrokers`: no connection, lock or claim), logging the wait and the resumption once each; the backlog is still measured on its own loop. Once the probe answers, passes resume and every row is due within the broker retry; passes no longer ask the probe until one meets the absence again.
- Security review round 1 (security-reviewer, 2026-10-26): FAIL. M1 (CWE-400): the cached probe had no bound of Ariva's own (only librdkafka's request timeout), so a description that never ended (its client retired under it after a fatal error) would keep the shared task incomplete and the relay skipping its passes for good. Fixed: `ProbeAsync` bounds the description at its timeout and `ProbeSlack` (1 s), one bound for the client's description and a test's (round 2's optional point a, after which a mutant without the bound fails the unit test). M2: the production transport's probe path was untested (an interface default of true would hide a regression). Fixed: unit tests through `IOutboxTransport` on `KafkaOutboxTransport` (not started, answering, not answering, no handle, cancelled) and `ImplicitTopicTests` on the live broker. M3: the runbook said the other topics carry on behind a leaderless partition; an event row's broker failure ends each pass at that row and the row is due again by then, so the whole outbox waits (head of line): docs corrected, the CWE-400 row updated, the residual filed as ARV-264 (hold only that topic). L4: stale runbook lines (passes "continue during an outage", "the leading relay", streaks while skipped) and the overview corrected. L5: a vacuous leader-lock assertion removed, the skip test asserts no probe after the brokers answer. Round 2: PASS for CWE-400, CWE-501 (the bounded topic tag), CWE-117/532 (the new lines carry the same fields as the existing Warning, no payload or key) and CWE-89 (no production SQL); optional points b (streak wording) and c (ASVS V16.5.2 evidence) taken.
- Tests: unit `OutboxBrokerStreaksTests` (7: once at the streak, not before, ended by a send or own failure, a new streak reported again, rows on their own, forget after an hour, at most 10,000), `ProducerHardeningTests` (streak setting bounds; the probe bounded and asked afresh; the transport's gate; cancellation), `MetricTagTests` (the counter driven, its topic tag); integration `OutboxRelayTests` (23, three new: the Error and the count once after the streak and not before; the streak started again after the row's own failure; passes skipped and the backlog measured while the probe says no, resumed after, no probe asked then), `ImplicitTopicTests` (the transport's answer on the live broker and without one), and the fault tests that drive the real probe through an outage, `BrokerOutageTests` (its log shows the skip and the resumption) and `CommitRaceTests` (every key resumes within 25 s of the restore). Mutants from saved copies: the skip off and a row's own failure not ending its streak fail the two targeted relay tests; the probe without its bound fails the probe test.
- Gates: `node scripts/verify.mjs story` on the final tree widened to the full suites (the chart's monitoring files changed): build, unit 8,001, security scan and self-tests, chart tests and release guards, audits, docs rules, E2E 923 (API and functional), all PASS. Its full integration run failed only because the session's disk allowance ran out (free space down to 3.6 MB; the shared PostgreSQL container went into recovery, 57P03, and 666 database tests failed with it). With the git-ignored E2E host logs of 10-25 and 10-26 deleted (2.4 GB, the owner's approval of 2026-10-26) and this session's own scratch (0.6 GB), the integration suite then ran on the same tree namespace by namespace (23 processes, each with its own containers): 806 of 806 pass, free space never below 2.7 GB. Earlier, on the reviewed tree: `OutboxRelayTests` 23, `ImplicitTopicTests` 3, `BrokerOutageTests` 1, `CommitRaceTests` 3.
- Gotchas: a whole integration suite in one process keeps every fixture's containers for the run and needs several GB of free disk here; namespace by namespace it fits in under 1.5 GB. A cached shared task (the probe) needs a bound of its own, not only each caller's wait: a caller that times out leaves the task, and the next caller gets the same stranded task. `Task.WaitAsync` on an already completed task returns it even with a cancelled token, so a cancellation test needs a task still running. Tests that build a new relay per pass lose its in-memory state; the streak tests keep one relay. `RecordingTransport` answers the probe true by default, so the existing relay tests keep their behaviour.

A chain that also asserted plain text keeps the plain part, after the secret's boolean (the first failure is the one printed). A secret: by name (ending in Password, Secret, Credential, a compound Token such as AccessToken but not CancellationToken, Jwt, ApiKey, the key kinds, RecoveryCode, TotpCode, TotpSeed, TotpUri, a number after it included; a variable named `token`); an index, range, substring or element of one; a concatenation, interpolation, `??` or `?:` that carries one; a call that issues one, computes a TOTP code (`Code`, `CodeNow`, `Totp.Code`) or reads a protected value back (`Unprotect`, `Decrypt`); read from the source, a secret JSON member (`GetProperty("clientSecret")`), a secret header (`GetValues("X-TOTP-Code")`, `X-Api-Key`) or the Authorization header; flags and messages about one (`MustChangePassword`, `InvalidCredentials`) are not. Self-test: 61 bad patterns, 56 good ones, a real file found on its line. `expect-messages.mjs` (TypeScript) gains the matcher rule: an expect's (or `expect.soft`'s) subject and its matcher's arguments (`expect.poll`'s arguments only) may not be a secret (`secretValue`: a secret-named member or variable, a variable whose latest binding is one, an element, part or encoding of one, a template, concatenation, `??`, `||` or `?:` carrying one, a call named for one such as `refreshCookie()` or `totpCode(...)`, a binding of a `process.env` key, secret, password, token or seed, the text of an element that reveals one, `credential-value`, `credential-reveal`, `totp-secret`, `recovery-codes`, a request's `authorization` or `cookie` header), unless the matcher prints nothing of it (`toBeTruthy`, `toBeDefined`, `not.toBeNull`, `not.toBeUndefined`, `not.toBeFalsy`); and a web-first text matcher on an element that reveals a secret is a finding too; its self-test holds 94 bad and 69 good patterns (one former good one, `not.toContain(account.password)`, is bad now). - Gotchas: the security scan's SEC-041 refuses `==` and `!=` on a Secret, Password, ApiKey or TotpCode name in tests too, so a test compares those with `string.Equals(a, b, StringComparison.Ordinal)`. FluentAssertions' `ContainKey(...).WhoseValue.Should().Be(x)` prints the value: read it with the indexer after `ContainKey`. `WithMessage` is a case-insensitive wildcard match: its stand-in after a boolean is `MatchEquivalentOf`. A Set-Cookie header asserted with `toContain('httponly')` prints the cookie with its token. Loop variables named `secret` that hold no secret were renamed to `value`. ## 2026-10-26 ARV-250: Uploads: a per-user limit on every upload, and the site configuration import's lock waited for a bounded time (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Api.Main, Api.Common, Infra, tests, docs)

- Why (CWE-400, CWE-770): the `upload` policy lets a host take one upload at a time, and only the CSV imports (ARV-155) were counted per user, so one user looping 20 MB floor plan or SSIM uploads, site configuration transfers or advertisements held the host's one upload permit for long stretches; the site configuration import took the site's row lock with no timeout while it held that permit.
- Limit: ARV-155's filter generalised. `UploadLimitAttribute(kind)` and `UploadRateLimiter` (`Ariva.Api.Main/Controllers/AdminArea/Uploads`, replacing `CsvImportLimitAttribute` and `CsvImportRateLimiter`) count per user (id, else the test scheme's name; 403 for neither) and kind: `csv-preview` and `csv-commit` (both CSV imports), `floor-plan`, `flight-schedule-preview`, `flight-schedule-import`, `site-configuration-export`, `site-configuration-import`, `advertising-media`. A sliding window per replica (`SlidingWindowRateLimiter`, the story's note): a permit is free again one window after its segment began, so at most the limit in any stretch one segment shorter than the window, where the fixed window let twice it through across its end. Settings `Security:RateLimiting:CsvImports` (6 in 600 s, 60 segments) and the new `Security:RateLimiting:Uploads` (10 in 600 s, 60 segments) as `SlidingWindowSettings`, refused at start out of bounds (a window of at most a day, 1 to 600 segments of a second at least). The filter is a resource filter of order -1: after authorization (a refused or forged caller spends nobody's allowance) and before the steady upload's and the advertisement upload's reads, so a refused request reads no body; 429 with Retry-After (the window and a margin, 610 s by default: a sliding window's refused lease names no time, and the partitioned limiter replenishes on a 100 ms tick, so the margin is one segment or a tenth of a second a segment, whichever is more) and a fixed text (`CsvImportErrors.TooManyImports` for the CSV kinds, `UploadLimitAttribute.TooManyUploads` for the rest), logged as 9129 `LimitReached`. Every endpoint of the policy declares 429. The advertisement upload keeps its own per-person window (30 in 10 minutes, counted once the file is read).
- Lock: `SvcSiteConfiguration` takes the site's row through `SvcDb.TryLockSiteAsync` with `SiteConfigurationLimits.SiteLockWait` (5 s) and answers `SiteConfigurationErrors.SiteBusy` (409, in `Conflicts`) past it, audited as refused in its own transaction, the request's unit of work rolled back; its private `LockSiteAsync` and `LockRow` are gone.
- Tests: unit `UploadLimitTests` (per endpoint: two allowed, the third 429 with Retry-After and the fixed text before the service, another user apart; a malformed body refused 429 unread past the limit and 400 within it; kinds and the CSV window apart; a caller refused for want of a second factor not counted; the import's SiteBusy 409; the inventory: every endpoint of the policy carries the limit with its kind and no other does; settings, `TryAcquire`, `CallerOf`, defaults), `CsvImportLimitTests` on the new attribute, `RequestTimeoutsTests` start-up refusals of out-of-bounds windows; integration `SiteConfigurationTests.Import_Should_AnswerSiteBusyAfterTheWait_When_AnotherTransactionHoldsTheSiteLonger` (`SiteHolder` holds the row: waits the 5 s, SiteBusy, nothing written, audited refused, the same bundle imports once free), and the concurrent import test accepts SiteBusy beside SiteNotEmpty for a loser. E2E: `Security__RateLimiting__Uploads__PermitLimit` 10000 in `playwright.config.ts`, as for the CSV imports.
- Docs: costly-operations section 7 (the new paragraph, the export, floor plan, SSIM, CSV, site configuration import and advertisement rows), wiki 04 (the CsvImports row, the new Uploads row), wiki 13a section 1, asvs-l2 V15.2.2 and V16.3.3.
- Security review: round 1 FAIL on the stated bound (Medium): the docs and comments said the limit bounds how long one user holds the host's one upload permit, but the `upload` policy's queue is taken before authentication, so one user's three slow 20 MB transfers hold the permit and both waiting places for about 33 minutes at about one request per kind every 11 minutes, far under the limit. Fixed by stating what the limit caps (the transfers a user starts), recording the residual as costly-operations section 15 item 17 and in the V15.2.2 evidence, and filing ARV-265 (a per-user share of the permit and its queue, taken after authentication); wiki 13a's "in any 10 minutes" corrected to 590 s. Its recommended points taken too: upper bounds on the window settings, Retry-After of the window and one segment, a 403 case (a role without the permission spends no allowance), and the docs saying the bundle's malformed case is refused before model binding. Round 2 PASS for CWE-400 and CWE-770 (and V15.2.2, V16.3.3, V15.1.3 evidence accurate); its two optional notes taken: the Retry-After margin is the larger of one segment and a tenth of a second a segment (the partitioned limiter's 100 ms tick, which a window of many short segments could outrun), and the CSV row says the count caps the transfers started, with item 17.
- Gates: the touched unit classes (184, `UploadLimitTests` 29 of them) and integration `SiteConfigurationTests` (19) first; then `node scripts/verify.mjs story` (wide: Ariva.Api.Common, the E2E configuration and the web's shared code, so the full suites): build, unit 8,034, the security step, docs rules, web, integration 806 (one skipped), visual 20, E2E 923, the artifact checks, all PASS. The checkpoint on 6c07ea5 ran green before it (5b71601).
- Gotchas: the checkpoint's visual and E2E steps build the hosts from the working tree (`scripts/build-backend.mjs`), so a story's uncommitted code leaks into a checkpoint still running: park the changes (copied to the scratchpad, the tree put back to HEAD) until the E2E step has built and started its hosts. A sliding window's refused lease carries no RetryAfter metadata. The park script's restore used `shutil.copy2`, which keeps the files' old times, so MSBuild took Core and Infra as up to date against the checkpoint's newer build of HEAD (CS0117 in the tests only): touch restored files.

## 2026-10-26 ARV-251: Test counts: every row of a theory listed once accounted for (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; scripts, test projects, docs)

- Why (test integrity): the count guard (ARV-164a) compares a run's TRX with the test executable's listing method by method, but xUnit lists a theory whose data it cannot serialize once and runs all its rows under that one case, so a lost row of such a theory, while another of its rows ran, passed (60 methods: 59 unit with 716 results, 1 integration with 12).
- Choice: the criterion's second option, a committed row count per method. Serializable data would have meant rewriting about 25 test files whose rows are delegates, entities or settings objects. `theory-rows.json` beside each test project (copied beside the executable by a `None` item) names each theory listed once with its rows. The guard reads it beside the dll (`--rows` with a saved `--list`) and fails on fewer results than the file says, more, an entry for a method listed by its rows, any method that ran more rows than it was listed with and has no entry, and on a whole (unfiltered) run an entry for a method not listed; a filtered run's listing names only what it selected, so there the stale-entry rule is off. A missing, empty, doubled or malformed row file fails; the self-test (62 checks) runs the command line itself as a child process against temporary files for those exits.
- Kept current: `TheoryRows` (one source, `Ariva.UnitTests/Setup/TheoryRows.cs`, linked into the integration project) counts each entry's rows from its `InlineData`, `MemberData` and `ClassData` by reflection, reports any other data attribute, a method named twice and an unknown theory, and refuses a test or data row under a display name of its own (the guard matches by the name before the parenthesis); each project's `TheoryRowsTests` runs it, and the unit one proves the counting and the refusals on sample theories (one listed once with two member data attributes, which is itself in the file) and on constructed attributes and rows. The reflection counts agree with every count taken from the last full runs' TRX files.
- Docs: wiki 16 section 2 (the guard's limits, the row file), test-cadence, cwe-controls row 4, the CI workflow's comment.
- Security review: round 1 FAIL on the docs only (wiki 16 still said the guard could not see a lost row), with six recommended points, all taken: a method with more results than listed cases and no entry is a problem whatever its name; display names of tests, data attributes and rows refused across each assembly; duplicate keys refused on both sides; the command line's fail-closed exits self-tested; stale entries reported on whole runs; one counter source linked into both projects; refused keys printed escaped. Round 2 PASS (no CWE touched), on the condition that the gate's unit count guard passes on the real suite, which it did; its optional notes taken: the one case still unseen named in the header and wiki 16, a plainer message for a nested object, the 100,000 cap on the C# side.
- Gates: `node scripts/verify.mjs story` with `--integration "FullyQualifiedName~TheoryRowsTests|FullyQualifiedName~AdvertisingPolicyServiceTests"`: build, unit 8,053 and its count guard on the whole executable (7,394 cases in 3,232 methods, 60 theories held to their rows, none left out: the new rules' first real run), the security step, docs rules, integration (filter) 34 with its guard (1 theory), E2E 5 spec files 341, all PASS. After review round 2's optional edits: the guard's self-test 62 of 62, both `TheoryRowsTests` (20 and 1 results) with the count guard on each.
- Gotchas: xUnit 3.0.1's `IDataAttribute.GetData` answers an empty array outside its own pipeline (the member held two rows), so the counter reads the attributes itself. A lambda in a collection expression for `TheoryData<Func<int>>` binds to `TheoryDataRow<T>` (CS1660): use typed delegate fields. ## 2026-10-26 ARV-254: A rider endpoint held by one message is visible and bounded (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Infra messaging, Di, chart, docs)

- Why (CWE-400, three lows of the ARV-253 review): since ARV-253 each MassTransit topic endpoint's Kafka consumer handles one record at a time, so a record that retries, stalls or waits for a refused dead letter holds every partition its consumer reads. Nothing alerted on such a hold, `RetryCount` had no bound of its own, and librdkafka's `max.poll.interval.ms` (300 s, not set by the rider) could be shorter than the hold.
- Finding (decompiled MassTransit.KafkaIntegration 8.5.11, then a real broker): `KafkaMessageConsumer.Consume` polls a record, waits for a slot of its prefetch (`PrefetchCount`, 1,000), then hands it to its lane, so once the records fetched behind a held one fill the prefetch the loop stops polling. `HeldConsumerTests` (a rider of its own: prefetch 2, 6 s session, a 20 s hold): with an 8 s poll interval the held record was handled twice (the consumer left its group and was given it again after the rebalance), with 40 s once.
- Bounded: `Kafka:Consumers:RetryCount` 0 to 10 at start. A dead letter the broker refuses is tried for a one minute window (`DeadLetterRetry.SendWindow`; the wait before the window's last attempt cut to what is left of it) and then kept in the outbox as at a stop (ARV-171), so the record completes ("... refused for its whole send window; kept in the outbox, which sends it later"); only when the outbox refuses it too is the broker tried for another window. `ConsumerSettings.LongestHold` (attempts at the handler timeout, the retry waits, the window, one more send of up to 45 s, the 10 s keep) is 410 s at the defaults, and every rider consumer's `MaxPollInterval` is that and a minute (470 s); a host refuses to start when it would pass a day, librdkafka's largest. Past the bound only: broker and outbox both refusing, a handler ignoring its token (ARV-096e), the inbox rollback after a cut (no token, the database client's timeouts).
- Visible: a receive filter on each topic endpoint (`KafkaConsumerHolds`, `ConfigureReceive` with `UseFilter`, so it spans the retry, the handler timeout, the inbox, the dead letter and the unreadable path) feeds the gauge `ariva.kafka.consumer_hold_seconds` by topic and group (tags from the registration only); chart rule `consumerHeld` (above `holdLimit` 420 s for 2 minutes; `holdLimit` a whole number of seconds from 60 to 86,400 in validate.yaml).
- Trade-off recorded: the poll interval is also the group's rebalance timeout, so a held member can delay its group's rebalance (a rolling update included) for up to 470 s at the defaults (300 before).
- Docs: wiki 10 sections 2, 2a (and its known gaps), 3.1, the dead-letter bullet of 4.5a and new 4.24; wiki 04 `Kafka:Consumers`; overview Producing; ADR-0018 (the ARV-253 note's sentence and a note of 2026-10-26); cwe-controls CWE-400 (control and tests); asvs-l2 V15.2.2 evidence; the kafka-streaming skill.
- Security review: round 1 FAIL, one Medium: the window was checked on one read of the clock and the wait cut on another, so a window ending between the two reads gave a negative wait that `Task.Delay` refuses, and the record would have been acknowledged with no letter. Fixed by one read per iteration, with a test proven against the two-read code (it threw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`). Four Lows (the CWE-400 test column, the dead-letter filter's stale XML docs, the other ways past the longest hold, the rebalance trade-off) fixed; recommended items taken (the day bound with its test, the V15.2.2 evidence, the outbox's load in runbook 4.24); not taken: a pipe-level test of the window path (the same return as ARV-171's keep, covered by its pipe tests). Round 2 PASS (CWE-400); its informational note (negative retry intervals, older than this story) filed as ARV-266.
- Gates: `node scripts/verify.mjs story` with `--integration "FullyQualifiedName~HeldConsumerTests|FullyQualifiedName~DeadLetter|FullyQualifiedName~KafkaPipelineTests"` (wide: Infra messaging and Di, so the full suites), after review round 1's fixes: build, unit 8,070 with the count guard on the whole executable, the security step, chart security (the holdLimit cases), docs rules, integration 811 (one skipped) with its guard, E2E 923, the artifact checks, all PASS. A first run on the round 1 code passed through the chart and security steps and was stopped as its integration suite started, to test the fix instead. The affected unit classes ran ten times in a row green (67 tests) after the clock change; the negative-wait test failed against the two-read code as expected.
- Gotchas: a `TimeProvider` sped up a thousand times on real timers (the first window tests) is flaky as soon as a wait is cut to a remainder: .NET truncates a timer's due time to whole milliseconds and may fire one early, which that clock turns into a second, so extra attempts crowded in before the window ended (1 run in 4). A clock that steps by the timers made on it (each moves it by its due time and fires at once) is exact. MassTransit's Kafka endpoint configurator has no `ConnectReceiveObserver`; `ConfigureReceive(r => r.UseFilter(...))` wraps the whole receive, rescue and dead-letter pipes included. A `*Seconds` field in the chart's alert values is derived from `*Days`/`*Hours`, so the rule's own limit is named `holdLimit`.

## 2026-10-27 ARV-255: MassTransit's cancel sites recorded, and the pipeline stop test waits on a condition (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Infra messaging, tests, docs)

- Why (CWE-400, two lows of the ARV-177a review): `DeadLetterFilter.IsTheStops` takes any failure after the message's own token was cancelled for the stop's (no dead letter, the record left for the next consumer). That is right only while MassTransit cancels a Kafka receive context when its consumer stops and never while the consumer keeps the partition; whether a revoke or a lost partition could cancel a record in hand was not recorded. And the ARV-177a pipeline test waited a fixed 100 ms for the endpoint's own `EndpointStopping`.
- Established from the decompiled source (MassTransit and MassTransit.KafkaIntegration 8.5.11, net10.0): a receive context's token is its own and is cancelled only by `BaseReceiveContext.Cancel`, from `PendingReceiveLockContext.Cancel`, from `ConsumerAgent.CancelPendingConsumers`, which runs on any stop of the consumer agent (the bus's stop, a restart after a broker error, a sibling consumer's stop, Ariva's stop of a skipped endpoint); `TrySetConsumeCanceled` and `TrySetConsumeException` reach it only with a manual consume task, which the Kafka consumer does not use. A revoke (`OnUnAssigned`) closes the partition's checkpointer, whose dispose waits for every confirmation it was given and commits them; a lost partition cancels the checkpointer first and the record in hand runs on (a duplicate for the next owner, never a loss). So `IsTheStops` is not narrowed. Recorded in an ADR-0018 note and in `IsTheStops`' doc.
- Shown on a real broker: `RevokedInHandTests` (two riders of their own in one group, a two-partition topic; host A holds a record 12 s, host B joins 2 s into it): the group is seen rebalancing while the record is in hand, its token is never cancelled, every delivery is noted on entry and the record is delivered once, the partition's committed offset is past it, and B then consumes a partition of its own.
- The ARV-177a theory now waits until the endpoint's own `EndpointStopping` has seen the stop (`KafkaEndpoints.AllStopping`, internal, read-only, no production caller; polled every 5 ms within 10 s and asserted), with no fixed delay; the bus-level observer it used is gone.
- The cost, written down (ADR-0018, CWE-400, ASVS V15.2.2, runbook 4.24 item 4): a revoke holds the consumer's poll and the group's rebalance until the records in hand and queued for the revoked partitions complete (up to the prefetch), so a rolling update or scale out during a hold stalls the group, bounded by ARV-254's poll interval.
- Security review: round 1 FAIL, two Mediums in the new test: the slow record was noted only after its hold, so a redelivery after the rebalance could go unseen; and nothing checked that the rebalance overlapped the hold. Fixed (every delivery noted on entry, only the first held; the committed offset read through the admin client; the group described until it is seen rebalancing with the record still in hand, asserted); the stall cost documented; `IsTheStops`' doc names every stop of the consumer agent. Round 2 PASS (CWE-400), with one Low on wording (the docs credited the test with measuring the revoke's wait, which it cannot, since nothing is produced for B before the hold ends): reworded to credit the source.
- Gates: `node scripts/verify.mjs story` with `--integration "FullyQualifiedName~RevokedInHandTests|FullyQualifiedName~HeldConsumerTests|FullyQualifiedName~DeadLetter"` (wide: Infra messaging, so the full suites), on the final code: build, unit 8,070 with the count guard on the whole executable, the security step, chart security, docs rules, integration 812 (one skipped) with its guard, E2E 923, the artifact checks, 32 steps PASS. Two earlier runs were stopped (the first when review round 1 changed the test, the second by a container restart in its E2E step after unit and integration had passed). `RevokedInHandTests` alone passed 3 of 3 before round 1 and 3 of 3 after it (the group seen rebalancing at 4.8 to 4.9 s, the hold ending at 14.7 to 14.8 s, partition 0 committed at 2 past the slow record at 0); `ConsumePipelineTests` 5 of 5.
- Not done (outside the criteria): the ARV-171 pipeline test still waits a fixed 200 ms "into the first retry wait" (`ConsumePipelineTests`), a candidate for the ARV-156 follow-up.
- Gotchas: a revoke in MassTransit's Kafka rider drains rather than cancels: the poll thread waits inside `OnUnAssigned` for the partition's confirmations, so the whole group's rebalance waits for the slowest record in hand. When a test holds a record and checks it was handled once, note deliveries on entry, or a redelivery that lands during the settle is invisible. B's `StartAsync` returning does not mean it has joined the group: describe the group to see the rebalance.

## 2026-10-27 ARV-256: Declarative filters and directions read without a copy per item (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Infra sensing, tests, docs)

- Why (CWE-400, Low 1 of the ARV-178 review): `DeclarativeMapper.Scalar`, used for the `where` filters and the crossing direction, copied a value read from the group (^) or the payload ($) for every item (`GetString`, `GetRawText`): a 250,000 character value compared against 8,000 items was about 4 GB of short-lived copies per push. And `Integer`, `Number` and `ToTime` parsed a shared value again per item, while the per-group cache was cleared at every group, so payload values were read again per group. Latent: no shipped mapping filters on a shared value.
- Bounded: `Scalar` looks at a value's written length first (as `Bounded` does for names since ARV-178): a string written in more than six bytes a character of the 64 a filter or direction may list (`DeclarativeMapping.MaxFilterValueLength`), or a number written longer than 64, matches none and is never copied; otherwise it is decoded and kept only if at most 64 characters. All listed values are 1 to 64 characters, checked when a mapping is parsed, so no outcome changes.
- Decoded once: the mapper's state keeps elements per message ($, no longer cleared per group) and per group (^), and decoded values (scalar, id, name, integer, number, time per unit) per message or group, keyed by the path and what it was decoded as; an item's own values (@) are never kept, and a value that fails to decode stores nothing (the message is refused at the first item, with the same text as before). `DeclarativeMapper.SharedDecodes` (internal, per thread) counts shared decodes, for the tests only: the first `[ThreadStatic]` in production code.
- Tests (unit `DeclarativeConformanceTests`): the allocation theory, a 250,000 character filter or direction value from the payload or from the group under 8,000 items, costs under 250 KB more than a short value (one copy would be 500 KB); `Scalar` at the 64 character bound, plain, escaped (`é`, six bytes each) and as surrogate pairs (32 pairs kept, 33 not), and numbers of 64 and 65 digits; three groups of five samples reading the zone and count from their group and the time and a filter from the payload decode 8 values, not 60, and a group's samples share one name string. Proved against mutations: without the bound 4 tests failed, without the cache the decode test did (60).
- Docs: sensor-adapters (Sections and Values rows), cwe-controls (the sensing row), costly-operations (the declarative mapping row, its status line), asvs-l2 V1.4.2's citation (now `ToTime`, not a line number).
- Security review: PASS (CWE-400, CWE-120) with four Lows, all taken before commit: the drifted V1.4.2 citation, the costly-operations row, a non-ASCII character in the test (written as an escape), the allocation theory covering the group level as its summary claimed; the optional surrogate-pair rows added. Info noted: a filter or direction string over 384 bytes holding a lone-surrogate escape used to make `GetString` throw, which the ingest answered as malformed JSON; such an item is now ignored instead, nothing of it kept (the same class of change ARV-178 made for names).
- Gates: `node scripts/verify.mjs story --specs tests/api/device-push.spec.ts --integration "FullyQualifiedName~Sensing|FullyQualifiedName~Ingest|FullyQualifiedName~Resend"` (not wide) on the reviewed code: 32 steps PASS, among them build, unit 8,081 with the count guard, the security scan, docs rules, the story-filtered integration tests (25) and E2E 344 (device push with the smoke set and the permission matrix) with no secret in the artifacts. After the review's test and doc fixes: `node scripts/verify.mjs backend` PASS (unit 8,085 with the count guard, the security step) and `node scripts/verify.mjs docs` PASS. The declarative classes (112 then 116 tests) ran 3 of 3 green before the fixes.
- Gotchas: an allocation test over thousands of items measures the walk's own allocations too (the item list, a filter's closure per item, 1 to 2 MB here): compare against the same walk with a short value rather than against an absolute bound. The Edit tool decodes `\uXXXX` in what it writes, so an escape meant for C# source lands as the character; write it with a byte-level replace and grep the added lines for non-ASCII.

## 2026-10-27 ARV-257: A per-site AMAN feed age gauge, before a second border site (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Infra border, script 0065, Di, chart, docs)

- Why (CWE-400, CWE-532; finding 3 of the ARV-125a engineer, filed by ARV-179): the AMAN feed alert watched `ariva.border.feed.records`, which has no `site` tag, so with several border sites a feed that stops at one site while another's flows raised no alert.
- Gauge: `ariva.border.feed_age_seconds` (meter Ariva.Border, unit s, tag `site` only), `BorderMetrics.ObserveFeedAges` fed by `AmanFeedAges` (Ariva.Infra/Border, registered by `AddArivaDeskFeed`). Script 0065 adds `desk_feed_state.heartbeat_utc`, which the desk feed writes in the upsert that saves the state (`LEAST(GREATEST(EXCLUDED.heartbeat_utc, desk_feed_state.heartbeat_utc), date_trunc('minute', @now))`: a read that brings none, or an older minute after a refused state rereads its overlap, never moves it back, and it never stays ahead of the writing pod's minute, as `AmanDeskFeed.Step` clamps the state's). `DeskFeed.SitesAsync`, at the start of every read, now returns `DeskFeedSite(Code, Aman, HeartbeatUtc)` (one grouped query: any AMAN mapping, e-gates included, and the stored heartbeat) and hands the AMAN sites to `AmanFeedAges.Listed`, which replaces the last listing (valid site codes only, first row wins, at most 1,000). Each age is the one at the listing (listing time minus the heartbeat, or minus this replica's first listing for a site never heard), never now minus the heartbeat, so no replica overstates a site; a replica whose latest listing is older than two polls and half a minute reports nothing, and the alert's absence rule takes over. A listing that brings a null heartbeat for a site this replica knew (its state row deleted, runbook 4.8i) keeps the known one.
- Alert: `amanFeedStale` reads the gauge, max per `site`, `last` above `minutes` times 60, `notificationSettings.groupBy` site, absence kept; its summary and description say what an alert naming no site means. The margin (`minutes` times 60 above 60 s plus AMAN's delivery interval plus twice `PollSeconds`: 2 for Kafka and REST, 3 for the pull transport) is in values.yaml and wiki 10 section 3.1.
- Redesigned after review round 1 (FAIL: M1 a read cut at the run timeout silenced the cut site and those after it; M2 after a restart a failing site was reported by no replica; R1 a failure revived a stale copy; R2 e-gate-only sites were left out; R4 entries were never pruned). The first design kept each site's heartbeat in the memory of the replica that read it and reported it while that replica read it. Patching it (marking the cut and remaining sites failed) would have made a false alarm with two replicas: one cut before a site on every run keeps reporting it older and older while the other reads it, and the alert takes the largest per site. Reading the stored heartbeat back at each listing closes all five: a cut or failing read leaves the stored heartbeat, a restart reads it back, nothing is revived, any AMAN mapping counts, and each listing replaces the last. The first criterion was amended to this wording (reported by each replica that listed the sites lately).
- Security review: round 1 FAIL (M1, M2, L3, L4 and six recommendations, above); round 2 PASS (CWE-400, CWE-532; data boundary: the column is one minute per site, served by no API) with two Lows and three Infos. Taken before commit: Low 1, the chart refuses `amanFeedStale.minutes` under 2 (a healthy feed reads up to about 90 seconds; a chart-security case); Low 2, `GREATEST` in place of `COALESCE` with an integration assertion (a refused state rereading older records keeps the later minute; proved by reverting to `COALESCE`, which fails it); Info 3, wiki 10 section 4.4 says the first listing after a desk feed outage can page once per site. ## 2026-10-27 ARV-258: A gauge of the queue engine's checkpoint age with its rule, and AIDX's feed tag pinned (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Infra streaming, chart, tests, docs)

- Why (CWE-400, CWE-501; Lows 3 and 6 of the ARV-179 review): `QueueStreamWorker` pauses reading after a failed checkpoint while a zone is at its bound, and some failures happen while the database answers (a statement timeout, a lock wait, a zone's state above `StreamStore.MaxStateBytes`): `databaseUnavailable` does not fire, `ariva.stream.consumer_lag` stays flat, and only the Error log "Queue stream checkpoint failed" said so. The revoke handler's checkpoint does not mark it: on shutdown `consumer.Close()` runs the revoke after `Clear()`, and marking there left a stopped worker reporting (the integration test found it).

Compared once the database is at the latest script (any script may change an object): behind, "not compared" (a FAIL but in restore's own check, as the runtime privileges); past it, a FAIL naming the release to use. New read-only command `schema [--full]` (and `ariva-ops.mjs schema`) prints the list, or every part line by line, to compare two databases.

## 2026-10-27 ARV-264: Outbox relay: an event topic without a partition leader holds only its topic, not the whole outbox (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Infra messaging, Di, tests, docs)

- Why (CWE-400): an event row whose send timed out in the client (librdkafka's message timeout, `Local_MsgTimedOut`) while the brokers answered, which is a partition of its topic without a leader, ended every relay pass at that row (ARV-245 left this as its residual), so one leaderless partition delayed every other topic by up to 30 seconds at each pass.
- Hold: `IOutboxTransport.IsPartitionUnavailable` (`KafkaProduce.IsPartitionUnavailable`: `Local_MsgTimedOut` alone). On such a failure the relay asks the producer's cached probe once; while the brokers answer it holds that topic for `OutboxRelay.EventTopicHold` (1 minute) and carries on with the other topics; when the probe says no broker answers the pass ends as before and the next ones are skipped (ARV-245). No attempt counts against the row.
- Every topic hold (this one, ARV-177's missing topic, ARV-175's dead-letter topic) is now the topic's: the relay keeps its holds in memory (topic to end, pruned each pass) and both claims skip a held topic (`NOT (o.topic = ANY(@heldTopics))`), so a row written to it meanwhile under a new key is neither claimed nor tried; on the rows, each key's earliest unsent row is due at the hold's end (one write a key, not a row), and the claim keeps the later rows of a key behind it, so a relay that takes the lead claims none of the rows there were and tries the topic once at most for a later one.
- Cost, stated in the docs: the relay cannot tell a row's partition, so every row of a held topic waits while the partition has no leader; the topic's oldest row tries it again at each hold's end, up to the client's 30 s (reported within about 40) about once every 90 s per topic; about two thirds of the relay's time with two such topics, nearly all with three or more, other topics going between; a second such try cut by the pass's end holds nothing and the next pass holds that topic. The oldest row's ARV-245 streak grows at each try, so `outboxBrokerStreak` fires on a hold that lasts.
- Metric `ariva.outbox.topic_holds` (counter by bounded `topic` tag and `kind`: `partition_unavailable`, `topic_refused`, `dead_letter`, else `other`); a held row's "trying again in 5 s" Warning gives way to the hold's own, and its streak Error says it tries again when the hold ends.
- `Kafka:Outbox:PassSeconds` validated from 10 to 120 at start (`EnsureProducerSettings`; 10, not 46, because `StuckProduceTests` measures the pass bound at 20 s); below `OutboxRelaySettings.MinPassSecondsForTopicHolds` (46: `KafkaProduce.SendTimeout` and a second) the pass cuts such a send before the client reports it, so no hold is taken, and the relay warns at start.
- Tests: integration `OutboxRelayTests` (`Relay_Should_HoldOnlyTheTopicAndSendTheOthers_When_ASendTimesOutWhileTheBrokersAnswer` with a new-key row written during the hold and a fresh relay showing the residual, `Relay_Should_HoldEachTopicInTurnWithinThePassBound_When_TwoTopicsHaveAPartitionWithoutALeader`, `Relay_Should_EndThePassAsBefore_When_ASendTimesOutAndTheBrokersDoNotAnswer`; 26/26), unit `ProducerHardeningTests` (the classification, the pass time's bounds, the 46 s constant, the start Warning), `MetricTagTests` (the hold's tags), `RunTimeoutInventoryTests` (the in-pass probe named).
- Security review (CWE-400, CWE-532): round 1 FAIL, nothing High: M1, rows written to a held topic during the hold under a new key were claimed at the next pass, each holding the topic again, and the re-holds pushed the oldest row's retry forward so its streak alert stayed silent; M2, the docs claimed the topic's rows on partitions with a leader waited at most the hold; L1, the bound stated per topic only (several leaderless topics leave the relay waiting most of the time) and untested with a clock; L2, `PassSeconds` unvalidated (at or below about 45 s the hold never happens); L3, each hold rewrote every unsent row of the topic; L4, the cost inventory, the run timeout exemption and the "trying again in 5 s" Warning before a hold. All fixed as above. Round 2 PASS (CWE-400, CWE-532, V15.1.3, V16.5.2); its Low (the pass's producing, not the whole pass, is bounded by `PassSeconds`, the probe adding at most 4 s) taken in the relay's summary, cwe-controls and wiki 10, with a note on the in-memory hold kept after a rolled-back pass.
- Gates: `node scripts/verify.mjs story --integration "FullyQualifiedName~Messaging.OutboxRelayTests"` PASS, widened by the gate to the full suites (messaging files are wide): unit 8,124, integration 816 and 1 skipped, E2E 923 passed and 1 skipped; build, security scan and self-tests, chart security, audits and docs rules. The round 2 Low (wording and a comment only) was taken after the gate; `node scripts/verify.mjs quick` before the commit.
- Docs: cwe-controls CWE-400, costly-operations (the relay row), asvs-l2 V16.5.2, wiki 10 (the metric row; section 4.5a: the hold, its cost, the ARV-175 and ARV-177 bullets, `PassSeconds`).
- Gotchas: a hold kept only on the rows holds only the rows there were: a topic keyed per item (flights) gets new keys all the time, and each new one tried the topic again, so keep a topic's hold where the claim can see it. .NET 10's `BackgroundService` runs `ExecuteAsync` on a task of its own, so a test that stops a host right after `StartAsync` may stop it before its first line; wait for a line it writes first.

## 2026-10-27 ARV-265: Uploads: one user's share of the host's upload permit and its queue (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Api.Main, Api.Common, tests, E2E config, docs)

- Why (CWE-400, CWE-770): the `upload` policy's one permit and two waiting places per Ariva.Api.Main process were taken by the rate limiting middleware, before authentication, so ARV-250's per-user window counted a request only once it held the permit: one user's three 20 MB transfers at the 32 KB a second floor held the permit and both waiting places, and every other user's upload and the site configuration export got 429 for about 33 minutes (costly-operations section 15 item 17).
- Places taken after authorization: the middleware takes nothing for the policy any more (`GetNoLimiter`; the policy name stays the endpoints' marker). `UploadLimitAttribute` (resource filter, order -1, before any body read) takes, in order: the caller's window check without counting (past it, 429 with the window's Retry-After, no place taken); the caller's share (`Security:RateLimiting:UploadShare`, default 1, refused at start outside 1 to 3; a second upload or transfer of the same user while one runs or waits: 429, Retry-After 10, `UploadUnderway`, event 9116 partition `user`); a place on the host (`UploadRateLimiter`: one permit, two waiting oldest first, awaited with the request's token; all taken: 429, Retry-After 10, `UploadsBusy`, 9116 partition `host`); then the window count, so a request the host turns away spends none of the allowance. Share and place are held until the request ends.
- Cost, stated in the docs: the wait for the permit now runs within the request's `transfer` timeout (15 minutes), where the rate limiter's queue ran ahead of the timeouts; a request still waiting then is answered 503 with Retry-After, and one that waited has that much less time for its own transfer. Residuals: three users (or accounts) together can still hold every place; places and shares are per replica. The E2E host sets the share to 3 (its workers upload in parallel with one account).
- Tests: unit `UploadLimitTests` (`Upload_Should_LeaveOtherUsersThePlaces_When_OneUsersUploadIsUnderway`: the same user's next upload of any kind refused before its service, two other users waiting, a fourth refused by the host and its allowance untouched, a request without credentials answered 401 at once, every place free after; `Upload_Should_BeRefusedWithoutAPlace_When_TheUserIsPastTheirWindow`; `Upload_Should_LetOneUserHoldEveryPlace_When_TheShareIsTheHostsPlaces`; the setting's bounds and default), and on a real Kestrel `SteadyUploadTests.Upload_Should_LeaveTheWaitingPlacesToOtherUsers_When_OneUserTricklesThreeUploads` (the trickler's next two refused before their bodies are asked for, two other users waiting and answered 200 once the trickle is cut off, a request without credentials 401 and a fourth user refused by the host meanwhile); the existing trickle test now probes with three other users.

All fixed: a bearer without its user refused 401 with every place taken and the queue untouched (in process and on the real Kestrel), `UploadLimitTests.Upload_Should_FreeItsWaitingPlaceAndItsShare_When_ItIsCancelledWhileWaiting`, `SecurityEventLogTests.UploadRefusals_Should_NameThePolicyAndTheKindOfPartition_When_TheUsersShareOrTheHostsPlacesAreTaken` (two 9116, `user` then `host`, no 9129, the key never logged), the pointers in V15.2.2, V2.4.1, V16.3.3 and the CWE-120 row; advisory A taken (`Endpoints_Should_NotUseTheUploadPolicy_When_TheHostIsNotMain`, Ingest and Integration). Round 2 PASS. Left open as advisories: a share above 1 accepted in every environment (only the E2E host sets it); with a share above 1 a request past its window can wait for a place before being refused; no test of the 503 for a request still waiting at the `transfer` timeout; Stream and Cronz left out of the host inventory (they map no controllers); advisory F (the section 7 test list) taken.
- Gates: `node scripts/verify.mjs story` with the upload E2E specs and `Topology.SiteConfigurationTests`, widened by the gate to the full suites (Ariva.Api.Common is wide): unit 8,137, integration 816 and 1 skipped, E2E 923 passed and 1 skipped, visual 20, and every other step PASS but the NuGet audit, which could not reach nuget.org while the container restarted (connection refused on the agent proxy); rerun after: no vulnerable package in any project. Advisory F (the section 7 test list) taken after the gate; `node scripts/verify.mjs quick` before the commit.
- Docs: costly-operations sections 1, 7 (the export row and a new ARV-265 paragraph) and 15 item 17 (closed), asvs-l2 V15.2.2 (residual narrowed), log-inventory 9116 (`upload` after authorization, partition `user`), wiki 04 (`Uploads` row and the new `UploadShare` row), wiki 13a section 2.
- Gotchas: a raw HTTP test that reads a refused request's answer until the connection closes waits while Kestrel drains the body it never asked for, long enough here for a trickle's grace to pass; read until the answer's text is in. ASP.NET Core's rate limiter runs before authentication, so a limit that must know the user (a share, a count) belongs in a filter after authorization, and its waits then run inside the request timeout.

## 2026-10-27 ARV-266: Kafka consumer retry waits refused at start when negative, out of range or inverted (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Infra, Di, tests, docs)

- Why (CWE-400, from the ARV-254 review): `Kafka:Consumers:RetryMinMilliseconds` and `RetryMaxMilliseconds` had no range; MassTransit's exponential retry took them as they were, and the only check was the stop budget, which a negative value passed. The review read MassTransit 8.5.11's IL: a negative cap made the first retry throw (`IndexOutOfRangeException`), and a negative base gave negative delays, which `Task.Delay` refuses or, at -1 ms, waits on for ever while a stop does not cancel it.
- Bound: each from 0 to `ConsumerSettings.MaxRetryMilliseconds` (60,000) and the base no more than the cap, or `EnsureProducerSettings` refuses to start (before the stop budget and the poll interval checks). With it, ARV-254's one-day poll interval check cannot fire through the settings (2,095 s at the largest), so its theory that drove the cap to 8,490,501 ms is replaced by a test pinning the largest values; the check stays, with a comment, should a bound move.
- What the waits are (corrected after the review): the base and the cap of MassTransit's waits; each grows from the base by 2^n times a random 0.8 to 1.2, is capped, then multiplied by a random 0.75 to 1.25, so the first wait is about 270 to 550 ms at the defaults and a wait can reach 1.25 times the cap; a base of 0 or 1 means no backoff. `LongestHold` and the stop budget count the cap, not the jitter above it: filed as ARV-268.
- Tests: unit `ProducerHardeningTests.AddArivaMessaging_Should_RefuseToStart_When_TheConsumersRetryWaitsAreOutOfRangeOrInverted` (0, 60,000 and equal pairs taken; -1 for either, 60,001 and an inverted pair refused; no retry configured, so the stop budget does not refuse first), `ConsumerHoldTests.MaxPollInterval_Should_StayWithinADay_When_EverySettingIsAtItsLargest`.
- Security review (CWE-400): round 1 FAIL on docs only (the code and its tests correct): the waits described as "the first and the longest" though MassTransit's jitter takes a wait to 1.25 times the cap and a base of 0 or 1 gives no backoff; `LongestHold` and `CleanStop` not counting that jitter (option b: ARV-268 filed, named as a residual in cwe-controls CWE-400, asvs V15.2.2, costly-operations and the overview); V15.2.2 and the V15.1.3 inventory not naming the bound. All fixed; round 2 PASS, its four optional wordings taken after the gate (the test comment, "counting from 0", "within its attempts", and the hold passing the poll interval only when the quarter is more than its minute).
- Gates: `node scripts/verify.mjs story --integration "FullyQualifiedName~Messaging.KafkaPipelineTests"` widened by the gate to the full suites (messaging is wide): the first run failed one unit test, `BoundedProduceTests.Produce_Should_WriteTheRidersKeyValueAndHeaders_When_AnEventIsPublished`, which met an `MT-Activity-Id` header because another test class's host was tracing `Ariva.Kafka` beside it (fixed in its own commit: the wire format test leaves the optional trace header out, the traced send having its own test); the rerun PASS: unit 8,147, integration 816 and 1 skipped, E2E 923 passed and 1 skipped, and every other step. The round 2 wordings were in that rerun.
- Docs: wiki 04 (`Kafka:Consumers` row: the range, the jitter, the base-0 warning, the poll interval within 2,095 s), cwe-controls CWE-400, asvs-l2 V15.2.2, costly-operations (the consumers row), architecture overview; the PRD gains ARV-268.
- Gotchas: a range bound can make an older start check unreachable; replace the test that drove the old check with one that pins the largest values, so a moved bound fails it, and say so above the check. MassTransit's exponential retry jitters every wait by 0.75 to 1.25 after the cap: a cap is not a longest wait.

## 2026-10-27 ARV-268: Consumer hold and stop budget count MassTransit's retry jitter (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Infra, Di, chart comments, tests, docs)

- Why (CWE-400, from the ARV-266 review, fix 3): MassTransit 8.5.11's exponential retry multiplies each capped wait by a random 0.75 to 1.25 (`ExponentialRetryPolicy.GetRetryInterval`), so a wait can reach 1.25 times `Kafka:Consumers:RetryMaxMilliseconds`. `ConsumerSettings.LongestHold` (and with it the rider consumers' `max.poll.interval.ms`) and `MessagingExtensions.CleanStop` (the stop budget) counted the cap, so a hold could run a quarter of its waits past the poll interval's minute of margin at the largest settings, and a stop at the budget's edge past the bus's share (a redelivery, not a loss).
- Change: `ConsumerSettings.RetryJitter` (1.25) and `ConsumerSettings.RetryWaits(retries, cap)`, used by both `LongestHold` and `CleanStop`. At the defaults the longest hold is 413.75 s (was 410), the poll interval 473.75 s (was 470), a stop during retries needs 28.75 s (was 25) within the bus's 35 s; the `consumerHeld` rule's 420 s stays above the hold. The stop budget's refusal now gives its figures to two decimals (a fractional need is common now).
- Tests: unit `ConsumerHoldTests` (the hold and poll interval figures at the defaults, the most and the largest settings; `RetryJitter_Should_BoundEveryWait_When_TheRetryIsBuiltAsTheConsumePipelineBuildsIt` builds MassTransit's own policy with ConsumePipeline's arguments and samples it: every wait below 1.25 times the cap and, with the base at the cap, one above 1.2 times it, so a MassTransit update that widens the jitter fails here; `ConsumerHeldAlert_Should_LimitAboveTheLongestHold_When_TheHostsKeepTheirDefaults` holds the `holdLimit` of every values file in the chart's folder to at least the default longest hold, 414 s, since the chart cannot read the hosts' consumer settings, and fails on a file that names the rule in a form it does not read), `ProducerHardeningTests` (the stop budget at 44 s taken and 43 s refused, 4 retries of 5,000 ms taken at exactly 35 s and of 5,001 ms refused, 6 refused; each refusal matched to its own check's message).
- Security review (CWE-400): round 1 FAIL with the code correct: four docs and chart places still gave 410 s or 25 s (wiki 10 sections 2 and 3.1, cwe-controls' ARV-165 text, the five chart templates' comments, checks.mjs and the upload-scan fixture), and the jitter test compared the constant with itself (nothing tied it to MassTransit, whose minor updates Dependabot takes). All fixed, with advisories taken (the values file test, the two-decimal message, an ADR-0018 note, the refusal patterns, the CWE-400 test column, the InHandAtStopTests comment); round 2 PASS, its three optional points: the values file test lists the chart's folder and fails on a form it cannot read (taken after the gate, the class run again, 19 of 19), the ADR note's wording ("just under 1.25 times ..., rather than the cap alone", taken), and the sampling test repeating ConsumePipeline's arguments rather than reading them from the pipeline (left: low risk, the pipeline's retry is one call). The overview's and cwe-controls' "up to 15 s of waits" in the hold's cost became 18.75 s after the gate as well (decisions.md keeps its dated text).
- Docs: wiki 04 (`Kafka:Consumers`), wiki 10 (sections 2, 3.1, 4.5a and 4.24), cwe-controls CWE-400, asvs-l2 V15.2.2, costly-operations, the architecture overview (also the hold's cost, 18.75 s of waits), ADR-0018 (a dated ARV-268 note correcting the ARV-165, 253 and 254 figures), the chart's values.yaml comment and the five host templates' comments.
- Gotchas: a constant that mirrors a library's behaviour needs a test against the library itself, not against the constant; sample the real policy, and assert both the bound and that the bound is reached (a bound nothing approaches proves nothing). When a figure moves, search the chart templates, its tests and fixtures, and the dated ADR notes as well as the docs the story names.

## 2026-10-27 ARV-246: Outbox relay waits after a pass that sent nothing, and a host's own producer failure holds no dead-letter topic (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Infra, tests, docs)

- Why (CWE-400, the ARV-175 round 3 review's N1 and N2): (1) the relay skipped its poll wait after any full batch with no failure, which a batch of rows of an event type this build does not know also met (held back without a failure), so during a rolling deploy the older leader ran back-to-back transactions on rows it could not send and took the leader lock again before the pods that know the type; (2) since ARV-175 a dead letter whose send failed for a reason not its own held its `.dlq.v1` topic for a minute for every relay, and `IsBrokerUnavailable` also covers conditions of one host's producer (disposed, `Local_Destroy` at a stop or a retirement, a fatal client error), so a pod stopping with a letter in flight held that topic although the broker was fine.
- Change: the loop passes again at once only when the pass also sent a row (`pass.Sent > 0`); `IOutboxTransport.IsProducerUnavailable` (default: disposed) and `KafkaProduce.IsProducerUnavailable` (a fatal client error, a message the client purged at it, `Local_PurgeQueue` or `Local_PurgeInflight`, `Local_Destroy`, disposed; a subset of the broker unavailability, which since this story also names the purge codes, so the row still counts no attempt): a dead letter's such failure ends the pass as an event's does (the producer cannot send the rest either) and holds no topic, in both catches; the broker's own absence and the dead letters' share still hold it (ARV-175).
- Tests: integration `OutboxRelayTests.Relay_Should_WaitThePollInterval_When_AFullBatchIsHeldBackWithoutAFailure` (the real loop, a 1 s poll and a batch of 2 unknown-type rows: every gap between passes at least 0.9 s), `Relay_Should_PassAgainAtOnce_When_AFullBatchSentARowThoughAnotherWasHeldBack` (the other side of the condition: an unknown row ahead of three known keys, a batch of two and a 10 s poll, the three sending passes within half the poll), `Relay_Should_EndThePassWithoutHoldingTheTopic_When_ADeadLetterFailsOnThisHostsProducer` (disposed, destroyed, purged, fatal: the events sent, the pass ended at the letter with no attempt counted, no row of the topic held, the topic's other letter sent at the next pass of the same relay, the failed letter after its broker retry), `Relay_Should_HoldNoTopic_When_ADisposedTransportWithTheDefaultsFailsADeadLetter` (a transport keeping the interface's defaults reaches the last catch: an attempt counted, no hold); unit `ProducerHardeningTests.IsProducerUnavailable_Should_NameOnlyThisHostsProducersOwnConditions` and the purge rows of `IsBrokerUnavailable_Should_ClassifyTheClientsErrors`. With the two relay lines reverted the first four integration cases failed; restored, OutboxRelayTests 33 of 33 and ProducerHardeningTests 121 of 121.
- Security review (CWE-400): round 1 FAIL, one required fix: librdkafka purges a producer's queued messages when it raises a fatal error, and their reports carry `Local_PurgeQueue` (not fatal), which neither classifier named, so the dead letter the relay had in the client at that moment (the likeliest case, one row at a time) took the generic catch, counted an attempt and held its topic, the very N2 symptom; both classifiers now name `Local_PurgeQueue` and `Local_PurgeInflight` (Ariva never purges, so these only come from the client's own state). Advice taken: a test of the loop's other side (a pass that sent a row passes again at once), a test of the last catch with a transport keeping the interface's defaults, the catch comment, the cwe-controls clause and tests column, and docs no longer saying the relay meets a producer failure at its own pod's stop (its pass is cancelled and rolled back before the producer stops: OutboxRelay stops before KafkaProducerLifetime) or that the other pods' producers can always reach the topic (a fatal cause can be cluster-wide, a missing IdempotentWrite ACL). Filed as ARV-269: `PollMilliseconds` and `BatchSize` without start bounds (0 makes the wait a no-op), and a producer's own failure still logged as the broker's and counted in the broker streak. Accepted residuals: an old leader still passes back to back while it sends anything (progress, bounded); `_brokersAway` stays set for a producer's own failure (one cached probe on the new client). Round 2 PASS, its two test comment nits taken after the gate.
- Docs: wiki 10 (the `Unknown event type` entry; the dead-letter topic hold warning, whose "known limit until ARV-246" is replaced), overview section 5 (the hold's exceptions; the relay's poll wait), cwe-controls CWE-400, costly-operations (the outbox relay row and its tests).
- Gotchas: a loop that skips its wait on "the batch was full" must also ask whether the pass did anything; rows held back without a failure fill a batch as well as rows that wait. A failure class shared by the broker and one host's client (here "broker unavailable") needs splitting before it drives a decision every relay sees.

## 2026-10-27 ARV-195: Per-request minimum body rates set over HTTP/1.x only (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; unit tests, docs)

- Why (CWE-400, from round 2 of the ARV-142b review): Kestrel takes a per-request minimum body data rate on HTTP/1.x only; on HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 setting `IHttpMinRequestBodyDataRateFeature.MinDataRate` throws, so an endpoint setting it on any protocol would answer every request over those 500 the day TLS ends on Kestrel.

- Change: the architecture test `MinimumBodyRateTests` reads every production source file under Platform and refuses any but `SteadyUploadAttribute.cs` that names either per-request rate feature (the request body's, or the response's, which is absent on HTTP/2 and HTTP/3) or assigns a rate (plain or `??=`); that file must name the feature once, assign once, and hold the protocol check, the feature and the assignment as one statement; a second fact reads the build files (every `.csproj`, `.props` and `.targets` under Platform and the root's `.props`) for an MSBuild alias of either feature. Proven with a throwaway file in Ariva.Api.Ingest holding the assignment: the test failed naming it; the file removed. 13 of 13. The three copies of the tests' fake feature became one, `Setup/BodyRateFeature`, which throws on HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 when the rate is read as well as set (Kestrel 10.0.12 measured by the reviewer), its value read through `Stored`: with `RequireRate` mutated to read the rate before the protocol check, the HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 rows of `HostRequestPathTests` failed (restored after).
- Security review (CWE-400): round 1 FAIL, one required fix in test code: the fake feature threw only on a set, though Kestrel's getter throws too on HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, so a later edit reading the rate before the protocol check would have passed the unit tests and the scan (which counted assignments); fixed with the shared fake. Advice taken: `??=` and the response feature in the scan, the allowed file pinned to one guarded statement, the build files read for an MSBuild alias, the misleading `== null` negative row dropped, filters on the relative path, ASVS V15.2.2 naming the test. Round 2 PASS; its optional point taken after the gate (the root's `.targets` read as well as its `.props`), the other left (a build folder directly under Platform would be read, not skipped: it can only add files)
- Docs: costly-operations (the steady upload paragraph and the HTTPS push row name the test), asvs-l2 V15.2.2.
- Gotchas: a fix that lives in one guarded helper needs a scan that keeps every caller on it; a unit test of the helper alone does not stop the next endpoint from setting the rate directly. A fake of a framework feature must fail where the framework fails (reads too, not only writes), or the test proves less than it says; measure the framework when in doubt.

## 2026-10-28 ARV-190: Not-evaluated border rules audited, deleted rules forgotten (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Infra, tests, docs)

- Why (CWE-778, CWE-400; the ARV-187 review's lows 4 and 5): a stored border rule that fails its metric's rule checks had its open alerts withdrawn (`RuleWithdrawn`) with no audit entry, only a log warning; and `NotEvaluatedWarnings` recorded the warned version before the tick's commit (a failed commit never warned again) and kept the entries of rules deleted later (`Forget` ran only when a rule was evaluated).

On the first sighting per values version `AlertRuleTick.NotEvaluatedAsync` writes one `AlertRule.NotEvaluated` audit entry in the tick's own unit of work: target `{site}:{code}`, after summary JSON with the values version, the fixed reason, the alerts withdrawn and `by: evaluation`, the evaluation's system user as the actor.
- Tests: unit `NotEvaluatedWarningsTests` (a failed commit warns again, `Keep` forgets the dropped rules and refuses null, the per-version and per-host behaviour kept); integration `PredictedAlertTests.Tick_Should_WithdrawAndWarnOnce_When_APredictedRuleNoLongerBelongsToTheBorder` (each of its 3 rows: one audit entry for two ticks, naming the site and code, the system user, 1 alert withdrawn, the reason and a values version; a second entry with 0 withdrawn after the values change). Two mutants each fail it: the version recorded before the commit, and the `Keep` call removed.
- Security review (CWE-778, CWE-400): round 1 FAIL: no test proved the entry commits with the withdrawal or that a failed commit records nothing (two mutants survived: the entry in another scope, the version recorded before the commit), and cwe-controls said the entry names the withdrawn alerts though it holds their number. Fixed with the trigger test and the wording; advice taken: the `Keep` call pinned by the same test, the per-replica and per-restart repetition documented (wiki 10, cwe-controls), the withdrawn count read as JSON, log-inventory's `audit_entry` row naming the evaluation's own entries and their border-only content. Housekeeping's withdrawals (rules disabled or deleted through the API) stay unaudited, as the reviewer agreed: the change itself is audited by the person who made it. - Docs: wiki 10 (the not-evaluated rule paragraph), wiki 18 (the release note's step 4), cwe-controls CWE-863 (the control and its tests), log-inventory (the `audit_entry` row).
- Gotchas: a "warned once" memory must be written after the commit that carries the warning's audit, not before, or a rolled-back tick silences the next; and a memory keyed by entity id needs a sweep driven by the set the job actually reads, or deleted entities stay in it for the host's life. The worker restart mid-probe left the mutated source on disk: probes keep a saved copy and are restored before anything else after a restart.

- Tests: unit `ProducerHardeningTests.AddArivaMessaging_Should_RefuseToStart_When_TheRelaysBatchIsOutOfBounds` and `..._When_TheRelaysPollIsOutOfBounds` (each edge, -1 and 0 refused, 200 taken); integration `OutboxRelayTests.Relay_Should_ReportTheProducersOwnFailureAsItsOwn_When_ItLastsPastTheBrokerStreak` (a theory over disposed, destroyed, purged and fatal, each for 75 s against a one-minute streak: no Error, no streak counted or followed, 15 warnings naming the producer and none the broker, no attempt; then sent) and `Relay_Should_EndTheBrokerStreak_When_TheProducerFailsTheRowInBetween` (one broker failure, the producer failing the row for 65 s, the broker again at 70 s: no Error; the broker alone for the next minute is reported once). - Security review (CWE-400): round 1 FAIL, two required fixes: the batch's maximum of 1,000 let one pass read up to 1,000 events and 1,000 kept dead letters (each up to about 1 MB of JSON) into memory before its first send, past every relay host's limit (750 Mi to 1500 Mi), so the leading host and then each that took over the lead would be killed for memory (and the summary's reason, row locks, was wrong: the pass's time bounds those); and a producer's own failure left a broker streak already running for the row, so its next broker failure could report the producer's time as a partition without a leader. Fixed: the batch is 10 to 100 and a producer's failure ends the row's streak, with the second test. Advice taken: the failure kinds as a theory, the warning's wording (due again, sent once the producer is ready), the catch comments for a transport with the defaults, the idle database cost and the lead's takeover in the docs, the minimum batch of 10, the overview's bounds; filed as ARV-270: the streak's Error naming its cause (a full local queue or the producer's own bound is not a partition). - Docs: wiki 04 (`Kafka:Outbox:*`, with the lead's takeover), wiki 10 (the producer's warning beside the broker entries), costly-operations (the relay row's bounds, its idle cost and tests), cwe-controls CWE-400 (the control and its tests), the architecture overview (the bounds), asvs-l2 V16.5.2; the PRD gains ARV-270.

## 2026-10-28 ARV-270: Outbox broker streak names its cause (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Infra, chart rule text, tests, docs)

- Why (CWE-400, from the ARV-269 review's advice 5): the ARV-245 broker streak counts every failure `IsBrokerUnavailable` names, and its Error always said "the topic's partition may have no leader", though a full producer queue on the pod (`Local_QueueFull`, Ingest under a sensor flood), the producer's own 45 second bound and the relay pass's bound are not a partition; the operator was sent to look for a leaderless partition that did not exist.
- Change: the Error carries `{Cause}`, a constant naming the last failure (the client's error code, else the exception's type, never its message: `KafkaProduce.FailureCode`), and `{Hint}`, one of six fixed texts (`OutboxRelay.StreakHint`): a partition without a leader only for the client's message timeout (`IsPartitionUnavailable`), the pod's producer queue full (`KafkaProduce.IsQueueFull`), the producer's own bound passed without a report (`IsReportOverdue`, `KafkaProduceTimeoutException`), the relay pass's bound cutting the send (`OutboxPassTimeoutException`, the client's cause then not known), any other timeout, else the brokers not reached. `IOutboxTransport` gains `IsQueueFull`, `IsReportOverdue` and `FailureCode` with safe defaults, so `OutboxRelay` still names no Kafka type; the metric, its tags and the rule's expression are unchanged.

## 2026-10-28 ARV-252: CI's unit and integration logs checked before they are public (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; CI, the artifact check, the count guard, verify.mjs, one unit theory row, docs)

- Why (CWE-532, from the ARV-164b review): since ARV-164a and ARV-164b CI runs the test executables, whose console output carries the in-process hosts' JSON logs; it was teed into the job log of a public repository, and the logs' last lines and failing tests went into the pull request's comments, with nothing checking them as `artifact-secrets.mjs` checks the E2E report and the hosts' logs (ARV-152).
- Change: the backend job writes each suite's output to `unit.log` and `integration.log` (no tee), each suite ended by coreutils `timeout -k 30s` (14 and 27 minutes, its process group with it) a minute before its step's own timeout, which would end only the step's shell and leave the suite writing on; the job's limit is 60 minutes. The test log check (`test-logs`, also after a failed suite) copies both logs, the TRX files and the AMAN pact to `checked/` and runs the artifact check on that copy; every later step reads and uploads the copy alone, so nothing written after the check reaches them. Only on its success are the logs printed (between `::stop-commands::` with a random token and its resume on a line of its own), their last lines and failing tests quoted in the step summary and the pull request comments (backticks taken out, so a line cannot end the code block), and the TRX files and the pact uploaded (the pact's upload moved after the check). A finding fails the job and none of it is shown; the comments then say the logs were not quoted. The count guard's failed listing (case names with theory arguments, printed before the check) goes through `redactSecrets`. `backendLogWiring` in the same script holds the wiring step by step, comments left out. The local unit and integration gates run the check on each suite's TRX file (`verify.mjs`), since CI checks the TRX too.
- Found on the way: the unit TRX held a recovery code's shape, a theory row of `TotpTests.Normalize_Should_ApplyCrockfordRules_When_UserTypesACode` (a row's arguments are part of its display name, which the TRX keeps), so CI would have failed every run; the row is now a letters-only dashed code, the digits covered by the other rows. The local TRX check then found two more: `RedactionEnricherTests.RedactText_Should_MaskCredentials_When_TheyAppearInsideText` (its JWT was built at run time so no scanner would see it in the source, but a MemberData row's arguments are its display name) and `SessionConcurrencyTests.PresentsCredentials_Should_ReadTheHeaderAsAuthenticationDoes_When_ItDecidesWhoIsCounted`; their rows now name the made-up credential by a placeholder the test replaces, and the failure message quotes the row as written. Recent local gate logs (the unit suite and the full integration suite's console output) and the integration TRX were clean.
- Tests: `artifact-secrets.mjs --self-test` plants a device credential in a host's Serilog JSON line (rendered message and properties, as `ArivaLogging` configures the console) in `integration.log`, and in a TRX's test output, beside clean logs: each time the check fails, names that file and the kind, never prints the value, and passes once the plant is gone. The real `ci.yml` wiring holds, and the wiring check refuses fifteen miswirings, each for its own reason: a suite teed, run again after the check, run through `dotnet test` or without a timeout; the check before a suite, skipped by a failed suite, continuing on an error or reading the logs in place; a log read in place, quoted unchecked, printed with commands live or resumed on a log line; a result uploaded unchecked or from outside the copy; a gate written in a comment. Probes in round 1: without the planted line the self-test failed; the wiring check caught the Test counts step printing its summary with commands live, fixed. Story gate green: unit 8,196 of 8,196 with the new TRX check passing (after the two fixtures below), security and docs steps, E2E 341 passed on the five specs it chose; the integration suite was skipped (no persistence change) and its latest full TRX scanned clean by hand. A first run failed on the new TRX check, which found the two theories below.
- Security review (CWE-532, the 14 CWEs, ASVS V13.3.1): round 1 FAIL, two required fixes: the wiring check read only the first step running each suite and not the order, so a check moved between the suites or a second, teed suite run after it passed; and a step timeout ends the step's shell, not the suite, which could keep writing to its log after the check had read it. Fixed as above (every suite step checked with its order; the checked copy and the suites' own timeouts), with most of its advice (trailing comments, path forms and globs, continue-on-error, the token's source and the resume's line, the count guard's tail, the pact, backticks, the log inventory, the CWE-287 row). Round 2 PASS (CWE-532 control in place and tested; CWE-77 workflow commands stopped and held by the wiring check; the other CWEs untouched or touched through test fixtures only; V13.3.1 stays Partly for the secret store, ARV-083c), and its follow-up on the two fixtures PASS. Semgrep's MCP server could not connect, so the project's scanner was the only static scan. Its remaining advice (symlinks in the copy, five deliberate-edit gaps of the wiring check) is in ARV-271.
- Docs: test-cadence (a cadence row and the CI paragraph), wiki 16 (the `unit` and `integration` scopes and the artifacts paragraph), log-inventory (the CI row), cwe-controls (CWE-287 row), asvs-l2 V13.3.1 and the story table, the ARV-217 note in the Azure PRD (the Azure gate's published results to be checked the same way). Filed ARV-271 (the mutation workflow's log and report checked before upload; the E2E failure comment's backticks) and ARV-272 (E2E host logs kept for the latest runs only: 33 runs had filled the disk during ARV-270's gate).
