## 2026-10-28 ARV-259b: bin maturity backlog, a metric and alert rule (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Infra, Di, chart, tests, docs)

- Why (CWE-400, CWE-532): wiki 10 section 3's alarm "bins older than the censoring timeout still provisional" had no metric. A bin becomes Final once the watermark has passed its end and its open entrants are resolved (exit, or censored after 120 minutes), so a bin still Provisional after its end, the censoring timeout and the lateness means a watermark that does not move, a queue worker stopped or lagging, or a fault in finalisation; the site's reports, SLA evaluation and staffing wait for Final bins.
- Change: Stream's bin maturity sweep (`BinMaturityMonitor`, registered whenever `Stream:Enabled`, Kafka or not, so it also sees a worker that stopped while its host runs) runs every `Stream:BinMaturitySweepSeconds` (60; 10 to 3,600) under a one-minute run timeout. `StreamStore.CountOverdueBinsAsync` takes `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(53, 0)` in its transaction (one replica a round; the others return null and keep their last copy, which lapses), then counts by site the latest revision of each `queue_bin` still Provisional that ended before now less the engine's censoring timeout and the longest lateness of any site (`StreamSettings.MaxLatenessSeconds`), among bins started within `Stream:BinMaturityLookbackHours` (24; 1 to 168), leaving out a bin whose zone has since written a bin under a newer profile version (the zone started afresh and no longer holds it) and a bin of a zone that is not a queue zone of its site's published profile (taken out of it), at most 100 sites, the most overdue first; one statement within the database command timeout. The times must be UTC (refused otherwise, before any connection). The gauge `ariva.stream.bins_overdue` (meter `Ariva.Stream`, tag `site`) reports the sweep for two intervals; the queue worker's `Clear` leaves it alone and the sweep clears it when it stops. The chart's rule `binsOverdue` (on by default, 15 minutes, Warning) reads its largest copy by site above 0 for the whole window: the default bin length, so a stream that lags by less finalises each bin before the next is mature.
- Found on the way: a zone that moves to a newer profile version starts afresh and leaves its open bins Provisional for good, so without the newer-version filter every publish would have fired the rule for a day; a running zone keeps its version until it is loaded again, so the filter is per zone (a later bin under a newer version), not the site's published version, which would have hidden every running zone after a publish. A zone taken out of the published profile left its last bins for the look-back too (26 hours of a Warning renotified every 4 hours, frequent while sites are commissioned), so the sweep counts only zones of the published profile (advice of the review's round 1). Bins left by a refused snapshot are still counted: nothing writes them Final today (the recompute of a period is a Target, wiki 10 section 4.10), so the runbook says to silence the site's alert or recompute the zone from scratch while the topics hold the period. The unit test hosts read the simulator's service settings (the shared output), so `Stream:Enabled` is off there; the run timeout inventory turns it on to see the sweep.
- Tests: integration `Streaming.BinMaturityTests` (as the runtime login): the count by site over the latest revision (a later Final revision not counted, a later Provisional one counted, at sites of their own), the maturity boundary (a bin ending at the instant is not counted), the bin's own length, the look-back's first bin counted and the one before not, a zone moved to a newer version not counted and one whose newer version only recomputed an earlier bin counted, a zone taken out of the published profile (in the retired version as a queue zone, in the published one as an overflow zone of that name, in the draft again) and a site without one not counted, the bound of 100 sites with the order; the lock (a held lock gives null and no gauge from this replica, the lock gone with the transaction), the monitor's maturity delay from the engine's defaults, its report and the gauge's two-interval freshness. Eleven query mutants each fail them (revision order, `<=` at maturity, a fixed 15 minute length, `>` at the look-back, a session lock, no LIMIT, the newer-version filter dropped or not tied to later bins, the profile membership dropped, matched at any site, at any status or for any zone kind; the last two survived until round 2 of the review had the removal seeded as it happens, a retired version and an overflow zone of the name), after a first version let the revision order survive (the provisional-then-final and final-then-provisional cases at one site gave the same count either way). Unit `Queueing.BinMaturityTests` (the gauge's tags, freshness, copy, the worker's Clear leaving it and the sweep's own; times refused unless UTC; the stopped monitor reporting nothing; the settings' ranges and edges; `MaxLatenessSeconds`; the maturity delay; the registration with and without Kafka), `MetricTagTests`, `RunTimeoutInventoryTests` (Stream's bounded loops), `MonitoringRulesTests` and `chart-security.mjs` (metric, aggregation, grouping and notification by site, threshold, window, severity). Story gate green (it widened to the full suites): unit 8,215 of 8,215, integration 838 passed and 1 skipped of 839 with both TRX checks, security, chart security with the new rule, docs rules, E2E 923 passed (API and functional). Two earlier runs were stopped to take the review's advice.
- Security review (CWE-400, CWE-532): round 1 FAIL on documentation only (the code passed every control): the sweep was missing from the costly operations register that backs ASVS V15.1.3 (now its row, the gauge's tag source and the Stream pool note), and wiki 10 and 18 sent the operator to a recompute that is a Target procedure (the golden replay writes evidence, not bins); fixed, with its advice taken (the removed-zone filter, the worker's Clear leaving the sweep's gauge, the full list of lock classes, times refused unless UTC, a sweep that keeps failing named in the runbook). Round 2 PASS (CWE-89, CWE-269, CWE-400, CWE-501 and CWE-532 touched with their controls and tests; the others untouched), and its advice taken (the removal seeded as it happens, which killed two more mutants; the interim actions' trade-offs); round 3 on those changes PASS. Semgrep's MCP server could not connect, so the project's scanner was the only static scan.
- Docs: wiki 10 (section 2's row, 2a the gauge, 3 and 3.1 the rule, the closing paragraph, new 4.5c what to check when it fires, including a sweep that keeps failing), wiki 04 (the two settings), wiki 17 (the troubleshooting row), wiki 18 migration notes, docs/security/costly-operations.md (the sweep's row, the gauge's tag source in the metrics row, the Stream pool note), the chart values comment.
- Gotchas: an alarm over stored state must tell abandoned rows from stuck ones: anything that restarts a unit of work afresh (a profile version, a refused snapshot, a removed zone) leaves rows that never change again. Decide per unit what supersedes them, and check that the superseding fact appears when the unit actually changes (here, when the zone is loaded again), not when configuration changes.

## 2026-10-29 ARV-259d: display stale, a metric and alert rule (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Infra, Main, chart, tests, docs)

- Why (CWE-400, CWE-532): wiki 10 section 3's alarm "display stale" had no metric. A display shows the neutral message once a zone's data is older than its stale threshold (60 to 1,800 seconds), but nothing on the server recorded it: the board endpoint only reads, and no player heartbeat is stored.
- Change: a display stale sweep in Ariva.Api.Main (`DisplayStaleMonitor`, every minute, a one-minute run timeout). One replica a round takes `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(54, 0)` in the sweep's transaction (`SvcDisplayStaleness`, behind `ISvcDisplayStaleness`), reads the enabled, live displays' site, stale threshold and entries only (no credential hash, no messages; `Display.EntriesOf` parses the entries as `EntryList` does), at most 2,000 by site and code (a Warning once while more exist), and judges each as its board would be judged now, by the player's own rule, now shared with the board (`SvcDisplayBoard.AgeSeconds` and `IsStale`: a band while the age, to a tenth of a second, is at most the threshold): stale when a zone it shows has no live snapshot or one older than its threshold. One Redis read per distinct zone a sweep; when Redis refuses or does not answer, the board answers 503 too, so every display not judged by then counts as stale and Redis is not asked again that sweep. A fresh snapshot without a nowcast (out of service) shows the neutral message by design and is not counted. The gauge `ariva.displays.stale` (new meter `Ariva.Displays`, exported) by `site`: every site with an enabled display, 0 when none is stale, at most 100 (the most stale first), reported after the sweep's transaction ends, for two minutes, only by the replica that swept; a skipped round leaves its copy to lapse, a stopped sweep clears it. The chart's rule `displaysStale` (on by default, 5 minutes, Warning, by site, runbook 4.8).
- What it does not see (wiki 10 section 3.1): a player that stopped asking for its board (recording each request would add a write to a hot endpoint on every Main replica), and operating hours: a site whose zones publish nothing while closed and whose displays stay enabled raises it then (a SigNoz planned downtime, more minutes, or the rule off).
- Tests: integration `Displays.DisplayStaleTests` as the runtime login against a real Redis (the stale rule with fresh, old, missing and out-of-service snapshots, the threshold's boundary, a disabled and a deleted display, another site's zone of the same name, each zone read once, a minute later the 60-second displays stale, the copy lapsing; the lock held by another transaction, the round skipped and the next two run; 2,001 displays judged up to the bound in site and code order; Redis refusing and timing out, each with its one Warning carrying the exception alone; the sweep's lock held while it reads Redis, as another connection's try fails then and succeeds after). Ten query and code mutants each fail them (the enabled filter, the boundary, the lock literal, the Redis short-circuit, the read cache, the zone key's site, the order, the bound, the Redis failure not caught, the lock statement run outside the sweep's transaction); the deleted filter's mutant survives because the NHibernate mapping already adds `deleted_on IS NULL` (an equivalent mutant; the explicit filter mirrors the board's). Unit `Monitoring.DisplayStaleTests` (the gauge's window, bound and copy, the shared rule's table, the monitor's run timeout and interval, the skipped round, the warning once per spell, the failed sweep rolled back, the stopped sweep cleared, the registration; two monitor mutants each fail them), `MetricTagTests`, `RunTimeoutInventoryTests` (Main's loops), `MeterExportTests`, `MonitoringRulesTests`, `chart-security.mjs`.
- Story gate green (widened to the full suites: Api.Common and Di changed): unit 8,242 of 8,242, integration 844 passed and 1 skipped of 845 with both count guards and the secret checks, security scan, chart security with the new rule, audits, docs rules, E2E 923 passed (API and functional). A first run was stopped in its unit tests to take the review's advice.
- Security review (CWE-400, CWE-532): round 1 PASS on every CWE (CWE-400, CWE-532, CWE-89, CWE-501, CWE-863, CWE-79 touched with their controls and tests; the others untouched), with four Lows and two Infos, all taken: the costly operations register's connections row names the leader's held Main connection; the docs and the alert say that during a Redis outage the count includes boards that cannot be refreshed and still show their last band until their own threshold passes (so with a threshold above 5 minutes the rule can fire first); a test that the sweep holds its lock while it reads Redis; a test of the Warning; the read projected to three columns; 'every site the sweep judged'. The follow-up on those PASS, and its one wording item (the rule's description given the same Redis caveat) taken; its other two (a test pinning the projection, a using order) left, as data minimisation and cosmetics. Semgrep's MCP server could not connect, so the project's scanner was the only static scan.
- Docs: wiki 10 (2, 2a, 3, 3.1 with what the rule does not see, 4.8), wiki 17 (Displays), wiki 18, docs/security/costly-operations.md (the sweep's row, the gauge's tag), the chart values comment.
- Gotchas: the integration tests share one database, so each takes out the displays an earlier one left (soft delete) and seeds its own sites; `AccountsHost` builds its services on the first user, so the runtime login goes into its settings before then, and the user names must differ. A filter that the NHibernate mapping already applies cannot be proven by a mutant. A sweep that holds a database lock while it calls another store needs a test that probes the lock from outside during that call; that it is free afterwards proves nothing about during.

## 2026-10-29 ARV-193: the advertising policy panel resets on a site change and keeps the profile version it reviews (Phase 3; branch story/mvp-phase1; Web, Infra, tests, docs)

- Why (from round 5 of the ARV-145 security review): the passenger displays screen's advertising policy panel kept its form (allowed, excluded zones, reason) when the screen moved to another site, and a refresh that brought a newer zone profile replaced the offered zones and the profile id the save names without a word. The server refused nothing it should accept (it checks the site scope and answers 409 to a stale review), but a save could carry another site's selections or confirm a version the administrator never saw announced. The board's advertising check also dropped a null zone before the rule, where the policy's view and script 0057 refuse it (not reachable: a display never stores one).
- Change: the form takes its review when it opens (the published profile's id, version and queue zones, read with the policy) and keeps it; the save names that id. A newer version on the policy while the form is open (after a refused save, or the screen's refresh after a display action) shows a notice naming both versions (`advertising-review-stale`, a status region; a third wording when no profile is published any more) with "Review version N", which takes the new version's zones; nothing switches by itself. Cancel and a successful save drop the review. A save keeps its site across its awaits and does nothing more (no toast, no problems, no change of the policy) once the screen has moved to another site; the screen drops a policy that is not for the site it shows (security review round 1). The screen keys the panel by its site (`{#key siteCode}`), so choosing another site closes an open form, and clears the last site's policy as soon as the site changes, so nothing on the panel stands for the new site before its own policy is read. `AdvertisingPolicyGuard.AllowsAsync` passes a null zone to the rule, which refuses it, and leaves it out of the zone lookup only. Strings in English and Arabic.
- Tests: functional `advertising-policy.spec.ts`: the form closes when the site changes and reopens with nothing of what was chosen, no save sent; a newer profile brought by the refresh after a (mocked) display deletion while the form is open shows the notice in English and Arabic, keeps version 12 and its zones, a save names 12 and is refused (409), Review takes 13 and its new zone, and the save confirms 13; the existing refused-save test now reviews 13 explicitly; a save held in flight until the screen has moved to another site answers there with nothing of the first site (not allowed, only its own reason, no excluded zones, its policy read once so no refresh started, Change opening with its own values). Either guard alone stops that leak (the panel's and the screen's), so the test proves the pair, not each. Unit `AdvertisingPolicyTests` (a null zone among the display's), integration `AdvertisingPolicyServiceTests.Guard_Should_RefuseADisplayOfANullZone_When_TheBoardAsksWithOne` (the zones taken from DMO's profile as published now, since other tests of the class publish new versions); the old code that dropped nulls fails both of its null cases.
- Story gate green (scoped: no wide folder): unit 8,243 of 8,243, integration 34 of 34 (the advertising policy class) with the count guard and the secret checks, web svelte-check, lint and build, visual regression (20), E2E 355 passed in 7 spec files (the two advertising policy specs and the display specs the gate adds), security scan, audits, docs rules. A first run was stopped in its unit tests to take the review's fix.
- Security review (the story names no CWE; judged against all 14: CWE-863, CWE-79 and CWE-89 touched): round 1 FAIL on one Low, a save that answered after the screen moved to another site put the first site's policy on the second site's panel (the panel reads the page's live site and callback after `{#key}` destroyed it, and the page's `onChanged` had no site check), so Change could open there with the first site's selections (the server's site scope, 409 and zone checks still held). Fixed in both places with the test above; the follow-up PASS on every CWE. Its notes, not blocking, filed as ARV-273: a save that finishes after the administrator moved away confirms nothing, and two administrators can overwrite each other's change of a policy (only the profile is checked, not the policy row). Semgrep's MCP server could not connect, so the project's scanner was the only static scan.
- Docs: wiki 11 (the advertising policy section).
- Gotchas: a component inside `{#key}` that awaits keeps running after it is destroyed and reads its parent's live props, so a value it must keep (the site) is taken before the first await, and the parent checks what comes back. The displays screen refreshes the policy after every display action, so anything a form shows from the policy must be taken when the form opens, or it changes under the user. A functional test can bring that refresh without side effects by answering the site's display list and a deletion itself.
